events.name: 200 Hour Vinyasa Yoga Teacher Training
events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
AWHI Yoga and Wellbeing’s accredited 200hr YTT program is a comprehensive and thorough journey into becoming a 200 hr certified Yoga Teacher. We are the only vinyasa yoga teacher training in the world that blends Te Ao Māori and ancient yoga wisdoms, offering a uniquely 'Aotearoa' experience while retaining universal relevance for teaching and practicing yoga in any part of the world.

Our training is suitable for individuals interested in becoming a yoga teacher, or those looking to take a personal journey towards deepening your own practice and knowledge. Either way, we guarantee a transformative and life-changing experience that will deepen your relationship to yoga, others, Aotearoa and your self.

Our uniquely Aotearoa Teacher Training explores the beautiful marriage between ancient Yoga and Te Ao Māori teachings over five separate modules during our three months together. Our course follows the Māori hauora/wellbeing model of Te Whare Tapa Whā, which takes the same holistic view of health taken by traditional Yoga. As we work through each pillar we start tapping into something way greater than ourselves, enabling us to connect with our purpose in life and how we might share this in service to the world!

A $1,000 deposit reserves your spot.

events.name: From the Fisher's Mouth
events.venue: Graze Wine Bar, 95 Upland Road
events.long_description:
Tom and Cole of Strait Speared have been supplying Wellington's best venues with spear-caught butterfish for four years using methods that have minimal impact on the ocean. Knowing your fisherman matters, and tonight they're coming to the table to talk you through why. 

A nine-course degustation using all the parts of the butterfish: fillets, collars, roe. Each preparation different, each one revealing something new about the fish and the selectivity it takes to harvest responsibly. You'll chat with the fishermen about their work, with the chef about different butterfish preparations, and with the people beside you as course after course unfolds. This is what transparent seafood looks like when the person who caught it is sitting across from you. 

Your ticket includes nine courses and one welcome drink on arrival. Additional alcohol can be purchased.

events.long_description:
Overview

This practical Business Continuity Planning workshop helps small and medium-sized businesses prepare for disruption before it happens.

Could your business keep operating if something unexpected happened tomorrow?

Disruptions don’t wait until you’re ready. Severe weather, supplier delays, cyber incidents, key staff absence, power outages, cash flow pressure or system failures can all stop normal operations fast.

This practical workshop will help you understand what a Business Continuity Plan is, why it matters, and how to start building one that works for your business.

You’ll learn how to identify your most critical business activities, understand the risks that could interrupt them, and put simple steps in place to keep operating, recover faster and communicate clearly when things go wrong.

What you’ll walk away with

A clear understanding of what a Business Continuity Plan should include
A practical framework to assess, prepare, respond and review
Tools to identify your critical processes, dependencies and recovery priorities
Simple steps to strengthen your business resilience over 30, 60 and 90 days
Confidence to start your plan without waiting for it to be perfect

Who should attend

This workshop is designed for New Zealand small and medium-sized business owners, managers and decision-makers who want to be better prepared for disruption.

Why attend

Because a simple plan started today could make all the difference when disruption arrives tomorrow.

events.id: 2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON-AJ ParkWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: 2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON
events.venue: AJ ParkWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
"The Future of IP Dispute Resolution" by Sir Colin Birss, Chancellor of the High Court of England and Wales
5.30pm | Pre-event refreshments
6.00pm | Public lecture

The Future of IP Dispute Resolution
The legal landscape is changing before our eyes. The advent of AI and digital assets, the internationalisation of dispute resolution, and the changing expectations of users, all pose challenges, and intellectual property has always raised issues of its own.
This lecture will examine the state of intellectual property litigation today in the wider context, consider where it needs to be in future, and look at how we need to adapt to meet the challenges.
The topics include the major legal problems in IP which will need to be addressed; the legal and practical impact of artificial intelligence; the importance of digital assets and tokenisation; and the emergence of alternative modes of resolving dispute resolution.
Colin Birss is the Chancellor (Head of the Chancery Division) of the High Court of England and Wales. Called to the English Bar in 1990, he practised intellectual property law. In 2010 he became judge at the Patents County Court (now IPEC), in 2013 he went to the High Court, and in 2021 to the Court of Appeal. He was Deputy Head of Civil Justice 2021-25, and appointed Chancellor in 2025. He sits in the Court of Appeal and in the High Court.

If you are a University of Melbourne alumni, information about your participation may be shared with the Advancement team, as explained in our privacy notice.
Read less

events.name: Ngā Mokopuna Tour
events.venue: Te Herenga Waka Marae, 46 Kelburn Parade, Wellington
events.long_description:
Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

The tour also provides an opportunity to view Te Tumu Herenga Waka Marae and hear how the marae and Ngā Mokopuna together express values of sustainability, kaitiakitanga, belonging, and connection.

Whether you're interested in sustainable design, Māori worldviews, education, architecture, or the future of the built environment, this tour offers a unique insight into a project that seeks to demonstrate what regenerative design can achieve.

Come and discover how sustainability and kaitiakitanga are being brought to life at Ngā Mokopuna.

events.long_description:
Join us for the launch of Otto Wine Club – a new monthly wine tasting series celebrating some of New Zealand's best wineries.

Each month we'll welcome a different winery to Otto, where you'll have the chance to meet the winemaker, hear the stories behind the wines, and taste a curated selection from their range.

Our first event features Schubert Wines, one of Martinborough's most respected boutique wineries. Drop in anytime between 5:00pm and 7:00pm to enjoy your guided tasting.
Your ticket includes:
- A tasting flight of five Schubert wines
- The opportunity to meet the winemaker and learn about the vineyard and winemaking process
- A relaxed after-work atmosphere with plenty of time to ask questions and discover your new favourite drop

Whether you're a seasoned wine enthusiast or simply keen to explore something new, this is a fun, informal way to discover great New Zealand wine.

Spaces are limited, so book early to avoid missing out.

About Schubert Wines: https://www.schubert.co.nz/wines/
After graduating from the German Viticulture and Oenology University Geisenheim Kai Schubert and Marion Deimling travelled the world in search of the perfect terroir and conditions for viticulture, especially their favourite variety – Pinot Noir. Their quest took them to the wine regions of France, Germany, Oregon, California, South America and Australia and ended in Martinborough in the beautiful Wairarapa Valley.

Here they found the perfect climate and conditions for producing low yields and excellent quality grapes. Since 1998 Schubert Wines have been growing and producing wines with intense and complex character that are now nationally and internationally award winning.

events.name: Book Group: The Grass is Singing by Doris Lessing
events.venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
We return to Africa for our September book: Doris Lessing's first novel The Grass is Singing, which takes place in Southern Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) in the 1940s. The novel opens with a newspaper clipping about the death of Mary Turner, a white woman, killed by her black servant, Moses. The bulk of the novel is the story of Mary's life and the divided society she lived in.

Lessing was born in Persia, to British parents, and moved to Southern Rhodesia when she was six. Many of her books are set in Africa. In 1949 she left the continent and arrived in London with her son Peter (leaving behind her two older children) and the manuscript for this novel under her arm. The Grass is Singing was published the following year. Lessing was awarded the Nobel Prize in literature in 2007.

This is a shorter book, fitting neatly between The Last of the Mohicans and W. Somerset Maugham's Of Human Bondage, which are both longer works. (Of Human Bondage was originally published in two volumes.) But The Grass is Singing packs a punch. Indeed, one Goodreads review begins: "Doris Lessing's first novel has the precision of a fine short story and the depth of a longer novel."

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

events.venue: Project 100Nelson, Nelson Region
events.long_description:
Overview






A workshop that will take you through the A to Z of writing a character driven romance novel from bestselling author George Penney.
Do you have dreams of typing “The End” on a romance novel you’ve written but don’t know where to start?
Have you always dreamed of being a writer but find the actual process of becoming one intimidating?
Or maybe you’re a forever-writer just looking for pointers for how to shape your ideas into a structure that’ll sell to readers.
This three hour workshop will take you from initial character creation, through romance story structure and then to practical tips on getting your romance novel finished.
You’ll be taken through different romance genres, how to come up with three-dimensional, interesting characters, how to built tension and conflict, tips on writing good sex scenes and how to write that truly satisfying Happy Ever After ending.
This is a practical workshop designed to leave attendees motivated, excited and equipped with the tools to go on and finish that book!

*Please note: This is an AI free writing workshop. We believe that writing should be a messy, wonderful, exasperating, rewarding process that explores the depth of human creativity rather than a test on how well someone can type a prompt into a LLM. If you'd like to argue this point, please send us a non-AI hardbound treatise of no less than one hundred thousand words, hand-written in iambic pentameter.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

events.long_description:
Behind the Scenes: Napier Port & Mainfreight Learning Adventure
Have you ever driven past Napier Port or watched trucks moving through Hawke's Bay and wondered what really happens behind the scenes?

Every day, thousands of tonnes of cargo, products and supplies move through systems most of us rarely get to see.

Yet these operations quietly keep our region connected to New Zealand and the rest of the world.

This is a rare opportunity to step behind the gates and discover two of Hawke's Bay's most fascinating and important operations.

Join us for a special Learning Adventure that takes you inside Napier Port and Mainfreight Hastings, guided by people who know these organisations better than almost anyone.

Our day begins with an exclusive guided tour of Napier Port, one of New Zealand's busiest maritime hubs. You'll hear stories of the port's history, watch the operation in action, and gain a new appreciation for the scale and complexity of what happens there every day.

After the port tour, we'll gather for a relaxed waterfront lunch at Madame Social in Ahuriri — a chance to enjoy great food, good conversation and wonderful company.

In the afternoon, we'll head to Mainfreight's Hastings depot for a behind-the-scenes look at one of the country's most innovative logistics operations. From live freight tracking and electric forklifts to sustainable building design and workplace culture, you'll discover what makes this Hawke's Bay business such a success.

Along the way, you'll meet interesting people, hear remarkable stories and see parts of the region that most people never get access to.

Meet Our Guides 🎤

Tony des Landes spent more than 50 years working at Napier Port and is one of Hawke's Bay's leading maritime historians. His knowledge of the port, its history and its role in shaping the region is unmatched.

John Mackay is Hastings Branch Manager at Mainfreight and brings deep insight into the day-to-day operations, innovation and culture that have helped make Mainfreight one of New Zealand's most respected companies.

What We'll Explore
• A rare behind-the-scenes tour of Napier Port
• The history and evolution of Hawke's Bay's maritime industry
• How goods move through New Zealand's supply chains
• Innovation, sustainability and culture at Mainfreight
• The people, stories and systems that keep our region connected

Wellington Chamber of Commerce and Pax8 are proud to host the Prime Minister, Christopher Luxon.
Join Business Central and the Wellington Chamber of Commerce for an exclusive breakfast event featuring Prime Minister Rt Hon Christopher Luxon in conversation with Hayley Horan, Chief Executive of Business Central.
Set within the iconic Banquet Hall at Parliament, this special event offers members and the wider business community a rare opportunity to hear directly from New Zealand's leader in a professionally moderated fireside chat.
Unlike a traditional keynote speech, this event has been designed as a genuine conversation. The discussion will be informed by the experiences, perspectives, and questions submitted by Business Central and Wellington Chamber members, helping to ensure the topics explored reflect the realities, opportunities, and challenges facing our business community today.
Designed to be engaging, insightful, and business-focused, the discussion will explore the opportunities and challenges shaping New Zealand's future. From economic growth, productivity, trade, infrastructure, workforce development and artificial intelligence, through to geopolitics and New Zealand's long-term competitiveness, the conversation will focus on the issues that matter most to businesses across our region.
Following the fireside chat, attendees will have the opportunity to participate in a live audience Q&A, providing further engagement with the Prime Minister and valuable insight into the Government's priorities and vision for New Zealand.

Shared breakfast at a round table with fellow business leaders
Exclusive access to a one-hour conversation with the Prime Minister
Opportunity to submit questions that may shape the discussion
Live audience Q&A
Networking with business, government, and community leaders before and after the event

events.long_description:
Overview












The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.




Welcome to the biannual New Zealand Physical Oceanography Workshop (POW).
As climate change fundamentally reshapes our marine environments, understanding the fluid dynamics, heat distribution, and structural dynamics of our oceans has never been more critical. This year, our community gathers under a vital, unifying theme: The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.

We invite abstracts and presentations exploring the fundamental physical processes driving—and reacting to—global environmental change:
Coastal Oceanography of New Zealand
High-Latitude and Polar Dynamics
Next-Generation Ocean Modelling & Data Integration
Cross-Disciplinary Climate Solutions
How to do oceanography in the age of gestures broadly

Call for Abstracts & Registration Details
Oral Presentations: Standard 15-minute slots (including Q&A).
Lightning Talks: Project snapshots—ideal for introducing preliminary findings, novel scripts, or new field deployments.
How to Submit: Please email your presentation title, authors' list, a brief abstract (max 250 words), and your presentation preference directly to the organising committee at oceanography.newzealand@gmail.com.
Abstract Submission Deadline: 20 August 2026
Registration Deadline: 20 August 2026
Hybrid Registration Deadline: 1 September 2026
Registration is $100 for general attendees and free for students. We also have a free hybrid attendance option with the ability to present. Early-career researchers are highly encouraged to present.

We are planning a fun dinner on Wednesday, and we aim to finish early on Thursday.
We're looking forward to seeing you in September!

events.id: Sunset Guided Tour-Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Sunset Guided Tour
events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

In a competitive healthcare market, top talent is rarely active on public job boards. We provide access to a pre-vetted pool of professionals in a format designed for speed and impact.

Full Candidate Roster: Names and background details provided in advance.

events.name: Hiatus Kaiyote tickets
events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: Live Nation
Genre-bending future soul visionaries Hiatus Kaiyote return to celebrate their 15th anniversary with an electrifying night of funk, jazz, hip-hop, rock and progressive R&B as only they know how.
Led by singer-guitarist Naomi “Nai Palm” Saalfield, the Melbourne funkateers –featuring bassist Paul Bender, keyboardist Simon Mavin and drummer Perrin Moss –exploded internationally with their 2012 debut Tawk Tomahawk, which drew praise from the likes of Prince, Erykah Badu and Questlove. They landed their first of three Grammy nominations for their Q-Tip collaboration Nakamarra, received their second for their polyrhythmic record Choose Your Weapon (2015), and had their music sampled by no less than Kendrick Lamar, Beyoncé and Drake (with whom Nai Palm also collaborated on 2018’s monster hit Scorpion).
The band’s kaleidoscopic 2021 album Mood Valiant sent them into the national top five and earned them another Grammy nod, while their latest, 2024’s Love Heart Cheat Code, landed them an ARIA nomination for Best Group. Wizards of the shapeshifting live show, Hiatus Kaiyote have built a formidable reputation for their spectacular stage performances – a high-wire mix of musical mastery and thrilling, edge-of-your-seat chaos.

events.name: Bánh Mì Workshop: Open to all VUW Staff & Students
events.venue: Ramsey House, 8 Kelburn Pde, Kelburn, Wellington 6012
events.long_description:
Bánh Mì Workshop: Open to all VUW Staff & Students
To commemorate the 81st National Day of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, we invite VUW staff and students to a hands-on Vietnamese Bánh Mì workshop. Come together to celebrate culture, community, and cuisine through one of Vietnam's most beloved street foods.

WHAT THIS WORKSHOP COVERS

- The history and cultural significance of bánh mì
- Learn how to make Vietnamese chicken liver and VEGAN paté, egg yolk and VEGAN mayonnaise, pickled carrot and daikon
- Prepare and assemble your own bánh mì

WHAT YOU WILL GET

- Hands-on guidance in making an authentic Vietnamese bánh mì
- A freshly made bánh mì to enjoy during the workshop
- A take-home recipe card with ingredients and step-by-step instructions
- Opportunities to connect with fellow VUW staff and students in a fun, inclusive environment

FACILITATOR

This workshop is facilitated by Yung Nguyen from I Love Vietfood, in partnership with Viet Hub NZ.

SUPPORTING COMMUNITY THROUGH FOOD

Your koha helps support our VUW Chaplaincy venue host and Viet Hub NZ's community initiatives, including free community meals, cultural activities, and educational programmes.

Join us and celebrate the sweetness of tradition, creativity, and community

events.id: Requirements Elicitation-Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBDWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: Requirements Elicitation
events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBDWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview



Gain a core understanding of requirements elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques.
Description
This one-day course provides a core understanding of elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques. Emphasis is also placed on the need to verify requirements with the business to confirm that an accurate understanding has been elicited. During the afternoon session course participants undertake a realistic elicitation exercise, to reinforce the principles and techniques learnt during the course.
Greater emphasis is being placed on skilled business analysts who have the ability to communicate strongly, engage with stakeholders, and elicit a clear understanding of business requirements. Requirements elicitation skills have never been more important for business analysts and IT professionals.

The Requirements Elicitation course is delivered by seasoned Equinox consultant practitioners who apply the techniques and practices presented in this course on a daily basis.

Outline
Introduction to Requirements Elicitation
Goals of elicitation
Elicitation in the analysis process
Requirements elicitation methodology
Plan
The need for planning
Common elicitation problems
Requirements elicitation techniques
Requirements election patterns
Selection criteria
The requirements elicitation plan
Do
Preparing for the elicitation session
Performing elicitation
Managing the elicitation session
Presenting the elicitation results
Check
Communicate the requirements set
Check elicitation results
Check elicitation process
Act – corrective action
Requirements elicitation exercise

Learning outcomes
Following the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Identify where requirements elicitation fits within the broader requirements process
Understand and adopt an elicitation methodology
Select appropriate elicitation techniques for the situation
Plan and manage a requirements elicitation session
Understand the need for verification of elicitation results

Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts and systems analysts of all levels of experience. The course will also be of value to any project team members who are involved in elicitation or requirements activities.

Prerequisites
It is recommended that participants have some experience with requirements in project environment before attending.

events.name: Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?
events.venue: Russell McVeaghWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
A global perspective on investment, reliability, and the risks of getting it wrong.
Three recent shocks to electricity markets - cheap renewables, declining storage costs, and the return of demand growth - have led some to conclude that electricity markets as we know them have run their course. Drawing on thirty years of restructured markets abroad, this presentation will argue that these developments actually strengthen the case for markets — and will explore what reliability means, and how it should be provided, in a greener electricity system.
Professor James Bushnell – Biography
Professor James Bushnell is a distinguished scholar whose research and policy contributions have helped shape modern understanding of electricity markets, energy regulation, and climate policy, making him one of the most influential voices in energy economics. He is an internationally recognised expert in energy economics, electricity markets, environmental policy, and industrial organisation.The event is being facilitated by ERGANZ and will be hosted at the Wellington offices of Russell McVeagh
Date and Time: Thursday 3 September, 4pm - 6pm @Russell McVeagh, 157 Lambton Quay, please join us for a drink and nibbles from 4pm, presentation to start at 4:30pm with a Q&A to follow.
Please email admin@erganz.org.nz with any dietary requirements.
RSVP: Registrations can be secured by clicking on "Reserve a Spot".

events.id: State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry-HMLT002 Hugh Mackenzie BuildingWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry
events.venue: HMLT002 Hugh Mackenzie BuildingWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
Why are semiconductors central to global power? This keynote explores state-market tensions, supply chains, and geopolitical rivalry.
Using the global semiconductor industry as a case study, this lecture explores ‘decoupling’ amidst the complex web of state-market relations.
Most studies of decoupling focus on the United States and China. In contrast, I focus on the relationship between the United States and the full range of key semiconductor producers (Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and China). I ask when, and how, states intervene in semiconductor markets and propose that while the main actors in the semiconductor supply chain are not hegemonic powers, their high production capacities mean that their power is ‘pivotal’.
I argue that while technology production chains reflect the conflicting interests of states, because production chains also embody key shared interests, states cannot completely ‘decouple’ from one another. Meanwhile, key stakeholders are not always states, but also private companies and skilled workers. These actors have their own interests as well, meaning that production chains become further intertwined, rendering true decoupling impossible. Their resistance to decoupling means that this ‘stickiness’ will be a feature of any state-led attempt to forge supply chain independence.

events.id: ITI Evening Seminar Wellington with Prof. Frauke Muller-QT WellingtonWellington, Wellington-Event Brite
events.name: ITI Evening Seminar Wellington with Prof. Frauke Muller
events.venue: QT WellingtonWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Implant Overdentures for Old and Very Old Patients
In New Zealand there is an increasing number of older persons who retain their natural dentition until later in life. Accordingly edentulous patients will not only be older, they will also be also more challenging to treat. Implant-supported overdentures (IODs) may significantly improve the functional performance in most domains, particularly the bite force and chewing efficiency. They also significantly improve the patients’ OHRQoL. Their design should take into consideration the physiological signs of ageing, but also the morbidity and social context. The lecture presents step by step the manufacturing of age-adequate IODs with conventional and digital workflows. Digital techniques may also be employed to meet the requirements of very old patients with reduced neuroplasticity, as they allow to import successful features from an existing denture. IOD management may become a challenge at the onset of dependency when denture handling relies on the knowledge and skill of caring staff. At this stage, hygiene is even more crucial to prevent aspiration pneumonia. The “back-off” strategy aims at accompanying the functional decline. In summary, IODs significantly enhance oral function and denture satisfaction and therefore be considered a valuable mosaic in the dental treatment for older adults.

Learning objectives
1. Design an age-adequate removable prosthesis
2. Develop concepts for patients with reduced neuroplasticity
3. Know strategies to accompany future functional decline in very old and multimorbid patients

events.name: Men's Circle & Breathwork
events.venue: Bhakti Lounge WellingtonWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview
A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, breathwork and meaningful connection in a space of trust and support.
Men's Circle & Breathwork 
Starts at 6pm
In a world where men are often expected to have everything figured out, this gathering offers a space to be genuine, not perfect.
This is a free event, with an optional plant-based dinner available for $15. While there’s no obligation to stay for dinner, sharing a meal together offers a meaningful way to strengthen connections.
Andre and Sri Jiva co-host this circle with a shared passion for creating authentic, supportive spaces where men can connect deeply, offering this gathering simply because they believe in its importance.
The Men’s Circle provides a safe and nurturing environment where men can share openly, express their feelings and encourage personal growth. Through honest sharing and collective support, participants build resilience, deepen self-awareness, and strengthen their sense of identity and purpose.
 Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
Breathwork is a powerful practice to help ground the nervous system and connect to a deep presence. 
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
 Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.
Join us after this free event for an optional plant-based dinner and dessert for only $20 (or $10 for students).
Meet Andre, your host:
Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Meet Sri Jiva, your host:
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

events.long_description:
Overview

Refresh body and mind with a gentle spring breathwork journey to release winter heaviness and reconnect with your natural aliveness.

Somatic Breathwork: Spring Renewal




Event starts at 6pm

September is a threshold month, a natural invitation to spring clean.

Not just the space around you, but the space inside you too.

Spring Cleansing is a somatic breathwork session designed to help you gently shift some of the heaviness that can build up over the colder months. Think sluggishness, brain fog, tension, low energy, or simply that feeling of being a little stuck in your body.

Through a consent-led, trauma-aware breathwork journey, we’ll create space to:

move stagnant energy and emotions
warm and reconnect with the body
release some of the heaviness that winter can leave behind
return to your breath, presence, and natural sense of aliveness

A chance to pause, breathe, and make room for something new.

You’ll leave feeling lighter, clearer, and more connected to your body, like opening the windows and letting fresh air move through.

This session is for you if:
you’ve felt heavy, puffy, sluggish, or “damp” after winter
your chest/breath has felt tight, shallow, or restricted
you’ve been waking up tired, unmotivated, or mentally foggy
you’ve been indoors more, moving less, and can feel it in your body
you want a reset that’s embodied, not performative
you want a welcoming, choice-based space to explore breathwork
What to expect
Arrival (consent + information) chair, side-lying, and low-intensity options available
Nervous system primer: clearing and activation safely
Breath demonstration + choice of intensity tracks (including a gentle nasal-only option)
A guided somatic breathwork arc. clearing, warming, and releasing what’s been holding on
Optional movement to support circulation (micro-shakes, shaking, or gentle unwinding)
Integration rest + grounding
Closing reflection (brief journaling prompt or quiet pause)
Benefits you may notice

You might experience:

a lighter body and clearer head
more warmth and circulation through chest/shoulders/hips
improved mood and motivation
emotional release without overwhelm
deeper, easier breathing
a renewed sense of momentum that feels steady (not forced)
Please bring:
Yoga mat
Warm layers (we’ll warm up, but your body may cool during rest)
Water bottle
Small towel
Optional eye mask or light scarf
Journal and pen
If you run cold, bring a blanket
Pre-class prep
Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at hi@lynofuro.co.nz if there’s anything you’d like to share before the session.
Contraindications and safety

Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy; serious cardiovascular conditions; uncontrolled blood pressure; glaucoma or retinal detachment; epilepsy or seizure history; recent surgery or concussion; or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.

Aftercare

After the session, remember to:

events.long_description:
Four Islands, Infinite Interpretations.

New Music Islands explores how we can forge connections across vast geographies while also doing our own thing, here, in our own way. The evening will be presented in two halves. The first 45 minutes feature a New Music Islands programme showcasing selected works from the Faroe Islands, Aotearoa New Zealand, the Canary Islands and Gotland. The second half celebrates the richness and diversity of contemporary music in New Zealand with a selection of works by New Zealand composers.

The programme centres on four works that embrace openness through flexible instrumentation and deliberately broad performance instructions. Each ensemble is invited to make the music their own, resulting in unique interpretations as the programme travels between the four island communities.

Featuring performances by Tristan Carter, Jonny Marks, Erika Grant, Naoto Segawa and Rebecca Steel, with music by Jesse Austin-Stewart, Ruby Solly, Elliot Vaughan, Ciro Hernández, Lasse Thornin, Weston Olencki, Michelle Scullion, Jessie Leov, Garling Wu and Chris Cree Brown.

Each concert will be a singular experience, with this being the Aotearoa New Zealand presentation. - New Music Islands is an international collaboration between four member societies of the International Society for Contemporary Music (ISCM): the Faroe Islands Section, VICC (ISCM Gotland Section), COSIMITE (ISCM Affiliated Associate Member representing the Canary Islands) and CANZ (ISCM New Zealand Section).

New Music Islands is an international collaboration between four member societies of the International Society for Contemporary Music (ISCM): the Faroe Islands Section, VICC (ISCM Gotland Section), COSIMITE (ISCM Affiliated Associate Member representing the Canary Islands) and CANZ (ISCM New Zealand Section).

events.long_description:
New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever, COME TOGETHER, returns in 2026 with an electrifying trio of landmark albums: Bruce Springsteen’s Born to Run, Radiohead’s OK Computer and Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense.

Each album will be performed live, in full, by a rotating supergroup of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed rock artists and musicians — followed by a second set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s extraordinary catalogue.

From the wall of sound production of Born to Run, to the haunting dystopian brilliance of OK Computer, to the joyful and immersive perfection of Stop Making Sense, the 2026 series celebrates three albums that have cemented their place in music history. Performed in some of the country’s most beautiful venues, Come Together once again promises epic musicianship, emotional punch and the kind of once-in-a-lifetime collaborations that have made the series a cultural phenomenon.

Widely regarded as one of the greatest live albums and concert films of all time, Stop Making Sense captured Talking Heads at the absolute height of their powers. A bona fide classic, it remains a benchmark for concert performance and sonic brilliance.

Recreated in all its Talking Heads glory, every track from the concert film will be performed — from Psycho Killer to Burning Down the House, Once in a Lifetime, and everything in between. Expect big grooves, art-school cool… and yes, some mighty suits.

Performed by: James Milne, Anthonie Tonnon, Dianne Swann, Julia Deans and the Come Together band — with more to be announced.

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Ballroom dance has never been more thrilling. For over 20 years, Burn the Floor has been revolutionising the fast and furious steps of ballroom style. Groundbreaking moves and rebellious energy are brought to the stage every night to create an electrifying experience. For its latest show. Luminous, twenty-six dancers, musicians, and vocalists will take to the stage. You’ll get to witness romantic waltzes, a futuristic foxtrot, and the passion of the paso doble and tango. You’ll also marvel at the footwork of the cha cha, samba, jive, and a smokingly irresistible Rumba. With lights, costumes, and eclectic live music, you’ll want to leap out of your seat to join in.
Director Jason Gilkison sets an uncompromising standard and comments, “From the very beginning, we set out to shatter every expectation of what ballroom dance can be. Burn the Floor has always been about pushing boundaries — and that hunger to evolve is what has kept us alive and thriving.”
Burn the Floor has grown into a global phenomenon, selling more than four million tickets across theatres in over 30 countries. The show is also seen by more than one million people each year through its four permanently installed productions with Norwegian Cruise Line.

events.id: Chris Parker — Take a Good Hard Look at Me-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Chris Parker — Take a Good Hard Look at Me
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
When comedian Chris Parker was young, he liked attention. He’s always endeavoured to make people look at him. In his latest show, he continues the theme of a lifetime. Take a Good Hard Look at Me displays the Kiwi comic’s sharp wit and clever timing. Chris says of his hour-long show — “There’s no secrets about to be dished, no valuable lesson to take away. I’m just a 35-year-old gay man, who was told there was something special about him as a kid and has been grappling with that ever since.” 
Chris is an actor, comedian, writer, and podcaster. He gained fame on TV’s Have You Been Paying Attention and Thank God You’re Here. He has written and performed extensively with Tom Sainsbury on live shows such as The Opening Night Before Christmas, Camping, Giggly Gerties, and Hauraki Horror. He also created and performed several sketch comedy shows with fellow comedian Hayley Sproull, including Tighty Whiteys, The Outsiders’ Guide, and Milky Bits.

INSPIRE Festival is for all tamariki aged 8-13 (up to year 8) who are interested in STEAMS learning.
Public ticket sales open on 7 August. Early access is currently available by invitation only.

INSPIRE Festival is 4-5 Sept 2026!
$60 per child per day for a full day of STEAMS learning!
INSPIRE Festival 2026 offers two days of student selected challenging discussions and hands-on workshops all focused around STEAMS (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Maths, and Society). This year the festival is being hosted at Nayland College!
• Friday: 1- or 2-hour workshops
• Saturday: 2-4 hour, in-depth workshops. Perfect for students to get really stuck in to topics.
INSPIRE offers thought-provoking discussions and hands on experiments for AGES 8-13 (up to Year 8). Students choose up to 4 sessions to attend, all based on the STEAMS model of education and delivered by New Zealand's top professionals, scientists, businessmen, and mentored college students.
INSPIRE will develop the connection between classroom theory and some very exciting and ground-breaking real careers which make a difference in our world. The inaugural INSPIRE was in 2012 and massive demand has led to it being hosted annually with over 650 students attending and has continued to grow. The energy and enthusiasm of the students is wonderful and, with their feedback, demonstrates the necessity and benefits of INSPIRE. All attendees will be our future leaders and creative thinkers and they have told us they want more; more challenge, more connections and more opportunities to grow and learn.
It is recommended that students attending INSPIRE Festival have a teacher/adult 'in-charge' of them. Students left at the venue without an adult 'in-charge' are left at their own risk.

events.name: 2026 Taiwan Update Lectures
events.venue: Room AM106, Alan MacDiarmid Building,Kelburn Parade, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
2026 Taiwan Update Lectures
Join us for three talks by experts on different aspects of Taiwan

About this Event



Session One:

Taiwan Studies in Australia: policy engagement and moral purpose in the shadow of a China-Taiwan war

Mark Harrison

Australia's institutionalised understanding of Taiwan exists in the context of an increasingly belligerent PRC escalating its threats against the Taiwanese. Knowledge of Taiwan is therefore a concern of Australian policy-making, yet in national discourse it remains constrained by questions of defence capabilities and alliance politics. Preparedness requires deeper Taiwan knowledge, able to recognise a crisis, define its thresholds, and understand what is at stake and for whom. This gives Taiwan Studies a distinctive contemporary purpose as a form of critical national infrastructure.

The talk assesses these themes through a 2025 study of Australian public and institutional responses to Taiwan Strait crises, conducted with John Fitzgerald, Kuo Mei-fen, Nathan Attrill and Marc Ablong, which found Australian understanding of Taiwan to be fragmented, event-driven and reactive, with Taiwanese-Australian communities distinctively marginalised.

I then move beyond this instrumental purpose to pose a moral problem the field cannot defer. When the threat to Taiwanese society, to friends and colleagues, is material rather than notional, supplying knowledge and practising critique are not the only responsibility of Taiwan scholarship. I examine what it means for Taiwan Studies to take on a moral purpose, as the discipline through which Australia comes to know Taiwan and answers whether it is willing to defend its existence as uniquely Taiwanese.

Session Two

A Young Democracy Threatened from Without and Polarized from Within

Ching-hsin Yu

As one of the model cases of third wave democratization, Taiwan’s progress toward democratic consolidation has attracted broad attention. Nevertheless, the development of democracy in Taiwan has not been without difficulties. Both external and internal challenges continue to test this emerging democracy. Externally, the security threat posed by neighbouring China, together with the complexities of contemporary international geopolitics, has led Taiwan to be widely regarded as a global flashpoint for potential conflict. These circumstances have compelled Taiwan’s political leadership to seriously consider how to strengthen national security and enhance societal resilience in order to respond effectively to potential external shocks and crises. Internally, increasing political polarization has made it difficult to achieve broad consensus on many critical policy issues. Furthermore, the existence of a divided government has contributed to persistent gridlock between the executive and legislative branches. Thus, long-standing political cleavages, deeply entrenched socioeconomic challenges, and increasing national security concerns have become intertwined and highly politicized. The interaction among these issues poses significant challenges not only for the government but also for Taiwanese society as a whole. This presentation examines these contemporary challenges facing Taiwan’s democracy. Drawing upon relevant academic research and public opinion survey data, it explores the political consequences of these developments and analyzes citizens’ attitudes toward the key issues confronting Taiwan today.




Session Three

Taiwan’s Tumultuous Past and the Conflicted National Self

Rosemary Haddon

The Taiwan issue is a multi-faceted Gordian knot compounded by contested ethnic and political interests, the Cross-Strait relations with China, and unresolved legacies bequeathed from the historical past. Solutions to the issue seem more elusive than ever. All the while, domestic arguments rage and tensions soar. This talk shifts the focus away from contemporary politics to the tumultuous past and the legacy termed the “conflicted national self”. Its theme is Taiwan’s identity formation during the Nationalist (Kuomintang) era and post-Martial Law Taiwan. Stories and novels from xiangtu wenxue (native soil literature) and bentu or pro-Taiwan literature illustrate the way the identity evolved. Further concepts include hegemony, becoming (Japanese, Chinese, Taiwanese), Orientalism, 228 (Ererba) and the White Terror (Baikong), and unification versus independence. The speaker draws on her experience living in Taiwan during the Nationalist era and her recent publication Taiwan’s Modern Identity Reimagined: Becoming Taiwanese (Routledge, 2026).

Join us for a special screening of the 1983 film by Directors | Hou Hsiao-hsien 侯孝賢 Wan Jen萬仁 Tseng Chuang-hsiang 曾壯祥
Adapted from three of Huang Chun-ming's short stories, this episodic film portrays the struggles of marginalised individuals during challenging times. events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

events.name: NZSO Rhythm & Dance
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, 111 Wakefield Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
John Adams The Chairman Dances
Copland Clarinet Concerto
Gabriela Ortiz Antrópolis (NZ Premiere)
Bernstein Symphonic Dances from West Side Story

Gemma New’s signature “strength, clarity and grace” (WTTW News) invigorates this 20th century American classic, Bernstein’s Symphonic Dances from West Side Story. In depicting a New York gangland Romeo and Juliet, Bernstein’s score captures an irrepressible American swagger. Rhythm & Dance also infuses John Adams’ The Chairman Dances, an outtake of Adams’ opera Nixon in China, which imagines the young Chairman Mao dancing the foxtrot with his mistress.

Aaron Copland’s Clarinet Concerto melds Latin American popular music with jazz in this work commissioned by “The King of Swing” Benny Goodman. And we proudly present the Kiwi premiere of Gabriela Ortiz’s Antrópolis. Grammy Award-winning Ortiz is one of Mexico’s hottest contemporary composers, and this work refers to el antro, Mexican slang for a nightclub.

events.name: Yoga Nidra
events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

events.id: A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production-Adam Concert Room, NZSM Kelburn Campus, Victoria University, Gate 7, Kelburn Parade, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production
events.venue: Adam Concert Room, NZSM Kelburn Campus, Victoria University, Gate 7, Kelburn Parade, Wellington
events.long_description:
Classical Performance students from the New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī present four performances of Jacques Offenbach's delightful comic opera A Voyage to the Moon, directed by Sara Brodie with musical direction by Kathryn Mosley.

Inspired by this year's space exploration milestones, including NASA's Artemis II mission, this production celebrates Offenbach's imaginative 1875 opera, which was a sensation in Paris, running for an impressive 185 consecutive performances during its first run.

Loosely based on Jules Verne's novel From the Earth to the Moon, A Voyage to the Moon takes audiences on a adventure filled with fantastical lunar landscapes, eccentric characters, and Offenbach's trademark comedic twists. The story follows King V'lan, his adventurous son Prince Caprice, and their companions—including Microscope and Rhombus—as they journey to the Moon, where they encounter Cosmos, Princess Fantasia, Flamma, and other curious inhabitants of the lunar world.

Directed by Sara Brodie, who also led last year's fantastic production of L'enfant et les sortilèges, the opera features vocal numbers performed in French with English surtitles. The spoken dialogue is presented in English, bringing the comedy vividly to life for contemporary audiences.

This production showcases the talents of students across the Classical Performance programme, with NZSM voice students performing all roles and in ensembles, and the NZSM piano students taking part as rehearsal pianists (répétiteurs) and playing for the performances. Musical direction is provided by Head of Collaborative Piano Kathryn Mosley, and the production is coordinated by Head of Classical Voice Jenny Wollerman.

Join us for an imaginative, entertaining, and truly 'out there' operatic adventure!

events.name: Katelyn Henshall EP Release With Jeline And Ari Leason
events.venue: Vogelmorn Upstairs, Wellington
events.long_description:
Katelyn Henshall fuses pop, R&B, and soul into something uniquely her own. Fronting the genre of what she claims to be whiskey lounge soul, Katelyn and her band are excited to share live performances from their debut EP, A lil somethin' somethin'. Kicking off 2026 with a bang, Katelyn has released two singles, Take Me Away and Nothing lasts forever (de verano), in anticipation of the full EP. A lil somethin’ somethin’” is a tasting tray of a few of the genres Katelyn is passionate about, showcasing the strengths and skills of every member of the band. Katelyn's band consists of Dónal Gunning (bass), Tane James (guitar), and Oliver Dudziak (drums).

Ōtaki-born singer-songwriter Ari Leason will open the show. Her soulful blend of indie folk and intimate storytelling shines through her debut album Hello Darling. Honest, vulnerable, and deeply authentic, Ari brings songs shaped by activism, travel, and a coming-of-age journey that resonates long after the last note.

Also supporting Katelyn is jeline, your ‘filipina-next door’ - an indie-pop-rock artist who's writing songs about feelings she can't contain to herself and belting her heart out to whoever's listening! jeline has surrounded herself in different genres and music tastes but after trying to find her feet as an artist, some honest talks with the industry and scrapping a whole ass album, she finally locked in to her recognisable indie-pop-rock sound. From songs about first love to obsessing over exes, jeline's relatability and vulnerability is always packaged in a song you can bop along to.

Doors open
7:30pm

Gig starts
8pm

All Ages
Cover charge*
Unwaged $15
Waged $20
Support the Artists $30
*Guide only - booking fees apply

Venue accessibility information:

Vogelmorn Upstairs is not a wheelchair accessible building. There is an accessible
bathroom in the space. This is an all ages venue but those under the age of 16 must be
accompanied by a designated adult after 8pm. The Vogelmorn Precinct is a community
space located in a residential area. With that in mind, the team ask that you be kind to
others' and that when you leave the gig, you do so quietly to avoid disturbing our
neighbours.

Come early before the show and enjoy a meal at Vogelmorn's restaurant, VBC Eats, from 4:00pm to 9:00pm. VBC Eats is a relaxed community-focused restaurant delivering tasty specials, from curries to salads to pizzas to bite-sized bar snacks. By locals for locals!

Expect soaring harmonies, a dynamic live show, and feel-good vibes when Mel Parsons performs live in Wellington this September. With a style that ranges from indie folk to alt-country, the Kiwi artist has established a reputation for moving songwriting. 
The tour repertoire is based around songs from her latest album, Castle Hill. Named after the remote mountain town in the Southern Alps where it was recorded, Castle Hill was recorded live with Mel’s longtime band members, Aaron Stewart on bass and Jed Parsons on drums. It also includes Ben King (guitarist from Goldenhorse and Grand Rapids). They will support her on stage too. Singles from the record that you’ll hear include alt radio chart toppers, Post High Slide, Brick By Brick, Be Here Now, and Grain by Grain. 
Since her first album in 2009, Mel has established herself in New Zealand’s musical landscape. Awards include Best Folk Artist (2020 New Zealand Music Awards) and Best Country Music Song (2016 New Zealand Music Awards).

events.name: Rhythm & Dance - Wellington
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre,111 Wakefield St, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Rhythm & Dance - Wellington
Stamp the beat and feel the heat in this concert of pan-American dance, jazz and pizzazz!

Programme
John Adams The Chairman Dances
Copland Clarinet Concerto
Gabriela Ortiz Antrópolis (NZ Premiere)
Bernstein Symphonic Dances from West Side Story

Gemma New’s signature “strength, clarity and grace” (WTTW News) invigorates this 20th century American classic, Bernstein’s Symphonic Dances from West Side Story. In depicting a New York gangland Romeo and Juliet, Bernstein’s score captures an irrepressible American swagger. Rhythm & Dance also infuses John Adams’ The Chairman Dances, an outtake of Adams’ opera Nixon in China, which imagines the young Chairman Mao dancing the foxtrot with his mistress.

Aaron Copland’s Clarinet Concerto melds Latin American popular music with jazz in this work commissioned by “The King of Swing” Benny Goodman. And we proudly present the Kiwi premiere of Gabriela Ortiz’s Antrópolis. Grammy Award-winning Ortiz is one of Mexico’s hottest contemporary composers, and this work refers to el antro, Mexican slang for a nightclub.

In association with New Zealand Herald.

events.long_description:
YOGA NIDRA
Unwind from the stresses of the week by finding a deep state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, or "yogic sleep," is a restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga Nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

WHAT TO EXPECT:
+ A 75-minute guided Yoga Nidra Meditation led by one of our experienced instructors
+ A comfortable space to lie down (mats, blankets, bolsters & cushions provided)
+ A supportive community of fellow meditation enthusiasts
+ Complementary herbal tea before/after the session;
+ An opportunity to journal your experience, if desired
+ A chance to destress and cultivate inner calm

Wear comfortable clothes, and bring an open mind, a journal and eye mask if you have one (not required).

INVESTMENT: FREE for AWHI members (on a 3/6/12 month contract) or $25 drop-in for passholders & visitors ($20 Concession pricing available for students, seniors & WINZ).

Want to become an AWHI member to receive this and other benefits? Email us today to sign up!

WHO IS THIS FOR:
Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

BOOKING:
Follow the link to register or simply turn up on the night! Drop-ins welcome.

Let's come together and discover the transformative power of Yoga Nidra Meditation. See you there! 🌟

events.long_description:
A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production
Classical Performance students from the New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī present four performances of Jacques Offenbach's delightful comic opera A Voyage to the Moon, directed by Sara Brodie with musical direction by Kathryn Mosley.

Performance dates:
Friday 4 September, 7:30pm
Saturday 5 September, 3:00pm & 7:30pm
Sunday 6 September, 3:00pm

Duration: 70 minutes
Venue: The Adam Concert Room
Tickets: On sale now via Eventfinda with student and concession discounts available!

Inspired by this year's space exploration milestones, including NASA's Artemis II mission, this production celebrates Offenbach's imaginative 1875 opera, which was a sensation in Paris, running for an impressive 185 consecutive performances during its first run.

Loosely based on Jules Verne's novel From the Earth to the Moon, A Voyage to the Moon takes audiences on a adventure filled with fantastical lunar landscapes, eccentric characters, and Offenbach's trademark comedic twists. The story follows King V'lan, his adventurous son Prince Caprice, and their companions—including Microscope and Rhombus—as they journey to the Moon, where they encounter Cosmos, Princess Fantasia, Flamma, and other curious inhabitants of the lunar world.

Directed by Sara Brodie, who also led last year's fantastic production of L'enfant et les sortilèges, the opera features vocal numbers performed in French with English surtitles. The spoken dialogue is presented in English, bringing the comedy vividly to life for contemporary audiences.

This production showcases the talents of students across the Classical Performance programme, with NZSM voice students performing all roles and in ensembles, and the NZSM piano students taking part as rehearsal pianists (répétiteurs) and playing for the performances. Musical direction is provided by Head of Collaborative Piano Kathryn Mosley, and the production is coordinated by Head of Classical Voice Jenny Wollerman.

Join us for an imaginative, entertaining, and truly 'out there' operatic adventure!

events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Whether you’re already retired, or planning ahead, this practical workshop will help you to reflect, re-envision and re-vitalise your life and develop a plan for your future, on your own terms. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, all others pay $109).

In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.

It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future, but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or child-rearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.

After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.

By the end of the day, you’ll have:
- Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
- Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your strengths
- Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
- Developed a blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and developed a “future-proofing” downsizing plan
- Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explored and implemented choices that provide you with that sense of purpose
Bring a pen and paper.

1 day, Sat 9:30 AM – 4:00 PM
Wellington High School
Presented by Angela Robertson

events.long_description:
Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Sometimes, our minds get stuck in habitual thought loops—endlessly cycling through the same worries, fears, and anxieties without ever finding a breakthrough. When words fall short, art therapy offers a different language. By shifting from thinking to creating, we bypass the noise of everyday stress and tap into an intuitive visual language that can surprise us with fresh insights, new perspectives, and profound meaning.
This workshop is a gentle, immersive introduction to a pathway of self-restoration, self-compassion, and self-worth—the vital foundations for true self-healing.
What you will experience:
A Shift in Perspective: Break free from repetitive thinking by engaging the creative, intuitive side of your brain.
Tools for Daily Coping: Learn how the simple act of making art can become a sanctuary for processing stress and finding grounding.
A Pathway to Wholeness: Explore how visual expression can reveal hidden strengths and foster a deeper sense of self-care.
Important Note: You do absolutely not need to be an artist or have any artistic experience to attend. This day is about the process of expression, not the final product. While this workshop is not a substitute for clinical individual or group therapy, it is a powerful, supportive introduction to the healing power of the arts.
What to Bring:
A journal and a pen or pencil. All other creative materials will be provided.  Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks and  photo ID.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Bike Maintenance for Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Bicycle Maintenance for Beginners
Have you recently started riding a bicycle and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?
Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?
This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.
Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!
Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.
Bring your pushbike along on the day.  If you have the following, please bring them as well:  A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.
Note: A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
- Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
- Fix a flat tyre
- Adjust your bike to fit your body
- Oil and clean your chain
- Identify and fix some common brake problems
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Description
The lentil is perhaps the world’s most versatile and indestructible food. It has significant health benefits from lowering cholesterol to supporting weight loss – and lentils are delicious when cooked well. Enjoy this half-day course that will show you how to cook lentils properly and make the most of this nutritious staple ingredient. Discover spices to complement and enhance lentils and create some mouth-watering dishes.

All ingredients included in course fee. Please bring your apron, a couple of teatowels, a sharp knife and leak-proof containers to take your food home in.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Recognise some different types of lentils.
Cook some delicious lentil dishes.
Understand some spices that will work well with lentils.
Follow simple recipes.

events.long_description:
Retirement Reinvented
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.
It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future – but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or childrearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.
After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
By the end of the day, you’ll have:
Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your values and your strengths
Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explore choices that can provide you with that sense of purpose
Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
Begun to develop your blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and have considered a “future proofing” downsizing plan.
Bring pen and paper.

In this workshop you will be guided in making a classic cut and fold 8-page zine from a standard A4 sheet of paper - this is a clever design you can easily photocopy and reproduce later! Cut and fold a classic 8-page zine format from a single sheet of paper
