events.id: Coptic Book Binding Workshop-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Coptic Book Binding Workshop
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Coptic binding is one of the earliest forms of creating a book, with raw simplicity you can produce a book of any size with the unique feature of opening out flat. No special tools or materials are needed and yet a wide spectrum of creative results can be created, from a notebook, sketch book and album to a highly crafted artwork. The books themselves can be made from found items, recycled material or quality art papers and card.

In this workshop you will be guided in assembling your chosen materials for your book, create decorative covers and learn Coptic binding - an elegant and simple binding that is unlimited in versatility. You will produce one bound book and one bound album. Once you have Coptic binding in your skill set you can produce your choice of books in any shape or form, for any purpose.

All basic materials supplied.

Half an hour for lunch. Bring a drink bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy House or explore the cafes in Te Aro. Coffee & tea provided at lunch.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course or attend with a paying adult.

events.name: Finding Tiny Moments of Joy in Everyday Life
events.venue: Project 100Nelson, Nelson Region
events.long_description:
Overview





Do you need more joy and calmness in your life? Then this workshop about how to find small joys in the world might be for you!
In an increasingly frenetic world with social media and news cycles encouraging us to see things as increasingly doom and gloom, this workshop will help you recalibrate by using micro journaling to rediscover the small joys in your everyday life.
Because while we can’t change the big things, sometimes a small shift to a more positive outlook can help us go about our day-to-day lives less stressed and more resilient.
With fun, practical steps George Penney, author of the US, UK and Australian bestselling book of people watching vignettes, Tiny Moments of Joy: Spotted on Market Day in Aotearoa New Zealand, will guide you through looking at the world around you with fresh eyes, finding moments of peace, calm and even happiness.


For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

Learn how to design a repeating pattern with artist and textile designer Greta Menzies. Greta Menzies is a multidiciplinary artist & designer with a background in textile design (MDes) living in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, Aotearoa NZ. events.long_description:
Eyegum Music Collective presents GREAT SOUNDS GREAT, a multi-venue music and arts festival taking over Pōneke's Te Aro precinct for one night only on Saturday 5 September 2026. Showcasing 40 of Aotearoa's best artists across 10 neighbouring venues, this is one big party you shouldn't miss.

Eyegum has worked hard to curate a programme that is sure to offer something for everyone, from first time gig-goers to seasoned live music obsessives. The eclectic lineup includes national treasures like Bic Runga and Savage, heavy-hitting legends Beastwars, Kody Nielson’s enigmatic project Silicon, indie math rockers So So Modern, powerhouse party starter Mokotron, local hip hop sensation MĀ, and everything in between.

Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.

It's not all music, three of our best poets Chris Tse, Dani Yourukova, and Jackson McCarthy will also perform.

Excitingly for 2026, we are adding a new venue, the incomparable Meow Nui, helping make this year's event bigger and better than ever. We are also throwing a warm-up party, The Night Before, across three venues in Newtown village on Friday 4 September. This will showcase 12 incredible up-and-coming artists and is the perfect way to prepare for the main event.

Ticket holders will receive a wristband that will give them access to each of the participating venues throughout the event. Information on how to pick up wristbands will be provided to ticket holders closer to the time.

Limited tickets on sale now from eyegum.co.nz/great-sounds-great

Presented with support from Abandoned Brewery, RadioActive.FM, and Wellington City Council.

Venues: Meow Nui, San Fran, Meow, Valhalla, Rogue & Vagabond, Bedlam & Squalor, Hotel Bristol, St Peter's on Willis, Flying Nun Records, Tonic Travelling Stage.

Lineup: Amamelia, Beastwars, Bic Runga, Bri Louise, Chris Tse, Crook, Cruelly, Dani Yourukova, Deathro (JPN), Dream Chambers, Fazed on a Pony, Groove Council, Hemi Hemingway, Hihi & The Stitchbirds, Hunter Jackson, In Good Company, Jackson McCarthy, JELL, Ludus b2b Rizzo, MĀ, Mauri Aura, mHz, Mokotron, More Blue Noise, Naakz & Babyzoot, Office Dog, Pearly*, Pitch Black, Savage (DJ Set), Savagehine, Sheeps, Silicon, So So Modern, Soft Bait, Tamatha Paul, The Sour, The Spectre Collective: Live-Scored Cinema, Tūi Band, Unsanitary Napkin.

Macaron Masterclass

Learn to create one of France's most iconic pastries from scratch. In this hands-on class, you'll master the techniques behind smooth shells, beautiful feet, and perfectly balanced fillings. We'll guide you through the macaron process step by step, including meringue preparation, macaronage, piping, baking, and troubleshooting common issues so you can recreate them confidently at home.

French meringue technique
Proper macaronage
Piping and resting
Baking for perfect shells
Ganache and buttercream fillings (recipe provided)

You'll take home: A box of handmade macarons, a recipe booklet, and the confidence to bake them again.

Duration: Approximately 3 hours

events.long_description:
The Spring Fling Express
🌼🚂 The Spring Fling Express – A Heritage Rail Journey to Central Hawke’s Bay’s Biggest Spring Celebration! 🚂🌼

Saturday 5th September 2026

Celebrate the arrival of spring aboard Steam Incorporated’s Spring Fling Express, a special return rail journey from the Kāpiti Coast and Manawatū to Waipukurau for the opening weekend of Central Hawke’s Bay’s much-loved Spring Fling festivities. Travel behind heritage diesel locomotive Da 1410 through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge and some of the North Island’s most picturesque countryside aboard our beautifully restored heritage train.

Once in Waipukurau, choose how you'd like to spend your day:

🌼 Taniwha Daffodils Experience
Enjoy coach transfers to the famous Taniwha Daffodils, where thousands of blooms create a spectacular spring display. Wander the gardens, soak up the atmosphere, enjoy a packed lunch, and even pick your own daffodils to take home.

☕ Explore Waipukurau at Your Own Pace
Spend the day discovering local cafés, shops, gardens and attractions before re-joining the train for the journey home. Perfect for those wanting a relaxed day out in the heart of Central Hawke’s Bay.

🚉 Boarding from:
Paekākāriki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Ōtaki, Levin and Palmerston North.

🎟 Fares from just $119 Adult / $99 Child
🌼 Taniwha Daffodils packages available!

Whether you're chasing spring colour, exploring a charming country town, or simply enjoying a day aboard one of New Zealand’s most unique heritage rail experiences, the Spring Fling Express promises a memorable day out for the whole family. Seats are limited and advance booking is essential. 🌸🚂

events.long_description:
Mantra, Pranayama & Meditation Course
You practice asana but do you practice YOGA?

This intensive workshop explores the foundational theory, embodied practice, and teaching methodology of pranayama, meditation, and mantra — three profound and transformative limbs of yoga.

Over two full days (plus pre-recorded content to complete in your own time), you'll cover breathing physiology and the subtle body, foundational meditation techniques across multiple lineages, the ethics of mantra, and safe trauma-aware instruction. The workshop includes extensive practice teaching time with peer feedback — so you leave not just informed, but ready to teach.

What you'll learn:
*Breathing physiology and the subtle body
*Foundational meditation techniques across multiple lineages
*The theory and ethics of mantra
*Trauma-aware instruction for breath and meditation practices
*Practice teaching with structured peer feedback

Format:
* Two full-day in-person intensives (9:00 am – 5:00 pm) on Saturday 5th September & Saturday 26th September 2026
*Pre-recorded content to complete between sessions at your own pace
*One optional online wānanga to follow up after the course concludes (date/time TBD)

Who can enrol:
There are no restrictions on who can enrol for this course. Anyone with an interest in learning more about yoga beyond asana is welcome - Haere mai!

200-CYTs can receive 25 Continuing Education credits with Yoga Alliance *or* earn 25 hours towards AYS's 300hr YTT pathway!

Facilitator:
Tom Brotherstone (E-RYT 500) - AWHI co-owner with over a decade of teaching experience in Yin and Vinyasa yoga. Tom trained in Rishikesh, India and his focus is on building community through practice — providing supportive platforms for growth and self-discovery. His easeful, approachable style puts students immediately at ease, and his classes weave yoga philosophy throughout, grounding movement in meaning.

events.name: Mel Parsons - Castle Hill Album Release Tour
events.venue: The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
Singer-songwriting luminary, Mel Parsons, has announced a seven-date national theatre tour with her band in August and September 2026, celebrating her much-anticipated new album, CASTLE HILL, to released on August 7.

Plus1 proudly presents Mel Parsons live around Aotearoa in some of our country's most beautiful theatres.

Thursday August 27 - Theatre Royal, Nelson
Friday August 28 - Isaac Theatre Royal, Christchurch
Saturday August 29 - Glenroy Auditorium, Dunedin
Thursday September 3 - Clarence St Theatre, Hamilton
Friday September 4 - Q Theatre, Rangatira - Auckland
Saturday September 5 - Opera House, Wellington
Sunday September 6 - Globe Theatre, Palmerston North

Full tour info at plus1.co.nz and MelParsons.com

Taking its name from the remote mountain town in the Southern Alps where it was recorded, CASTLE HILL was produced by Josh Logan and recorded live with Mel’s longtime band members Aaron Stewart (bass) and Jed Parsons (drums); joined by Ben King (Goldenhorse, Grand Rapids) on guitars. Parsons says of these sessions: “it was a full immersion recording experience over a stolen summer holiday”

Following the release of SABOTAGE in 2024, multi-award winning Parsons toured the country with Crowded House, performed in Canada and Australia, and has continued her stellar run including a finalist nod for Best Folk Artist at the 2026 AMA’s.

Singles already released from the record include the alternative radio chart toppers Post High Slide, Brick By Brick, Be Here Now, Don't Leave The Light On, and Caravan, as well as new single Grain By Grain. Castle Hill album release tour is funded through NZ On Air and supported by the NZ Music Commission.

Expect soaring harmonies, a dynamic live show, and a feel-good vibe throughout as Mel Parsons performs live this August and September. Come and celebrate one of Aotearoa’s finest live artists!

events.name: Trip: Raumati South Peatlands
events.venue: Poplar Ave, Raumati South, Paraparaumu 5032,Paraparaumu, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Trip: Raumati South Peatlands
This property was originally held by the Crown as an alternative route for the Kāpiti Expressway. Now planned for housing, large areas are protected SNAs including an area of mostly intact mānukā/kanuka fen which is unusual on the Kāpiti Coast.

Species of note include Scrambling Coral-Fern (Gleichenia microphylla) and Fork-leaved Sundew (Drosera binata). Time can also be spent determining the presence of Kunzea robusta and/or Kunzea amathicola.

Meet: 9:30 am at entrance of Te Rā school. Park at the QEP entrance and cross the road, please don’t park at the school. If travelling by train a pick-up can be organised from Paeākāriki Station, or walk 3.6 km/50min from Paraparaumu Station.

Leader: Andy McKay (Tel 04 296 4653, Mobile 027 555 5653, )

Join Kelburn Community Garden and Seeds to Feeds on the first Saturday of every month at 11am for a volunteer working bee. (Note: we've switched up the usual date during autumn/winter to Saturdays and 11am.)

events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Widely regarded as one of the foremost songwriters of her generation, Suzanne Vega emerged as a leading figure of the folk revival of the early 1980s. Four decades later, she is still writing and singing great songs. In her Wellington show, Suzanne will perform a career-spanning set. See her on stage at St James Theatre performing favourites like Tom’s Diner, Luka, Marlene On The Wall, and plenty more. There’ll also be new songs from her 2025 album, ‘Flying with Angels’. Joining her on stage will be longtime guitarist, Gerry Leonard, and cellist Stephanie Winters. 
Since the release of her self-titled, critically acclaimed 1985 debut album, Suzanne Vega has played to sold-out concerts across the world. She is a masterful storyteller who, according to one The New York Times critique, “observes the world with a clinically poetic eye.” Her song lyrics often focus on city life, ordinary people, and real-world subjects. They are notably succinct, understated, and immediately recognisable.

events.long_description:
The Tui Express
Climb aboard The Tui Express for a spectacular, first-class rail experience. This is our fan-favourite excursion and an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages, making it the perfect, easy day out for anyone looking to enjoy a fantastic Sunday on the rails with friends and family. It also falls on Father's Day weekend, offering a wonderful opportunity to treat Dad.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front-row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to experience this than from our open-air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for taking photos, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.
Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. You can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, hot espresso coffees, and sweet treats right from the rails as the scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15-minute walk to the world-famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for you. Once at the brewery, relax and enjoy the iconic historic grounds. Your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non-alcoholic alternative) to wash it down. If you prefer to opt out of the meal, you can do so during booking for a discounted fare.

Your ticket covers your return journey from Plimmerton in beautifully maintained premium carriages alongside exclusive rail-only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling refreshments, espresso coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non-alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

Approximate Itinerary
Morning Travel – Northbound to Mangatainoka
Plimmerton depart – 7:50am
Paraparaumu depart – 8:25am
Ōtaki depart – 9:15am
Levin depart – 9:50am
Palmerston North depart – 11:00am
Mangatainoka arrive – 12:15pm

Evening Travel – Return Journey
Mangatainoka depart – 2:15pm
Palmerston North depart – 4:20pm
Levin depart – 5:15pm
Ōtaki depart – 5:40pm
Paraparaumu depart – 6:25pm
Plimmerton arrive – 6:50pm

Space in these premium carriages is strictly limited and this fan-favourite trip fills up incredibly fast, so secure your tickets today for an incredible Sunday on the rails!

events.long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass at the Winter Special Price!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Silver Clay Taster
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Precious Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant or earrings, or a collection of charms - it's up to you.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

𝐀𝐁𝐎𝐔𝐓 𝐒𝐔𝐙𝐀𝐍𝐍𝐄 𝐕𝐄𝐆𝐀

Widely regarded as one of the foremost songwriters of her generation, Suzanne Vega emerged as a leading figure of the folk revival of the early 1980s. Accompanying herself on acoustic guitar, Vega sang what has been called contemporary folk or neo-folk songs of her own creation in Greenwich Village clubs. Since the release of her self-titled, critically acclaimed 1985 debut album, she has given sold-out concerts in many of the world’s best-known venues. Known for performances that convey deep emotion, Vega’s distinctive, “clear, unwavering voice” (Rolling Stone) has been described as “a cool, dry sandpaper-brushed near-whisper” by The Washington Post, with NPR Music noting that she “has been making vital, inventive music” throughout the course of her decades-long career. Bearing the stamp of a masterful storyteller who “observes the world with a clinically poetic eye” (The New York Times), Vega’s songs have tended to focus on city life, ordinary people and real-world subjects. Notably succinct and understated, her work is immediately recognizable—as utterly distinct and thoughtful as it was when her voice was first heard on the radio over 40 years ago.

events.venue: 3 Market Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011
events.long_description:
Silver Clay Taster - Spring
Join us in our warm and friendly studio to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Silver Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants, earrings or charms. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Silver Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant, earrings, or a couple of charms.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous). We will also have gold leaf available to purchase.

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

Workshop fee $185, early bird $167 till 16 August.

Imagine Wellington B.C. (Before Coffee). Thankfully, we don't have to.

Treat yourself to a cup of history with the closing weekend event for Wellington Museum's Capital of Kai exhibition with the C is for Coffee Walking Tour.

Beginning at Wellington Museum, Senior Curator Ian Wards will take you along Willis Street and discuss the capital's introduction to cafe culture. You'll continue onto Dixon Street for more iconic Wellington coffee highlights and wrap up on Cuba Street at Midnight Espresso, one of the longest-standing cafes in the city.

events.long_description:
Overview

Hear from leading experts in typography and design history for a panel discussion on the Future of Print.

Join leading experts in typography, print culture, and design history, including Vanessa Wairata Edwards-Buerger, Professor Indra Kupferschmid, Kris Sowersby, and Professor Johnson Witehira, as they explore the past, present, and future of print.

Drawing on perspectives from Germany and Aotearoa New Zealand, the international panel will consider print's historical evolution, its complex and contested introduction to Aotearoa, and the current and future roles of printing in visual and material culture.

Tuesday 8 September

5.30 – 8.00 pm

Panel Discussion 6.15 pm

The Pit Lecture Theatre, Block 12 Level C

Massey University Pukeahu Wellington Campus

Light refreshments will be served from 5.30pm, before the panel discussion begins at 6.15 pm. Parking on campus will be free in unmarked, unlined car parks.

Vanessa Wairata Edwards-Buerger (Ngāti Tūwharetoa, Whakatohea, Ngāti Kuri & Ngāti Kahu) is an artist and curator based in Whanganui, where she works as Educator at Te Whare o Rehua Sarjeant Gallery. Her print practice explores Māori cultural sovereignty, whakapapa, and storytelling through traditional and experimental techniques like drypoint, relief printing, and mixed-media sgraffito. She is a founding member of Toi Whakaata Māori, a collective of Māori printmakers dedicated to advancing Māori printmaking through creative practice, collaboration, and cultural exchange.

Professor Indra Kupferschmid is Professor of Typography and Type Design at HBKsaar (University of the Arts Saarbrücken, Germany) and a member of the DIN committees on type legibility and classification. An internationally respected typographic scholar, her research has focused on the history of twentieth-century German sans-serif typefaces, including Akzidenz-Grotesk and Neue Haas-Grotesk/Helvetica, as well as the ways in which type production technologies have evolved over time. Author of the award-winning typographic reference Buchstaben kommen selten allein and co-author of Helvetica Forever, she has spent nearly three decades teaching typography across Europe. For more information: https://www.hbksaar.de/personen/details/kupferschmid

Kris Sowersby is the founder, director & lead type designer of Klim Type Foundry (Klim). Through Klim, Sowersby has developed bespoke typographic solutions for a global clientele, including The Financial Times, PayPal, and National Geographic and Apple. Within Aotearoa, his practice includes the creation of custom type for The Bank of New Zealand, Trade Me, and Tourism New Zealand. He is a member of the Alliance Graphique Internationale and was named an Art Laureate by The Arts Foundation for his continuing contribution to New Zealand Art and Design. For more information: https://klim.co.nz/about/

Professor Johnson Witehira (Tamahaki, Ngāi Tū-te-auru & Ngāti Hinekura) is Professor of Toi Hangarau – Creative Technologies – at Massey University, and Head of School of Te Rewa o Puanga, Music and Screen Arts. He is a distinguished indigenous artist, designer, and academic whose work integrates Mātauranga Māori with contemporary creative technologies, aiming to decolonize and indigenize design and digital media. Together with Kris Sowersby, Professor Witehira developed Matarongo, a contemporary digital typeface family built from rigorous research into Māori letterforms. Witehira traced Māori letterforms through traditional crafts, from tuhi waitohu (hand lettering) to tātai kupu toi (typography), and Sowersby translated that research into type. For more information: https://www.johnsonwitehira.studio/about

The Future of Print is presented by Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, Massey University, in partnership with The German Embassy Wellington.

Read less

Overview

Discover the science behind better health with Presidential Director Marcia Schaefer.

Join us for a special First Look event with Presidential Director Marcia Schaefer, DC, a licensed Chiropractor and passionate health educator, as she explores The Missing link in health

We all strive to make healthier choices, eating well, staying active and looking after our wellbeing. But what if the key isn't simply doing all the right things, but understanding what's missing and putting the pieces together in the right order?

In this engaging session, Marcia will explore the science behind healthy ageing, glycans and the vital role they play in supporting communication at the cellular level. Discover why providing your body with the right nutritional foundation may be the missing link to helping you get the most from your overall health and wellness journey.

Since partnering with Mannatech in 2010, Marcia has been dedicated to educating practitioners and communities on the importance of nutrition, preconception health and creating the conditions for healthier generations. Her ability to simplify complex science into practical, everyday knowledge has inspired audiences around the world.

Whether you're new to Mannatech, wanting to learn more about glycans, or looking to better understand the science behind healthy ageing, this is an event you won't want to miss.

Join us for an inspiring and educational evening that may change the way you think about health and discover why glycans are considered by many to be the missing link.




Visit the Venue Site: The Loft at Harbourside Function Centre

Parking: Please note that there is no on-site parking available at Harbourside Function Centre.

events.name: TAHI: New Zealand Festival of Solo Performance
events.long_description:
Comedy, cabaret, poetry, family-friendly acts, and world premieres are all on the radar for this theatrical event. The annual TAHI NZ Festival of Solo Performance provides a stage for more than 25 actors, celebrating emerging artists to experienced professionals. Storylines vary from rugby to the manosphere to an improvised nature documentary. Laughing and crying are both considered acceptable responses.

Tahi in Te Reo Māori translates to ‘one’, but another translation for this word is ’unity’. Dr. Sally Richards, director of TAHI, chose the name because of this duality. Solo theatre requires both personal courage and creative collaboration. As Sally says, “I see the stage manager, broom in hand, sweep before and after a performance. It reminds me that the solo performer is a misnomer — that solo performance relies on successful collaboration with others.”

Discover the brilliance of solo theatre at TAHI this September.

events.long_description:
Overview

Create a team that communicates better, takes ownership, and solves problems together.

Every team experiences tension.

A conversation goes sideways. Someone starts blaming. Another person steps in to fix everything. Before long, the real issue has been lost and the same pattern begins again.

This free leadership session will help you recognise those patterns and respond differently.

Leadership: Escape the Drama Triangle is a practical 90-minute workshop for business owners and team leaders who want their people to communicate clearly, take greater ownership, and solve problems together.

During the session, we will explore how workplace conversations can fall into the roles of Victim, Rescuer and Villain, and how leaders can help shift those conversations from blame, excuses and denial towards responsibility, accountability and ownership. This reflects the workbook’s movement from the “Victim Cycle” to the “Victor Cycle” and its focus on improving the quality of words, conversations, relationships, collaboration and achievement.

You will learn how to:

Recognise the Drama Triangle in everyday team conversations
Identify when people are operating below the line
Avoid rescuing, blaming or taking over
Reframe conversations so people can take responsibility
Create clearer, more productive team discussions
Help your team move from problems towards practical next steps

This is not about removing every disagreement from your workplace.

It is about giving you a simple way to recognise unhelpful patterns early and guide the conversation towards a better outcome.

You will leave with practical language and ideas you can begin using with your team straight away.

Who is this for?

This session is suitable for:

Business owners
Managers and team leaders
People responsible for workplace culture
Leaders dealing with repeated communication issues
Anyone who finds themselves stepping in to solve everyone else’s problems

Event details

Date: 9 September 
Time: 12:00 pm–1:30 pm 
Venue: Paraparaumu Beach Golf Club 
Cost: Free

Places are limited, so early registration is recommended.

blackpill
In the deepest reaches of the online manosphere, incels (involuntary celibates) preach their dogmatic ideology, express profound hatred for women, and share their own pervasive loneliness. But what draws young men into these spaces, and why do they stay?

This verbatim solo play takes you inside the forums where isolation turns to misogyny turns to violence. Darkly funny and occasionally disturbing, blackpill interrogates an ideology that offers both belonging and misery.

After a critically acclaimed 2024 development season, blackpill has its world premiere at TAHI 2026.

Recommended 16+. Contains verbatim content from extremist forums, and as such includes content that may offend or disturb including but not limited to hate speech, expressions of body dysmorphia, and suicidal ideation. Audience discretion is advised. Contains flashing lights/strobe.

Creator/Writer/Director: Rachel McLean
Performer: Zachary Klein

About this Event



Pasifika Business Fono 2026 🌺

Your business. Your voice. Our future.




Calling all Pasifika in business across the Wellington region!




Whether you’re running an established business, building your first start-up, growing a side hustle, or simply thinking about starting your business journey, we want you in the room.

The Wellington Pasifika Business Network (WPBN) is bringing Pasifika business owners, entrepreneurs, start-ups, and aspiring business owners together for a special Pasifika Business Fono.

This is an opportunity to come together, connect, share your experiences, and have your say on what Pasifika businesses across our region need to thrive.




Help shape the future of WPBN

WPBN is entering an exciting new phase, and we want to hear directly from our Pasifika business community about what matters most to you.

What support do you need?
What opportunities are you looking for?
What are the barriers you're facing?
What would make a real difference to your business?




Your voice will help us shape our next network strategy and future programmes, events, and business support so that WPBN can deliver what our Pasifika business community needs.

This isn't a formal presentation where you sit and listen, it's a fono. A chance to Talanoa, connect, share ideas and build relationships with other Pasifika people on their business journey.




Meet the WPBN Board

Come along and meet members of the Wellington Pasifika Business Network Board, find out more about who we are and what we do, and learn about the support, connections, opportunities and benefits available to you through WPBN membership.




Whether you're already a member or have never connected with WPBN before, you are welcome.




Come for the fono. Stay for the connections.

Expect an evening of:

Talanoa and meaningful conversation
Connecting with other Pasifika business owners and entrepreneurs
Sharing ideas, challenges and opportunities
Having your voice heard and helping shape WPBN's future
Meeting the WPBN Board and learning about membership
Discovering opportunities for business support and connection
Delicious refreshments provided by a local Island catering company

LOWER HUTT
📅 Wednesday 9 September 2026
📍 The Dowse Art Museum, Lower Hutt
🕠 Doors open: 5:30pm
🕕 Fono starts: 6:00pm

🎟️ FREE COMMUNITY EVENT

This is a free event open to Pasifika people across the Wellington region who are:

✔️ Established business owners
✔️ Start-up founders
✔️ Side hustlers
✔️ Aspiring entrepreneurs
✔️ People thinking about starting a business
✔️ Pasifika professionals and partners who support our business community

Everyone is welcome, wherever you are on your business journey.




📌 RSVP IS ESSENTIAL

This event is free, but RSVPs are essential so we can make sure we have enough space and, most importantly, enough delicious kai for everyone.

Come along, bring your ideas, bring your questions, bring your business journey, and let's shape the future of Pasifika business together.

Your voice matters. Your business matters. Our collective future matters.




🌺 Fa'afetai, Malo lava, Kia manuia, we look forward to seeing you there!

events.long_description:
Grab a spot on our couch and enjoy the noise at The Racket Lounge - a chill classical music series showcasing up-and-coming Pōneke musicians.
If you’ve never been to a classical concert before, or if you have and now you want to see talented emerging musicians experimenting and playing what they want to play, then The Racket Lounge is for you. Over the past two seasons we’ve seen classical covers, jazz ensembles, video game soundtracks, original compositions, loop pedals, poetry and much more. Our 2026 season is shaping up to be just as epic, plus with your tickets starting at just $5 you can afford to take a chance on something new.
Each concert will feature a different line up of musicians and genres, to be announced a week before each session. If you’re a musician looking to perform at The Racket Lounge, then head to the New Zealand String Quartet’s website to see how to apply.
So, we’ll see you at Bedlam and Squalor to make a racket!
The Racket Lounge is created and presented by the New Zealand String Quartet Trust - Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa, New Zealand’s longest-running professional string quartet. With support from Wellington City Council.
Our ticket prices range from $5 to $100, so just pick the ticket price you feel like paying. At The Racket Lounge, we believe everyone should have access to high-quality but affordable art. If you're a bit strapped for cash right now, but still want a good night out, no worries! Just book yourself a $5 ticket! If you can afford to pay a little more and want to do some good for your community, then pick one of our higher ticket prices and rest assured that your dollars are going towards funding great, accessible art in your city.
All proceeds from ticket sales will go directly into presenting the next Racket Lounge, including paying musicians and artists, hiring instruments and marketing costs. Plus, by choosing a higher price point, you're ensuring that we're able to continue to offer tickets at a lower price point for those who need it.
PLEASE NOTE: Bedlam & Squalor is a licensed venue, so under 18s must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. Everyone must bring ID.

Overview

Learn ways to resolve conflict with customers and co-workers, influence successful outcomes and develop a peaceful workplace.

Transform conflict and difficult situations, people/customers into opportunities by equipping your staff with the skills and techniques required to manage these situations with confidence, professionalism and pride.

We have all experienced the stress that comes from having unresolved conflicts with our customers and co-workers. Conflicts that are ignored or resolved poorly don’t go away, they cause people to feel resentful and to avoid each other. The effects on the business are a loss of productivity, turnover and absenteeism. Wherever two or more people come together, there is bound to be conflict. This workshop will give participants a six-step process that they can use and modify to resolve conflicts of any size. Participants will also learn crucial conflict resolution skills, including dealing with anger and using the Agreement Frame.


Learning Outcomes:

Transform conflict into opportunity
Develop constructive strategies for dealing with difficult behavior
Develop communication skills to diffuse the situation
Increase confidence and assertiveness in dealing with difficult behaviour
Manage your emotions and deal with stress
Understand the power of words and how to use them to your advantage


For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 06 354 5555

Overview

Please note: This workshop is designed for the public and is not for health professionals.

This workshop offers helpful information for Family/Whānau about death and dying. Advance care planning and community resources will be discussed.




Many people find it difficult to talk about dying, yet dying is an important stage of life and is inevitable. We plan for the birth of a child, yet when it comes to the end of life, we don’t often want to think about it or talk about it.




Having a plan outlines our care preferences for the future. Having an Advance Care Plan (ACP) that aligns with our beliefs and values, is a gift that we can give to our family / whānau.




We will explore:


Why is it hard to talk about death and dying?

What to expect when someone is dying

Supports available

Advance care planning processes

Join us for a very special lunchtime recital.

Concert pianist Lưu Hồng Quang presents a remarkable programme from Franz Liszt's Years of Pilgrimage, Third Volume – a deeply spiritual and reflective work from the composer's later years.

This performance forms the final public presentation of Lưu Hồng Quang's Doctor of Musical Arts research at the New Zealand School of Music | Te Kōkī. What is Advance Care Planning (ACP)?

This workshop is for anyone wanting a "hands on" help with thier ACP - either to start or to finish.

Advance Care Planning is about thinking ahead, talking with your whānau and healthcare team, and making decisions about the care you want if you are unable to speak for yourself.

Learn more about what advanced care planning is, work through a tailored guide, and capture what matters most to you should you become unwell and unable to speak for yourself.

events.long_description:
Overview

Share ceremonial cacao, heartfelt conversation and a nourishing dinner in an evening of authentic connection and presence.

Cacao & Connection Circle
Starts at 6pm

This evening is an invitation to slow down, be present, and experience genuine human connection. Together we'll share ceremonial cacao, meaningful conversation, and a welcoming space where there's no need to perform, impress, or have all the right words. Just come as you are.

What to Expect

We'll begin with a gentle grounding practice to help everyone arrive. This is an opportunity to pause, settle into the present moment, and reconnect with yourself before connecting with others.

From there, we'll gather in a circle to share ceremonial cacao. 

We'll then move into a heart-sharing circle. A thoughtful question will be offered as a prompt, and you're warmly invited, but never expected to share your experience. There is no advice-giving or fixing here. Instead, we practise honest expression, deep listening, and creating space for one another to simply be witnessed.

What Heart-Sharing Can Offer

 Authentic Connection

Experience the kind of connection that comes from being seen, heard, and accepted exactly as you are.

Meaningful Conversation

Step beyond everyday small talk into conversations that invite honesty, curiosity, and presence.

Greater Self-Awareness

Sharing and listening often brings unexpected clarity about your own thoughts, emotions, and life experiences.

Gentle Personal Growth

Speaking from the heart and listening without judgement can quietly shift perspectives and deepen understanding.

A Sense of Belonging

Being part of a supportive circle can ease feelings of isolation and remind us that we all share common human experiences.

 

After the circle, we'll enjoy a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert together, both included in your ticket. It's a relaxed time to continue conversations, connect naturally, and simply enjoy each other's company.

Meet Andre, your host:

Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.




Read less

events.venue:

Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Journey inward through Māori sound, pūrākau and crystal bowls, creating a peaceful evening of deep listening, rest and restoration.

Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey




Starts at 6pm

Experience a peaceful Māori sound journey blending taonga pūoro, story, and crystal bowls for deep relaxation and inner calm

“Āio” speaks to peace and inner calm. In this immersive evening, pūrākau, taonga pūoro and waiata are woven together with the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls, creating a space for deep listening, rest and restoration.

The organic tones of traditional Māori instruments including kōauau, pūtōrino, porotiti and pūtātara blend with the resonance of crystal bowls, chimes and ukulele, inviting you to slow down, soften and reconnect with your wairua and body. Through story, sound and vibration, this is a gentle journey inward.

What to bring:

Yoga mats, blankets and cushions will be provided, but you are welcome to bring extra for comfort!




After the sound journey, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket, a warm way to close the evening together.

Meet your hosts & musicians: Smita, Peter, and Alexandra:

Smita (Ngāi Te Rangi) was born and raised in Aotearoa. From a young age she was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.

Peter is Pākehā, with grandparents from England and Ireland, and has been on a four-year journey learning the art of taonga pūoro — the traditional Māori musical instruments of Aotearoa. Guided by the wisdom and generosity of expert makers and players, he has learned both to craft and to play these unique instruments. For Peter, taonga pūoro offer a way to connect deeply with sound, story, and the natural world, and he is excited to share their voices as part of this sound bath experience.

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Pub Sing - where the audience turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band,

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

events.name: Pianist Lưu Hồng Quang Performs Liszt at Lunchtime
events.venue: Old St Paul's
events.long_description:
Pianist Lưu Hồng Quang Performs Liszt at Lunchtime
Join us for a special lunchtime recital as concert pianist Lưu Hồng Quang presents a remarkable programme from Franz Liszt's Years of Pilgrimage, Third Volume – a deeply spiritual and reflective work from the composer's later years.

This performance forms the final public presentation of Lưu Hồng Quang's Doctor of Musical Arts research at the New Zealand School of Music | Te Kōkī. The Third Volume of Years of Pilgrimage is among Liszt's most profound yet least frequently performed works, making this a rare opportunity for Wellingtonians to experience this extraordinary music in the fitting surroundings of Old St Paul's.

Adding to the occasion, Lưu Hồng Quang leaves New Zealand shortly after the recital, making this a fleeting chance to hear him perform before his departure.

All very welcome.

Entry by koha.

Artist's webpage: https://luuhongquang.com/

events.long_description:
Big Low Dream - Wellington
BIG LOW DREAM is a new contemporary dance work about what we reach for, together, in the dark. Choreographer Jessie McCall looks to dream logic - unruly, queer, ethically imaginative, as a way to hold onto meaning in a time of overlapping crises. Paradises slip their frames. Unexpected pleasures co-inhabit with the unthinkable. Spectacle flirts with collapse.

Ominous and funny, intimate and sweeping, BIG LOW DREAM is a rehearsal of possible futures — tender, desperate, and rising.

Choose Your Price Night - preview show Thurs 10 Sept 7pm

Creative Team
Choreography: Jessie McCall
Production Design: Meg Rollandi
Sound Design: Thomas Lambert
Lighting Design: Tony Black

Cast
Airu Matsuda, Caleb Heke, Sasha Matsumoto, Millie Maden

Praise for Jesie McCall:

"Through the combined impact of dance and design, McCall enables multiple truths to coexist, just as they do in our reality… This is a production in the hands of an artist who knows precisely what they’re doing. It’s focused and formidable; well-made and compelling." - Tate Fountain, Bad Apple, 13 October 2022 for I GET SO EMOTIONAL BABY

“Deeply perceptive and provocative work… It does exactly what art is supposed to do – it opens a window into our soul, and shines a light on moments we may often try to keep hidden.” - Emily Napolitano, Theatreview for TASSEL ME THIS

events.long_description:
Over three sessions, create stunning jewellery using the age-old lost wax technique. This is an excellent opportunity to treat yourself to some creative fun on a Friday night!

In weeks one and two, you will learn how to work with jeweller's hard wax to create beautiful textures in metal that can be used to create amazing rings or objects. Your waxes will be sent away for casting in the metal of your choice.

Then there will be a week's break before the third session, to allow time for everyone's waxes to be cast. The third session covers how to trim, clean and finish your casts, turning them into original jewellery ready to wear!

More advanced students can use these sessions to complete projects in a class setting.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs which vary from student to student depending on what sized ring they want to make and the type of metal you choose. Small castings can cost around $6.65 - $12 and might cost between $7 to $30 in metals depending on if you use red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is great for teens and kids over 12 or so. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
Pioneers of the iconic Madchester sound, the Happy Mondays are heading back to New Zealand to celebrate the 35th anniversary of their seminal album, Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches.
Fusing funk, rock, psychedelia, and house with the pulsating energy of the UK’s burgeoning rave scene, the Happy Mondays became the face of a cultural revolution. Their 1990 release, Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches, catapulted them into the mainstream, spending over six months on the UK Albums Chart and earning its place as one of the defining records of the decade.
Fronted by the inimitable Shaun Ryder, with Bez ( freaky dancing and percussion), Mark Day (guitar), Gary Whelan (drums), Mikey Shine (bass), Dan Broad (musical director/guitar/keys), and Firouzeh Berry (backing vocals), the band will perform highlights from the classic album; including anthems like Step On, Kinky Afro, and Loose Fit, alongside fan favourites such as 24 Hour Party People, Hallelujah, Judge Fudge, and W.F.L.
Their enduring influence on British music was formally recognised in 2016 when they received the prestigious Ivor Novello Inspiration Award, a testament to their legacy as one of the UK’s most beloved and groundbreaking bands.
‘Always a great buzz when we play Australia and New Zealand . Looking forward to bringing the Happy Mondays Pills ‘n’ Thrills party there in September’’ - Shaun Ryder
This isn’t just a tour, it’s a full-throttle revival of Madchester chaos, and the year's wildest party is coming.

events.long_description:
AI Masterclass: Going Further with AI
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $250 with ID.)
You’ve been using AI for a while – maybe daily. You know how to prompt. But you’re still doing one-shot chats when your work deserves a proper system. This masterclass changes that.
Before you arrive, you’ll fill in a short intake form – what you do, what you want AI for, and what you can’t do (paste client data into public ChatGPT, work outside regulated tools, etc.). Jon reads every submission before class and shapes the day around the room. We won’t be doing a generic feature tour; the day is built to be a hands-on and customised workshop.
We’ll spend the day wiring AI into your actual work: the Claude desktop app, connectors to the tools you already use, a project built around your real documents and tasks, and Claude Design. You’ll leave with a working AI system to improve your life and work.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
•     Set up the Claude desktop app with Chat, Co-work, and Code – ready for real work
•     Enable and use connectors (Gmail, Drive, calendar) – and know which ones to leave off
•     Build a Claude project around your own documents and tasks, with voice input and plan mode
•     Write operating rules for your workspace – constraints, verification triggers, what never goes in public chat
•     Discover and run Anthropic-provided skills on your real task
•     Stress-test your output with synthetic personas before you ship
•     Produce polished visual artifacts with Claude Design
•     Apply professional judgement: when to delegate, when to verify, when not to use AI at all
 Please bring: A laptop (Co-work and Code need a keyboard). The Claude desktop app installed and signed in. A paid Claude subscription (Pro or Team) – required for connectors, Co-work, and skills. Your intake form submitted at least 3 days before class. One real task you want to work on.
  A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Burnout to Balance - Proven Techniques to Pause, Recover & Return!
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In today’s high-pressure world, burnout is often worn as a badge of honour—until the physical and mental toll becomes impossible to ignore. True recovery requires more than just "taking a break"; it requires resetting the nervous system from the inside out.
Led by Simon, a former high-stakes litigation lawyer who successfully navigated his own severe burnout, this workshop bridges the gap between understanding stress and actively healing from it. This practical, evidence-based workshop is designed to take you on a journey from chronic depletion to sustainable balance. You will explore what burnout actually is, identify your personal triggers, and master powerful physiological techniques to pause the stress response, recover your vitality, and return to life and work with renewed resilience.
What We Will Cover
Part 1: Understanding the Burnout Cycle (The Setup)
Before we can fix the problem, we must understand it. We begin by unpacking the foundations of chronic stress to help you map your own journey.
What is Burnout? Defining the psychological and physical parameters of exhaustion.
The Root Causes: Identifying the systemic, professional, and personal drivers of chronic stress.
The Nervous System Hijack: How prolonged pressure traps the body in a constant "fight-or-flight" state, impacting sleep, digestion, and cognitive function.
Part 2: The Science of Physiological Recovery (The Solution)
While mindset matters, burnout lives in the body. We will introduce the fastest, most effective tool for resetting a hijacked nervous system: Functional Breathing Training.
The Three Dimensions of Health: How biochemical, biomechanical, and psychophysiological breathing patterns dictate your stress levels.
Measuring Your Stress Tolerance: Learn how to assess your current breathing efficiency and physiological stress baseline.
Immediate Relief vs. Long-Term Resilience: Practices that offer instant calm during acute anxiety, paired with lifelong training to rebuild your nervous system.
What You Will Walk Away With
By the end of this one-day workshop, you will:
Recognise the Warning Signs: Deeply understand your own burnout triggers and early warning indicators.
Interrupt the Stress Response: Master proven, discreet techniques to pause the "fight-or-flight" response in real-time.
Improve Everyday Well-being: Know how to optimise your breathing patterns to combat poor sleep, fatigue, and brain fog.
A Personalised Recovery Plan: Walk away with a practical toolkit to integrate self-regulation and physical recovery into a busy professional life.
What to Bring: Please bring a notepad and pen to track your personal pacing metrics, record your breathing patterns, and map out your recovery strategy.
Participant Self-Management & Safety
This workshop is designed for adult learners. It is a supportive, respectful space where you are encouraged to engage at your own comfort level and self-manage your energy throughout the day (including taking breaks to decompress as needed).
Please note: The advanced physiological recovery techniques practiced in this workshop are highly effective for nervous system regulation. No prior experience with breathwork or yoga is required.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

“Relationships are all there is. Everything in the universe only exists because it is in relationship to everything else. Nothing exists in isolation. We have to stop pretending we are individuals that can go it alone.” -Margaret J. Wheatley
You aren't alone. In a world of screens, finding genuine, in-person connection can feel surprisingly tough. But building a supportive network and circles doesn't require a total personality makeover—it starts with who you already are.
This hands-on, high-energy workshop is designed to help you map out your unique strengths, passions, and existing ties to build a community where you truly belong. We skip the generic networking advice and dive straight into practical, real-world tools to help you spark meaningful relationships.
What you’ll walk away with:
Your Personal Connection Map: A clear overview of your unique interests, strengths, and hidden community links.
The "Icebreaker" Blueprint: 1–2 simple frameworks to confidently shift casual small talk into deeper, more rewarding conversations.
The "Reach Out" Breakthrough: Break the ice right then and there by sending two messages or writing a letter during the session—getting the hardest part out of the way!
A Ready-to-Use Action Plan: A customised roadmap to connect with 1–3 new or existing friends, with your first milestone already crushed before you leave.
"Networking is not about just connecting people. It's about connecting people with people, people with ideas, and people with opportunities." — Michele Jennae

events.long_description:
Overview

A self-publishing workshop delivered by an internationally bestselling author.

Are you interested in learning how to become a full-time self-supporting author?

Want to see your name on best-seller lists around the world?

Have you always dreamed of seeing a book that you wrote on the shelves at your local bookshop or library, available for anyone to read?

Or maybe you dream of being published with one of the big traditional publishing houses but have discovered that the main way they're picking up books nowadays is by scooping up already successful independently published authors?

This three hour workshop will be delivered by George Penney, an internationally bestselling author of fiction and non-fiction, a twenty-year industry veteran who has been published both through Penguin Random House and independently, and the owner of Swashbuckler Press, an independent publishing company formerly based in London--now in Nelson, New Zealand.

It will provide you with a crash-course rundown on how to independently publish and distribute your novels, poems and short stories, using the same processes, editors, cover designers, and distribution techniques as the large publishing houses.

Participants will leave with a solid starter-foundation for establishing a successful publishing career.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

Overview

Tap into your inner knowing through Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation and sound.

This workshop is part of an 8-part chakra journey across 2026. Each session stands alone or can be experienced as part of the full series.

Join us for an afternoon of deep connection as we explore the Third Eye Chakra (Ajna) through the powerful practices of Kundalini Yoga and the healing vibrations of a Gong Bath.

The Third Eye Chakra is the centre of intuition, insight, clarity, and inner knowing. When balanced, it helps you trust your intuition, quiet mental chatter, and see life's path with greater clarity. Through movement, breathwork, meditation, and sound, we'll create space to connect with your inner wisdom and restore balance to this energy centre.

🧘‍♀️Kundalini Yoga | 1:30pm – 3:00pm

Experience a 90-minute Kundalini Yoga class designed to awaken the Third Eye Chakra through breathwork (Pranayama), dynamic movement and postures, meditation, and deep relaxation.

☕Herbal Tea Break | 3:00pm – 3:30pm

Take time to relax, enjoy a cup of herbal tea, oracle cards and connect with others in a welcoming and supportive environment.

🎶Gong Bath | 3:30pm – 4:30pm

Lie back, get comfortable, and allow the soothing sounds and vibrations of the gong to guide you into a deeply restorative state of relaxation. A gong bath can help calm the nervous system, release stress, and leave you feeling refreshed and centred.

✨Choose the experience that suits you—you are welcome to attend either the yoga or the gong bath sessions or enjoy the full afternoon.

💫Suitable for beginners and experienced practitioners alike - no experience with yoga or sound healing needed. Modifications are offered throughout the yoga class.

💫 Bring an open heart, a yoga mat, blanket, water bottle and anything you need to feel cozy + supported.

✨Whether you're joining the entire afternoon or just one session, you'll leave feeling calmer, clearer, and more deeply connected to yourself.

Spaces are limited, so bookings are recommended.

Investment:

$35 Yoga | $30 Gong Bath | $55 Both

Special discounted ticket options:

$100 two person special - bring a friend with you to attend the yoga and the gong session. Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. both people must book together).
$150 three workshop special - for one person to attend the last three workshops in this series (both kundalini yoga and gong bath) - on 12 September (third eye), 18 October (crown), and 6 December (aura). Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. all 3 workshops must be booked together).

If you want to pay by cash on the day or by bank transfer, please send an email to mel@prosperityyoga.co.nz to book your place.

events.long_description:
Dying Matters Week, FREE Tawa Community Expo

Join us in Tawa for the FREE Dying Matters Week Wellington Expo, a welcoming community event where you can explore, ask questions, and discover the many ways people are helping our communities navigate dying, death, grief, and bereavement.




Whether you’re planning ahead, supporting someone you love, or simply curious to learn more, there’s something for everyone.

Meet a diverse range of people who are passionate about sharing their knowledge, services, products, lived experience, and ideas.




Ever wondered what terramation is and why more people are talking about this environmentally conscious alternative? Curious about pet water cremation and the choices now available to honour our beloved animal companions? Or perhaps you’d like to learn about the beautiful role of Whakaahuru -The Gentle Singers, who offer comfort through song at the bedside, along with many other people, ideas, and services you may never have considered before.




Explore the stall holders below and start planning who you’d like to meet. We look forward to welcoming you to Tawa!

Agnes “Aggie” Widfeldt, Celebrant
Angela Robertson, Write Your Life Story – Penning Your Past
Annette Burrell, Inner Path
Aquafare – Pet Funerals and Aquamation (Water Cremation)
Cancer Society
Claire Laurenson, Grief Relief
Coveted Jewellery
Death Without Debt
ELDAA – End of Life Doula Alliance Aotearoa
Final Farewell, Funeral Planning
Gemma O’Donnell, Lawyer – Chronically Legal
Healing Touch NZ
Health & Disability Advocacy Service
Jennifer Watson, Life Coach and Grief Educator
Kristen Phillips, Author – Dad You’ve Got Dementia
Kylie Welch, Children’s Book Author
Lee-Anne Duncan, Too Young – Childhood Parental Bereavement
Mary Potter Hospice
Miranda Smith Homecare
MyTrove
Porirua Cemeteries
Terramation Aotearoa – Natural Organic Reduction
Third Story – Angela Swan, Senior Project Leader
Whakaahuru – The Gentle Singers
Wellington and Ōtaki Natural Burials







Healing Touch NZ will also be offering complimentary Healing Touch sessions throughout the afternoon. A sign-up sheet will be available on the day.




Questions to 




Three sessions (also free) will be running alongside the expo and can be booked separately:

• Legal Information Session with Gemma O’Donnell from Chronically Legal

• An Introduction to the Beautiful Role of Whakaahuru – The Gentle Singers

• Crystal Singing Bowl Experience with Annette Burrell from Inner Path

To book one of these free sessions, head to the Dying Matters Week Wellington events page and RSVP to the event you would like to attend to secure your place.

Places are limited, so registration is essential.




Find out more at Go With Grace https://gowithgrace.nz/resources/events/dying-matters-week/wellington-events/porirua-and-tawa/

Overview

Experience Marlborough’s Arts Trail and Gala Evening with Michael Hurst. Art, artists, and inspiration.

The Alzheimers Arts Trail returns for its fifth year on 19 & 20 September 2026, showcasing the depth and diversity of artistic talent across Marlborough.

Now a much-anticipated event on the local arts calendar, the Trail invites visitors to step inside studios and exhibition spaces, meet the artists behind the work, and experience creativity in a uniquely personal way.

2026 promises to be our biggest and most engaging Arts Trail yet, connecting artists with a wider audience while supporting the important work of Alzheimers Marlborough.

NOTE: Arts Trail brochures must be collected in person...details below.




Gala Evening

Saturday 12 September 2026

6.00pm - 8.30pm
Hosted by Oak & Ivy, 42 Alfred Street, Blenheim

Join us for a special Gala Opening Evening to launch the Arts Trail in style.

Enjoy a relaxed and vibrant evening featuring canapés and Hunters Wines, alongside an inspiring talk from guest speaker Michael Hurst.

With a career spanning more than 30 years, Michael Hurst is one of New Zealand’s most respected actors. Alongside Jennifer Ward-Lealand, he recently starred in the acclaimed production of In Other Words, a powerful and moving story exploring the impact of Alzheimer’s.

A natural storyteller and engaging speaker, Michael will share insights and stories from his remarkable career in the arts.

The evening will also feature both a live auction, raising funds to support the important work of Alzheimer’s Marlborough.

A wonderful evening of conversation, creativity and community.

Tickets:

$55 per person




Alzheimers Arts Trail

Saturday 19 & Sunday 20 September 2026
10:00am – 4:00pm daily
Locations: Across Marlborough (multiple studios and galleries)

A self drive event over two days, the Arts Trail opens the doors to artists across the region, offering a unique behind-the-scenes look at Marlborough’s creative talent.

What to expect:

Open studios and gallery spaces
Meet-the-artist experiences
A wide variety of art styles and mediums
Opportunities to purchase original artwork

Visitors will receive a full Arts Trail programme with trail map, allowing you to plan your own route and discover Marlborough’s vibrant creative community.

Tickets:

$25 Early Bird Ticket per person
$30 General Ticket per person (from 1 August)




Arts Trail brochures to be collected in person from:

Wine + Food Experience, 42 Alfred Street, Bleheim

Wednesday 16th, Thursday 17th, Friday 18th September, 4.00pm - 6.30pm

Saturday19th & Sunday 20th September, 10.00am - 12.00pm

Silent Art Auction




In the lead-up to the Arts Trail, browse and bid on an outstanding collection of donated artworks in the Silent Art Auction.

An inspiring gala with curated art and experiences, raising funds for support services and family violence prevention in our community.

One Night. One Cause. Lasting Impact.
Join us for an inspiring evening of connection and purpose; all in support of building a safer, stronger community for wāhine and whānau.


The Women’s Support Motueka Gala is a special fundraising event dedicated to strengthening our prevention work alongside our essential support services. Every day, we walk alongside women and whānau navigating the impacts of family violence. At the same time, we are deeply committed to creating change before harm occurs; through education, community awareness, and early intervention.

Enjoy a beautiful evening featuring the auction of a range of experiences and curated art, with contributions from generous businesses and talented local artists that reflect the richness and spirit of our region.

All funds raised will support Women’s Support Motueka to continue providing free, confidential services; including advocacy, counselling, and support for healing, while also growing our prevention efforts such as education workshops, and our youth outreach campaign focused on building healthy relationships from an early age.

This is more than a night out. It is an opportunity to stand alongside our community, and to be part of creating lasting change.

events.long_description:
Happy Mondays // Wellington // Celebrating 35 years of Pills 'n' Thrills & Bellyaches
𝑫𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒓𝒐𝒚 𝑨𝒍𝒍 𝑳𝒊𝒏𝒆𝒔 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑺𝑩𝑴 𝑷𝒓𝒆𝒔𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒔𝒆𝒏𝒕
𝐇𝐀𝐏𝐏𝐘 𝐌𝐎𝐍𝐃𝐀𝐘𝐒
𝐂𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐛𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝟑𝟓 𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐬 𝐨𝐟 "𝐏𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐬 '𝐧' 𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐲𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬

Sᴀᴛᴜʀᴅᴀʏ, 12ᴛʜ Sᴇᴘᴛᴇᴍʙᴇʀ 2026
Mᴇᴏᴡ Nᴜɪ, Wᴇʟʟɪɴɢᴛᴏɴ

⏰ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐢𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐭𝐬:
DAL Presale: Wed 28 Jan @ 9AM 𝑳𝑶𝑪𝑨𝑳
𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧 𝐮𝐩: 𝐃𝐀𝐋 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞 ➟ https://daltours.cc/HappyMondays
General On Sale: Fri 30 Jan @ 9AM 𝑳𝑶𝑪𝑨𝑳

Pioneers of the iconic Madchester sound, the 𝐇𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐲 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 are heading back to Australia and New Zealand to celebrate the 35th anniversary of their seminal album, 𝑃𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 '𝑛' 𝑇ℎ𝑟𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝐵𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑦𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠.

Fusing funk, rock, psychedelia, and house with the pulsating energy of the UK’s burgeoning rave scene, the 𝐇𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐲 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 became the face of a cultural revolution. Their 1990 release, 𝑃𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 '𝑛' 𝑇ℎ𝑟𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝐵𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑦𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠, catapulted them into the mainstream, spending over six months on the UK Albums Chart and earning its place as one of the defining records of the decade.

Fronted by the inimitable 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐮𝐧 𝐑𝐲𝐝𝐞𝐫, with 𝐁𝐞𝐳 ( freaky dancing and percussion), 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤 𝐃𝐚𝐲 (guitar), 𝐆𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐧 (drums), 𝐌𝐢𝐤𝐞𝐲 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞 (bass) 𝐃𝐚𝐧 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐝 (musical director/guitar/keys), and 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐳𝐞𝐡 𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐲 (backing vocals), the band will perform highlights from the classic album; including anthems like 𝑆𝑡𝑒𝑝 𝑂𝑛, 𝐾𝑖𝑛𝑘𝑦 𝐴𝑓𝑟𝑜, and 𝐿𝑜𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝐹𝑖𝑡, alongside fan favourites such as 24 𝐻𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑦 𝑃𝑒𝑜𝑝𝑙𝑒, 𝐻𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑙𝑢𝑗𝑎ℎ, 𝐽𝑢𝑑𝑔𝑒 𝐹𝑢𝑑𝑔𝑒, and 𝑊.𝐹.𝐿.

Their enduring influence on British music was formally recognised in 2016 when they received the prestigious 𝐈𝐯𝐨𝐫 𝐍𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐨 𝐈𝐧𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝, a testament to their legacy as one of the UK’s most beloved and groundbreaking bands.

‘Always a great buzz when we play Australia and New Zealand . Looking forward to bringing the Happy Mondays Pills ‘n’ Thrills party there in September’’ - 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐮𝐧 𝐑𝐲𝐝𝐞𝐫

This isn’t just a tour, it’s a full-throttle revival of Madchester chaos, and the year's wildest party is coming.

‘’Funky dancing, maraca shaking, and incredible vocal performances Happy Mondays showed why they were so big in the 90s and have been able to keep that special place in the hearts of the fans for so long.’’ – 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐍𝐞𝐰𝐬 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐡𝐥𝐲

‘’With Bez and Ryder’s between song banter raising the amusement stakes, the promised Hallelujah was given an airing and its iconic sounds had the crowd bouncing and swaying, it was clear that the Monday’s have lost none of their magic. They are still funky, downright vulgar but so endearing.’’ – 𝐔𝐊 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐢𝐞𝐰𝐬

‘’The show was packed with anthems. Friday night's headline set from the Happy Mondays provided a wonderful dose of nostalgia from one of Manchester's most iconic outfits.’’ – 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐍𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐄𝐜𝐡𝐨

events.venue: Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush, 160 Wilton Road, Wilton, Wellington
events.long_description:
Take a guided night tour through Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush and discover some of the fascinating night-time residents on your way to see the titiwai/glowworms. Enjoy the tranquil beauty of the bush after dark and witness the magical glow of these unique creatures.

This outdoor night-time tour takes just over an hour.
The tour requires a moderate level of fitness; the route includes numerous steps and a steep incline to and from the glowworms.
No dogs, and not suitable for babies and young children.

Meet at the Ōtari Visitors Centre, 150 Wilton Road. Wrap up in warm clothes, wear sturdy walking shoes, and bring a torch or head lamp.

Glow Worm Tour Ticket Refund Policy:
• No Refunds: We do not offer refunds for Glow Worm Tour tickets.
• Ticket Transfers: If you can’t attend your booked tour, with 2 weeks notice we can put you on a future tour, subject to availability.
• Weather Conditions: Tours operate rain or shine. In the event of extreme weather or unsafe conditions, we will reschedule your tour or provide a refund.

For any changes or enquiries, please get in touch with us in advance at Treehouse@wcc.govt.nz or call 04 499 1400.

This tour is operated by the Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush Trust. Join the Trust from only $20 a year and the glow worm tour is free, plus you’ll be supporting the amazing work the Trust does. Join today at owbt.nz/membership-donations/

events.long_description:
As Bambas Do Samba
The Undercurrent presents As Bambas Do Samba!

Vem sambar! Get ready to sing, dance and samba your way through an afternoon of infectious Brazilian grooves.

This vibrant all-female collective brings the joyful sounds of samba and samba rock to Wellington, with an upbeat, irresistible set that’s guaranteed to get toes tapping and bodies moving. Featuring Fabiola and Kitty on vocals and guitar, Adrianna on cavaquinho, Sandra on pandeiro, Geeta on tamborim, Jeanette on flute and tantan, and Sonya on trombone, the group creates a rich, rhythmic sound full of Brazilian swing.

Their repertoire celebrates the music of mulheres brasileiras — Brazilian female artists — while also exploring a wider selection of classic and contemporary samba and samba rock. Expect muita alegria, infectious rhythms, beautiful melodies and plenty of opportunities to join in.

Whether you already love Brazilian music or are discovering it for the first time, todo mundo é bem-vindo! Families, friends and samba lovers alike — come ready to cantar, dançar e se divertir!

Following a hugely popular performance at CubaDupa earlier this year, the group is bringing that same energy to The Undercurrent.

Vem com a família, traga seus amigos e deixe o ritmo levar você! - Come with the family, bring your friends, and let the rhythm carry you!

Samba, música, alegria — até lá!

Saturday September 12
Doors 2:30pm
Music 3pm
$10 (Free entry for children)

Tickets available online and at the door!
https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/gig/104103/As-Bambas-Do-Samba.utr

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆

Spring for Kaibosh - musical fundraiser
DJs, dancing and doing good.

Dress up, get down to Moon and boogie all night while helping Kaibosh feed those in our communities that need it most.

Don’t miss this fantastic fundraiser with stellar DJs spinning all night, lights and visuals from the legendary Cubeman and Metrokorg, and sweet sounds from Torque Sounds.

House, breaks, tech house, techno, rave, bass music and more, with good times guaranteed.

Raffle, plus spot prizes for the best dressed (costume theme: spring!).

All proceeds from ticket sales and raffle go straight to Kaibosh Food Rescue. If you can’t make it, you can donate or become a supporter via the Kaibosh website. https://kaibosh.org.nz/get-involved/donate/

Early bird special and reduced ticket price for the unwaged.

Under 18s must be accompanied by their legal guardian.

DJs

Flatmate
Dance Therapy record label head Flatmate (aka your Flatmate) has a playful curiosity for music, a passion for storytelling and an infectious energy whether behind the decks, in the studio or on the dancefloor. He builds worlds rich in story and sonic diversity, capturing the warmth of the past while exploring the progressive endeavours of the present. (@flatmate__ and @dancetherapyrecords on Insta)

Nam Chucks b2B Amira
Nam and Amira possess a deep appreciation and respect for Soundsystem philosophy, dedicating their musical selections to the concepts of unity, inclusivity and respect for all sounds sacred and indigenous. Join these two empowered wāhine through sounds of their diaspora. (@nam_chucks on Insta)

Hexadecimal Emerging from the UK underground breakbeat scene in the early 2000s, Scott Reeder quickly established himself as an internationally respected DJ and producer. With 150+ releases to his name and two albums on Distinctive Records, his output has helped shape a generation of forward-thinking club music.
Now based in New Zealand, Hexadecimal remains highly active, delivering genre-blending, dancefloor-driven DJ sets that reflect both his deep roots and global perspective. (@hexadecimalmusic on Insta)

Ché D
Ngāmotu New Plymouth–based visual artist and musician/producer Ché Rogers, aka DJ Ché D, weaves stylish minimal house and techno tunes. Shaken, not stirred, he blends underground classics, originals, and live-improvised remixes with a serving of indie and goth condiments. (@che_rogers_art on Insta)

Lowli
Event co-organiser Laurie and his DJ sets are, in a word: FUN! He’s guaranteed to get carried away and bring anyone, and everyone, on the dancefloor with him. (@lowli_dj on Insta)

The Village Idiot
Longtime Kaibosh supporter, Lee Slater, has been hogging house-party stereos, and sound systems, for over 20 years. Expect flowing, bouncy tunes and a little bit of wonkiness.

DJ Danger

Cubeman

If you’re not familiar with his ‘work’ prepare to have your minds blown! (@vjcubeman on Insta)

His VJing, custom projection mapping and immersive mood lighting have helped craft hypnotic visual environments for major festivals and events including Bloom, CubaDupa, Sunny Side Up and numerous Kāpiti gigs. (@metrokorg on Insta)

We’re stoked that this epic event will be POWERED BY TORQUE – Pōneke’s brilliant, custom-built Tub’s Audio sound system. (@torque_sounds on Insta)
