events.long_description:
The Broken Heartbreakers with Eigenface
*Just announced, Eigenface will be joining in support at the Vogelhorn Bowling Club show!*

Ōtepoti’s longstanding indie folk favourites The Broken Heartbreakers have emerged from the mists to announce their brand new album, as well as a full nationwide tour this September. Imagine If We Could Just Keep Driving marks the band’s fifth album and debut on Nadia Reid’s boutique Slow Time Records label, set to be unveiled on July 17th.

FULL BAND ALBUM RELEASE TOUR - SEPTEMBER 2026
FRI 4 SEPT - GRAINSTORE GALLERY, OAMARU
SAT 5 SEPT - SPACE ACADEMY, CHRISTCHURCH
THURS 10 SEPT - WHAMMY, AUCKLAND
FRI 11 SEPT - ARTWORKS THEATRE, WAIHEKE
SAT 12 SEPT - VOGELMORN BOWLING CLUB, WELLINGTON
SAT 19 SEPT - HANOVER HALL, DUNEDIN

With the ballad of The Broken Heartbreakers harking back all the way to 2002, it’s clear that the band understand that the finer things in life take time. Their critically adored album How We Got To Now arrived over a decade ago in 2015, with a smattering of non-album singles and live appearances over the years keeping the band in the hearts and minds of their ever-loyal fanbase.

“Rachel and John are such gifted writers, observers, singers, and players,” says Slow Time Records founder Nadia Reid. “These songs are the stuff of life – life on life’s terms. They sound like Dunedin, and Ireland, like K’Road. I’m so grateful that this record is joining Slow Time’s stable of records.”

Music critic Graham Reid once described the band as having “a sound which draws equally on the Left Banke, the Everly Brothers, Brian Wilson, Beatles, alt-country harmonies and the Anglofolk tradition”. The Broken Heartbreakers’ music mixes the bleak with the beautiful, drawing on deep roots of folk and classic pop melody, but with a defiant, subversive twist and more than a touch of modern electricity.

Howell and Bailey’s new songs find them more defiant than ever, proudly redefining what a band known for having a wistful folky element can or should represent. Whilst The Broken Heartbreakers certainly enjoy plumbing “the broken hearted depths of personal despair and loss”, they also gleefully admit that their songs exist to take “well aimed barbs at the socioeconomic wasteland of the neoliberal era”.

To hear The Broken Heartbreakers on record is a special thing indeed, but to witness them live with a full band is a rare pleasure. This September, fans can hear these very special songs live in all their glory, with six shows spanning the motu. As well as the band’s core pair, the full touring band will feature drummer Paul McLennan-Kissel (who also performed powerfully and beautifully on the record), Ayumu Kobayashi on bass, and a mystery figure on keys and synths.

Don’t miss catching The Broken Heartbreakers on the Imagine If We Could Just Keep Driving album release tour; these magnificent stars may not align again for some time.

“beautiful, world-class music” - Victor Billot, Audioculture

events.long_description:
XCOMMUNICATE
The formidable powerhouse duo COMMUNICATE are bringing their clubnight, XCOMMUNICATE, back to Cuba St Tavern in September.

Known for their long sets that incorporate decades of sound, Cyril Orson and Heylady have been punishing dance floors across Aotearoa since they joined forces almost 4 years ago. Since the last XCOMMUNICATE at the Tavern in November, they have launched their label, XCOMMUNICATE RECORDS, with two EPs now out in the wild and more time being spent in the studio writing new music and collaborating with other NZ artists, the project is proving to e a success. They've played sets at R&A, Electric Avenue, CubaDupa, Arkadien, The Mothership and more. With no plans to stop this train any time soon, they are pulling up at Cuba St Tavern on September 12 for another journey through sound

Usually XCOMMUNICATE is a six hour adventure through decades and sonic realms, however as Heylady is still recovering from burnout they’ve roped in two of their good friends, both amazingly talented; Jen Kyle and Hape, to join them.

Jen Kyle grew up on a steady diet of killer music in Scotland. Exposed to the gritty, raw nightlife Glasgow had to offer, she developed a taste for quality sound across genres. You’re just as likely to hear acid lines as you are dope disco, organized and honed into a melting pot of goodness by a critically good ear.

Hape has been rolling dancefoors since the late 90s. He's played sets around the country and had residencies at some of Auckland and Wellington's most well known establishments. Known for his soulful, energetic sound, layered with hints of progressive and always a cheeky vocal, a Hape set never fails to make you dance.

On top of all this, we'll have a lushed-out environment with added lighting care of the amazing Lighterxx.

We recommend arriving early so you don't miss any of the show.

IMPORTANT INFO:

Our event is a safe space for all. If you or someone you know is feeling unsafe or harassed, please approach one of the DJs or bar staff. If you are behaving badly and impacting others ability to have a good time safely, you will be removed. Please act with respect and care for your fellow attendees at all times, no means no and this goes for conversations as well as more intimate requests.

events.long_description:
Manawa: AHIAHI
Haere mai e te whānau to our debut gig for Manawa: AHIAHI.

Ahiahi, the shift from sun into evening, is a time for us to gather and kanikani the night away, celebrating the birth of our collective and the community that is at the heart of it.

Join us for a night with the artists at the core of Manawa, taking you all on a journey to the inner morning:

Queenie
Clydesdale
Releaf
__________

Manawa is a collective based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Aotearoa that celebrates the creativity, community, and diversity within underground electronic music.

In te reo Māori, Manawa refers to pulse, heart, breath and patience. It is the emotional, spiritual and physical centre of a person, where aroha is held and expressed.

We open the space as a collective to focus on a shared experience through dance and rhythm, shaping the energy in the room and our relationship with one another.

We aim to remove walls between genres and people, curating journeys that evoke curiosity, self-expression and connection on the dance floor, while exploring the never ending depths of underground music.

Design by Chelsea Parker

STRUNG OUT (USA) RETURN FOR FULL-BLOWN NZ TOUR —PERFORMING
SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES IN FULL

Tickets Available now!
https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/.../33281/Strung-Out-USA.utr

Strung Out tore through NZ in 2023, and you lapped it up. You loved them, and they loved
you—so much so that they’re returning this September for a full-blown New Zealand tour, hitting
four locations across both the North and South Island.

And this time, they’re bringing something special.

To celebrate the 30th Anniversary of SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES, Strung Out
will be playing the album in its entirety.

One of punk’s holy grails, it’s fast, ferocious, and
precise—a record that helped define the genre and influenced generations of bands that
followed.

Released in 1996, SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES pushed the boundaries of the
genre—faster, sharper, and more intricate than anything that came before. Three decades on, it
still hits hard, and hearing it played live, front to back, is an experience no self-respecting punk
fan can miss.

Hailing from Simi Valley, California, Strung Out are long-standing punk rock royalty and one of
Fat Wreck Chords’ defining “big four.” With decades of touring under their belts, they have a
proven track record of igniting crowds and delivering high-octane, full-throttle punk shows.

Expect a night of relentless energy: razor-sharp riffs, pounding drums, and shout-along
choruses delivered with force.

This is controlled chaos at its best: sweat-soaked rooms, ringing
ears, and intensity that pulls you right in.

Last time Strung Out were here, shows sold out. This run will be no different.

Don’t sleep on it, or you’ll miss it.

Friday September 11th, 2026 — Last Place — Hamilton
Saturday September 12th, 2026 — Whammy Bar — Auckland
Sunday September 13th, 2026 — Valhalla — Wellington
Monday September 14th, 2026 — Loons — Christchurch

events.long_description:
The Daffodil Express
All aboard for one of Steam Incorporated’s most popular events of the year!

Join us on our annual Daffodil Express — a special heritage train journey to Carterton’s much‑loved Daffodil Festival in the heart of the Wairarapa.

Travel in vintage style behind our beautifully restored locomotives and carriages, with convenient boarding available at Wellington, Petone, Waterloo and Upper Hutt.

Sit back and enjoy the journey as we leave the city behind, race through the Hutt Valley suburbs, head through to the Wairarapa — including the famous 8.8km tunnel, one of the longest on New Zealand’s passenger network.

Once in Carterton, you’ll have time to explore everything the festival has to offer, including stunning daffodil fields at Middle Run Farm, bustling street markets and artisan stalls, live music and entertainment, food, crafts, and family-friendly fun.

After a relaxing few hours, simply hop back onboard for the return journey — no traffic, no parking hassles — just a great day out by rail.

🎟️ This excursion is extremely popular and sells out every year, so early booking is essential.

Make it a day to remember — gather your friends and family and experience this iconic Wairarapa tradition the best way possible: with Steam Incorporated.

Natural Textured Rings - Spring Taster - Wellington!
Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Workshop fee is $165, Early bird pricing $148 (ends 17 August).

Finding Ground in an Uncertain World; Ancient Wisdom for Modern Turbulence




The world feels increasingly chaotic—from economic pressure to global political shifts and an unpredictable future. When external conditions are completely out of our hands, how do we keep from feeling overwhelmed?
This interactive workshop bridges contemporary psychology with timeless philosophy from the Bhagavad Gita to help us build unshakeable internal resilience and stay anchored in times of uncertainty. We’ll look at the big picture, unpack what it means to live with the unknown, and share practical tools to maintain clarity amidst the noise.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.

Meet your host Sivananda

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

events.long_description:
"Ash rule. They are geniuses. Gods maybe."- NME
Ireland’s favourite power pop trio, Ash, finally return to Australia and New Zealand to Celebrate the 30th Anniversary of their iconic debut album, ‘1977’, by performing the album in full. Released in 1996, the album’s title references both the decade the band members were born in and the year Star Wars first hit cinemas.
‘1977’ has sold more than 2 million copies worldwide and was written, recorded and released when most of Ash were still only 19. A cinematic punk-pop soundtrack to binge drinking, chasing girls, youth and frustrated adolescent idealism, the album fused power pop, glam rock, post-grunge and Britpop into a loud, melodic and exuberant sound.
It struck a chord with the hearts, minds and hormones of a generation of like-minded teens, delivering a run of singles including “Girl From Mars”, “Kung Fu”, “Angel Interceptor”, “Goldfinger” and “Oh Yeah” — all of which reached the UK Top 20 and helped cement Ash’s reputation.
The 30th Anniversary Celebration of ‘1977’ will give Ash fans the chance to relive the album that featured “hit after honey-topped hit” and Britpop ruled the airwaves. Oh yeah!

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

Pasifika Business Fono 2026 🌺

Your business. Your voice. Our future.




Calling all Pasifika in business across the Wellington region!




Whether you’re running an established business, building your first start-up, growing a side hustle, or simply thinking about starting your business journey, we want you in the room.

The Wellington Pasifika Business Network (WPBN) is bringing Pasifika business owners, entrepreneurs, start-ups, and aspiring business owners together for a special Pasifika Business Fono.

This is an opportunity to come together, connect, share your experiences, and have your say on what Pasifika businesses across our region need to thrive.




Help shape the future of WPBN

WPBN is entering an exciting new phase, and we want to hear directly from our Pasifika business community about what matters most to you.

What support do you need?
What opportunities are you looking for?
What are the barriers you're facing?
What would make a real difference to your business?




Your voice will help us shape our next network strategy and future programmes, events, and business support so that WPBN can deliver what our Pasifika business community needs.

This isn't a formal presentation where you sit and listen, it's a fono. A chance to Talanoa, connect, share ideas and build relationships with other Pasifika people on their business journey.




Meet the WPBN Board

Come along and meet members of the Wellington Pasifika Business Network Board, find out more about who we are and what we do, and learn about the support, connections, opportunities and benefits available to you through WPBN membership.




Whether you're already a member or have never connected with WPBN before, you are welcome.

Talanoa and meaningful conversation

Overview

The world wants minerals, but scientists around Aotearoa are working on what we could make instead.

The MacDiarmid Institute is a network of leading researchers from around the country united in a common goal: to create and explore innovative, sustainable materials that will improve the lives of people in Aotearoa New Zealand and around the word. This talk will focus on critical minerals - raw materials that are essential to many existing and future technologies and have been making headlines in recent times due to increasing supply chain vulnerabilities. In this talk we will present materials science solutions that are being developed and utilised right now, in Aotearoa New Zealand, to recycle, replace or reduce our need for critical minerals.

Speakers:
Professor Chris Bumby, Principal Investigator with the MacDiarmid Institute and Chief Scientist at Paihau - Robinson Research Institute

Professor Nicola Gaston, Principal Investigator and Director at the MacDiarmid Institute and Professor in Physics at the University of Auckland

Introduction to Business Analysis
Get a pragmatic introduction to key business analysis concepts and the business analyst role, and apply what you learn.

About this Event


Description

This course provides a pragmatic introduction to key business analysis concepts and the business analyst role. It includes a number of hands-on exercises to apply what you learn. It is targeted at those who are new to Business Analyst roles or considering moving into this profession. The course is also highly suitable to subject matter experts, business representatives, and project roles that involve business analysis activities.

Business analysis is a broad and exciting profession and skill set. Your role is to understand businesses, their needs and their problems and then help assess and validate solutions to fulfil these needs or solve these problems. In the process you will be involved in a wide range of activities including analysis, requirements management, communication, solution assessment and validation, and planning.

The ‘Introduction to Business Analysis’ course is delivered by seasoned business analysis practitioner consultants who undertake business analysis activities on a daily basis.

events.name: SHRED FEST - FEAT OBSCURA (GER), FVKVSHIMA & GUESTS, WELLINGTON
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Tickets here

SHRED FEST 2026 is coming! The renowned travelling metal festival will storm across New Zealand, delivering an unmatched celebration of technical excellence, intensity, and musical precision.

This year’s New Zealand edition features two of the most acclaimed names in modern extreme metal Obscura (GER) & Fvkvshima (NZ)

OBSCURA (GER) – Progressive death metal pioneers and masters of technical virtuosity. Following two successful Australian tours along with a return to New Zealand, OBSCURA is back to present their latest album A Sonication as part of their ongoing world tour.

Joining the international lineup are one of New Zealands most formidable local acts:

FVKVSHIMA - A progressive, driving, mechanical powerhouse surfacing from the shores of Wellington, NZ. Gargantuan, lurching drop-tuned phrases, layered with soaring apocalyptic textures. Resurrecting members from Shakahn, Backyard Burial, Planet of the Dead, and Diecast, FVKVSHIMA has collective decades of songwriting experience across a variety of genres, now condensed into its menacing live set.

Additional guests will appear in every city on this tour

Line Up
OBSCURA (GER)
FVKVSHIMA (NZ)
+ Special Guests

Dates
15/09 NZ Auckland – Whammy
16/09 NZ Wellington – Valhalla
17/09 NZ Christchurch – Churchills Tavern

SHRED FEST 2026 promises a diverse and uncompromising showcase of extreme metal — from technical precision to devastating heaviness. Expect the ultimate convergence of musicianship, passion, and power.

Tickets on sale via www.yourmatebookings.com & https://www.shredfest.net/

Obscura shared their thoughts on the upcoming tour:
"We're thrilled to bring Shred Fest to Australia in 2026 alongside the crushing talents of Fallujah, Anoxia, and Ashen. It’s been a long time coming, and we're ready to deliver a relentless set for our fans down under. No VIP packages — every band will be at the venue to meet you, talk music, and celebrate the most extreme sounds around. Come early, stay late, and support every act. We can’t wait to see you all there."

Official SHRED FEST channels;

Website: https://www.shredfest.net/
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61569365417641 / https://www.facebook.com/shredfestausnz / https://www.facebook.com/yourmatebookings
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/shredfest_moreisnotenough / https://www.instagram.com/shredfestausnz/
Tiktok: @shredfest_world
YouTube: youtube.com/@SHREDFEST_MOREISNOTENOUGH

All Interviews and Press Enquiries; please get in touch with Anthony ab@yourmatebookings.com

events.long_description:
The World of WearableArt (WOW) Show is an internationally acclaimed annual event. Held every spring, WOW is New Zealand’s largest arena spectacle. This not-to-be-missed event features an electrifying combination of live music, cirque, dance and dazzling wearable art.
This year, the inspiration for WOW is GLO! It will see imagination run riot across six sections of pure, unfiltered, high-voltage entertainment. Expect live music, aerialists, dance, and of course, dazzling wearable art. Those six sections correspond with the competition categories at the heart of WOW. As the world’s premier wearable art competition, every garment on stage is a finalist. They are selected for imaginative storytelling and execution excellence. The competition offers a global platform for artists and designers and the chance to win over NZD$200,000 in prizes.

events.long_description:
Overview

Join us for Blue September | Lunch for a Cause - good vibes, great food, all for a meaningful mission!

Good Food. Great Company. Supporting Men's Health.




This September, we're proud to be supporting Blue September—a nationwide campaign raising awareness and funds for men's health across New Zealand.

Join us for a relaxed community lunch where great food, meaningful conversations and connection come together for an important cause.

Whether you're a long-time Q Space member, a local business owner, working remotely or simply curious about coworking, we'd love to welcome you.

Take a break from your workday, meet fellow professionals and enjoy lunch in a friendly, welcoming environment while helping shine a light on an important issue affecting thousands of Kiwi men and their families.

Everyone is welcome.




What's Included

🍽 Complimentary community lunch

☕ Unlimited tea, coffee & hot chocolate

🤝 Casual networking with local professionals

💙 Support for Blue September and men's health awareness

🏢 Optional guided tour of Q Space




Wear Blue!

Help us show our support by wearing something blue on the day.

Whether it's a shirt, scarf, tie, jacket or even just your favourite blue socks, every splash of blue helps raise awareness and creates a fantastic community atmosphere




About Blue September

Blue September is the Prostate Cancer Foundation New Zealand's annual awareness and fundraising campaign, encouraging New Zealanders to start conversations about men's health and support life-changing research, education and support services.

By coming together as a community, we can help raise awareness while supporting an incredibly worthwhile cause.

Learn more at www.blueseptember.org.nz




Why Q Space?

Located in the heart of Lower Hutt, Q Space is more than just a place to work.

We're home to a vibrant community of businesses, freelancers, entrepreneurs and remote workers who believe that great work happens when people connect.

From flexible coworking memberships and dedicated desks to private office suites and premium meeting rooms, Q Space offers modern workspaces designed to help businesses thrive.

If you've never visited before, this event is the perfect opportunity to experience our community in a relaxed, no-pressure environment.

Read less

Overview

The Outlook for New Zealand Growth, Inflation, and Interest Rates with Satish Ranchhod

New Zealand households and businesses continue to navigate a complex economic environment shaped by persistent inflationary pressures, evolving interest rate settings, and an increasingly uncertain global backdrop. With the upcoming election also influencing the business landscape, understanding the forces driving economic change has never been more important.

Join Westpac Senior Economist Satish Ranchhod for an insightful briefing on the key trends shaping Wellington's economy and the wider New Zealand outlook over the year ahead.

Key topics include:

• Interest rates and monetary policy outlook

• Inflation trends and global economic influences

• House price movements and property market insights

• Economic implications of the evolving policy and electoral environment

Whether you are planning for business growth, managing investment decisions, or seeking to better understand the economic environment ahead, this session will provide valuable insights and practical context to support informed decision-making.

Event details:

12:00pm - Networking
12:15pm – Presentation
1:15pm – Wrap-up

Chamber members and Westpac customers: Free entry
Non-members: $10.00 donated to Life Flight Trust through the Westpac Chopper Appeal.

Hosted at the Westpac Building, Wellington
(Level 10, 1 Victoria Street, Wellington)

Empower Her, female networking group that offers a welcoming and safe environment for women of all business backgrounds and experiences

Monthly Topic: Focus, Flow and Productivity

Hosted by: Vidya Kurella

Running a business can often feel like juggling a hundred priorities at once. This month's networking session is all about creating more focus, finding your flow, and working in a way that feels productive without leading to burnout. Together we will share practical strategies, tools and ideas to help you minimise distractions, stay accountable, prioritise what matters most, and build a business that works with you, not against you. Leave with fresh inspiration and simple actions you can put into practice straight away.

Want to get your ticket for FREE?

Are you a woman in business looking for a supportive community to help you connect, grow, and learn?

As an Inner Circle member, you can attend as many of our networking hubs as you like for FREE! This includes our hubs across Auckland, NZ, Australia and the UK. Enjoy unlimited access to our netwokring events and take full advantage of the community and networking opportunities.

Join the Inner Circle

Join the Inner Circle to unlock even more benefits:

Monthly Masterclasses: Learn from industry experts on topics that will elevate your business and mindset.

Accountability Calls: Stay on track with our supportive community and achieve your goals.

In celebration of WOW in Wellington, meet our costume artisans and discover how legendary characters begin at the hobby bench and leap to the screen, stitch by stitch.

Meet our makers! At our exclusive events, step into our cinema in the heart of Wētā Workshop, as two of our costume technicians reveal how a hobby grew into a career and how the skills behind blockbuster films can begin at your own kitchen table.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Bench Music and TEG Touring
Few figures have shaped the sound and spirit of house music like Timmy Regisford.
From New York's legendary WBLS radio station to executive A&R roles at Atlantic, MCA, Motown and DreamWorks Records, Regisford has spent more than four decades helping define dance music from both behind the scenes and behind the decks.
As founder and resident of the iconic Club Shelter, Timmy created one of dance music's most influential institutions - a sanctuary built on soulful house, disco, Afro rhythms, jazz, gospel and community that continues to inspire DJs and dancers around the world.
Known for marathon sets that unfold over many hours, Timmy's performances are journeys through rhythm, emotion and timeless music rather than peak-time moments. His influence stretches across generations, remaining just as essential to young selectors discovering the roots of house as it is to those who experienced New York's golden era firsthand.

events.long_description:
O'Flynn | Wellington
WELLINGTON! O’Flynn makes his long-awaited New Zealand debut this September, arriving with a new album that captures him at a defining moment. 🌴

TICKET INFORMATION:
Pre-Sale Live: Wednesday 8th July, 10 am (NZT)
General On Sale: Thursday 9th July 10 am (NZT)

THESE TICKETS WILL GO FAST! GET IN EARLY, SIGN UP FOR PRE-SALE NOW.

Meow
Thursday 17th September | 8:00 pm - 12:00 am
Support from: Beccie B, Rydr

For over a decade, O’Flynn has quietly become one of the UK’s most respected producers and DJs, a singular voice in contemporary electronic music, grounded in dexterous production and an instinctive feel for the underground. His catalogue runs deep, shaped by curiosity, and marked by collaborations with artists such as Bonobo and Barry Can’t Swim.

Releasing music across Ninja Tune, Blip Discs, and his own imprint Hundred Flowers, O’Flynn’s work has earned support from tastemakers including Four Tet, Ben UFO, Gilles Peterson, and James Blake.

A pivotal moment came via Bonobo’s Fabric mix, which led to the collaborative track Otomo, a quietly monumental piece, and later saw O’Flynn join Bonobo on tour. Around the same time, he released Shimmer, a collaborative album with Frazer Ray via Ninja Tune’s Technicolour imprint, praised by DJ Mag as “a perfect cocktail of soaring emotions and bottom-heavy bass.”

Live, O’Flynn completed a five-week sold-out residency at London’s Phonox, followed by a sold-out headline show at KOKO, marking a clear step up in scale and demand.

In 2023, O’Flynn became a resident on Rinse FM, further cementing his role as both curator and craftsman. More recently, he delivered the inaugural release on Barry Can’t Swim’s Earth’s Only Paradise label, two tracks that stretched from disco-lit dancefloors to sharp-edged club pressure.

Now, O’Flynn returns with Kairos, his third full-length album, released July 17 via his own Panthus label. Named for the ancient Greek concept of the decisive moment, when conditions align, Kairos feels exactly that: a record where club energy meets patience, detail, and atmosphere. Music built for immersion.

This debut NZ tour marks the arrival of an artist fully in his stride, backed by an album rich in colour, tone, and intent.

events.long_description:
The Hunt for the Canterbury Panther
You’re formally invited to the Shirley-East Cryptozoological Convention — where Aotearoa’s monster hunters gather to share their research into creatures beyond the realm of “modern science”. Rumour has it Naomi Coleridge has caught the Canterbury Panther… but is it real? And what’s that growling coming from the side of the stage?

Grab your tinfoil hat and join Naomi as she faces the trials and tribulations of Aotearoa NZ’s outdoors in pursuit of something greater. Heartfelt, cringey, and very silly, this play explores achievement, family expectations, and self-realisation, with a strong connection to our natural environment.

Best suited for rangatahi aged 10-14 and their families. Contains flashing lights.

Co-writer, Producer and Performer: Anna Barker

events.long_description:
The Bay Express to the Hastings Blossom Festival
Welcome spring in style and climb aboard The Bay Express for a magnificent full-day rail adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for the spectacular Hastings Blossom Festival!

Sit back and relax as our majestic steam locomotive takes you through changing landscapes, winding its way toward the sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the sights and sounds of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, hearing the thunderous echo of the engine, and catching the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. You can purchase a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, hot espresso coffees, and sweet treats right from your seat as the scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight into the heart of the action. The train will be stopping right in the middle of Hastings, putting you directly in the center of the festival. Upon arrival, you'll step off the train and straight into the vibrant celebrations of the annual Hastings Blossom Festival. Enjoy a fantastic afternoon exploring the famous public parade, live entertainment, market stalls, and beautiful spring blooms. It’s a proud local tradition celebrating the region's rich orchard heritage, and you are perfectly positioned to enjoy it all at your leisure before our return journey home.

What's Included
Your ticket covers your return journey to Hastings in beautifully maintained premium carriages alongside unrestricted access to the open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography. You will also have full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling refreshments, espresso coffees, and snacks. Best of all, you get direct arrival right into the heart of Hastings for the Blossom Festival celebrations with plenty of time to enjoy the festival parade, markets, and entertainment.

Plimmerton depart – 5:25am

Levin depart – 7:00am
Palmerston North depart – 8:10am

Evening Travel – Return Journey

Palmerston North depart – 7:50pm

Ōtaki depart – 9:15pm
Paraparaumu depart – 9:45pm

Space in these premium carriages is strictly limited, so secure your tickets today for a classic spring day out on the rails!

events.long_description:
Debt Club - Foothold Release Tour W/ First Reserve & Dillon Jo - Live @ San Fran
Following the release of their recent single, “I Do Mine”, Debt Club announce their first Aotearoa nationwide tour. The tour will celebrate the release of their debut album “Foothold” which is out August 12th & available for vinyl pre-order now!

Debt Club are a Pōneke based indie / folk rock six piece who blend jangling indie rock, folk, alt-country and emo into a sound defined by rich arrangements, soaring saxophone melodies, and emotionally direct songwriting. Since forming in 2023, the band has quickly become a notable presence in Aotearoa’s underground music scene through their dynamic live performances and textured, heartfelt songs. Debt Club have shared stages with Marlin's Dreaming, Phoebe Rings and Australia’s Floodlights, while appearing at festivals including Rhythm and Vines, Twisted Frequency, CubaDupa and Newtown Festival. Following the release of their debut EP, “Taste For Stout,” the band recently unveiled “I Do Mine,” the first single from their forthcoming debut album “Foothold,” due out on August 12th.

Joining Debt Club for the Wellington date is First Reserve & Dillon Jo!

First Reserve is inevitable. Before adopting the moniker in 2023, Ryan Connaghan had been prolifically writing music that communicated their experiences in life, love, and loneliness. These themes are all approached on songs like “Last One” and “Me & My Friends” – the first offerings from First Reserve’s debut EP “There’s A God” set for release on November 14th, 2025. Thanks to their exhilarating live performances joined by a four-piece band, First Reserve has amassed a cult of devoted supporters both in their hometown of Te Whanganui-a-Tara and beyond. On stage, their sound is both intimate and larger-than-life, combining influences from alt-rock, indie-folk, and pop. First Reserve has supported visiting internationals Hot Mulligan (US) and Keli Holiday (AUS), and have toured with Kiwi favourites PARK RD, There’s A Tuesday, and Wet Denim.

Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s staple, Dillon Jo, is a queer, female-fronted four-piece band formed at Massey University in Wellington. Describing their sound as “Dreamy Droppy Rock Pop,”. ‘Dillon Jo’ is the project of Wellington Based artists Betty Smith and Georgie Levien, building paths between the elements of dream pop, shoegaze, folk, alt rock, and indie pop to create their genre defying sound. They have discovered vibrant chemistry over the past few months since making quite a stir in Wellington, playing numerous shows including opening for The Rions, Foley, Wet Denim, Hemi Hemingway and Coast Arcade only to name a few. Having heard of each other through the Reality music TV show Take The Mic 2022 which they were both contestants on, they formed Dillon Jo in early 2025. Releasing their first acoustic single ‘It was you (she’s been waiting for)’ in April 2025 and releasing two more singles later in the year, including ‘Shiver’ and ‘Jo’. The band also consists of Kahu Sanson-Burnett, (a multi-talented musician, producer, and previous member of Parallel Park) and Ruadh Munro, (Drums and previous member of Scarlett crush) Dillon Jo has transformed their live sets into an unbridled big-sound shoegaze experience

Alphabethead, Grecco Romank & Special Guests || Meow || Te Whanganui-a-Tara

Please join Alphabethead and Grecco Romank this spring for a thrilling evening of turntablism, brutalist sewer-pop and dirty, chaotic, electronic dance music!

Alphabethead is celebrating the release of Misanthrope, his new animated music video. A collaboration with Dr D Foothead, the video presents a hunk of organic matter lying dormant in a Cronenberg-esque laboratory. As this undulating subject is fed aural and visual stimulation we marvel at its mutation and evolution in real-time...

﻿Alongside their classics, Grecco Romank’s set may feature primordial offerings from their upcoming album ‘The Heels of The Isthmus’ to be released this year and usher in the full reign of the Antichrist.

More about the artists:

ALPHABETHEAD finds himself adrift in the musical cosmos, somewhere between the constellations of Hip Hop, Electronica and Experimental Rock. As a teenager he won the New Zealand DMC DJ Championship and this title sent him performing across the globe. Over the next twenty years he'd go on to make seven albums as Alphabethead, five albums as one third of cult genre-shredders All Seeing Hand and two records as half of the psychedelic Hip Hop duo Bad Taste. He also contributed production or turntable scratching to Home Brew, Death & The Maiden, Tourettes, and The Etymologists. His highly technical and singular approach to playing the turntable as a musical instrument has led to tours through Aotearoa, Australia, UK and China.

Now signed to Sunreturn, Alphabethead's new music is explorative electronica stemming from sound design, synthesis and manipulation of sound on vinyl. His live performances are bouncy, sweaty ordeals where the turntables are pushed to their very limit. An Alphie performance where the needle doesn’t break or fly off the vinyl and completely derailing the dance-floor is considered a miracle...

https://alphabethead.bandcamp.com/
https://www.instagram.com/alphabetheads

﻿GRECCO ROMANK are Tāmaki Makaurau’s premiere purveyors of brutalist sewer-pop: stitching together opera, industrial rave, and gleefully uncommercial chaos. Formed in 2020 their world is one where high art slips in dog shit, crashes head-first into a drum machine, and emerges snarling, sweaty, and weirdly catchy. For this series of shows, Grecco will be joined onstage for vocal duties by fiercely talented and demonically popular Sean Murphy (CCTV, Boxer Priest) and Princess Paradox.

Over their decrepit six year existence Grecco have released a rapid-fire series of albums (Red Tower, Wet Exit, Arts Colony) that have dominated alternative charts, been nominated twice for Best Alternative Artist at the AMA’s, and topping the Student Radio Network’s Top 10 in 2023, all whilst refusing every expectation of commercial sense. Critics have described their music as everything from “luxuriously bogan techno” to “the rave you never want to end up at but always get dragged into.” Their live shows — part rave, part performance art, part deranged group fitness class — are infamous for their intensity.

﻿Collaboration fuels the band: they’ve worked with Princess Chelsea, Our Carlson, Eden Burns, Lawrence Arabia, Dick Move, and dozens more, expanding their sonic universe while keeping their core chaos intact. Their 300-page Arts Colony book, now sold out, extends their world into satire, visual art, and fictional cultural history.

https://greccoromank.bandcamp.com/
https://www.instagram.com/greccoromank

events.long_description:
Overview

Special General Meeting and Annual General Meeting

Hui details

Saturday, 19 September 2026
10.00 am
Omaka Marae
120 Aerodrome Road, Blenheim

The Special General Meeting will begin at 10.00 am. The Annual General Meeting will be held immediately afterwards.

Registration helps us plan for catering and seating.

Special General Meeting

At the Special General Meeting, whānau will be asked to consider proposed amendments to the Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō Trust Deed and the Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō Charitable Trust Deed.

The proposed changes would:

change the Trust’s balance date and income year so future AGMs can be held in February or March, during Raumati
make transitional changes to some Trustee terms
clarify how casual Trustee vacancies are filled
update the Trust Deed to reflect changes to the Māori Fisheries Act 2004

Moving future AGMs to Raumati is intended to make it easier for more whānau to travel home and participate.

Voting on the proposed amendments

Resolutions 1 to 4 will be decided by postal and online voting. Voting closes at 12 noon on Friday, 11 September 2026.

Resolutions 5 and 6, confirming that the proposed amendments are for the collective benefit of Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō, will be decided in person at the Special General Meeting as part of the meeting agenda.

Special General Meeting agenda
Karakia tīmatatanga and welcome
Apologies
Presentation of the proposed Trust Deed amendments
Resolutions 5 and 6 to be decided in person

Nelson, Nelson Region-Event Brite
events.name: Rebellious Words - A poetry zine making workshop
events.venue:
Project 100
Nelson, Nelson Region
events.long_description:
Overview

Your perspective is not a problem to solve. It is material.

A poetry zine is a tiny act of self-publishing: a place for sharp thoughts, soft confessions, beautiful rage, private jokes, inconvenient truths, strange images and the parts of ourselves we are often taught to make smaller.

In this two-hour Guerrilla Poetry workshop, poet and collage artist Rowan Taigel will invite you to cut, write, tear, layer, rearrange, make space for contradiction - and make a handmade poetry zine that refuses to behave like a tidy little craft project.

A zine (pronounced ‘zeen’) is a small handmade place for the thoughts that do not fit neatly into the version of the world we have been handed: beautiful rage and ordinary tenderness; difficult questions and private jokes; grief and glamour; politics and pleasure; softness and refusal.

This is for people who are drawn to art, language, DIY culture and creative expression. For anyone who has ever been called too much, too intense, too sensitive, too political, too imaginative, or simply “extra” - but may need someone to hand them the scissors and say: start here.

Come and make a tiny publication with people who also see the cracks in the story and feel compelled to write in them. Something interesting is bound to happen.

No experience is needed. Bring your curiosity, your opinions, and any feelings that might benefit from becoming art.

Leave with your own handmade poetry zine: clever, strange, beautiful, defiant, or all four.

Part of Beautiful Words at Project 100. All materials provided.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

events.long_description:
Our on-farm Craft Open Days are aimed primarily at knitters, spinners, crocheters and other fibre crafters.

Nestled in the small rural community of Tinui is Rewa Rewa Station. Operating as a hill country Sheep & Beef breeding farm with a strong focus on NZ Wool & Fibre. Romney, Corriedale cross Romney, Polwarth & Gotland sheep provide the fleeces to create fibre products for crafters, which are sold via the Rewa Rewa Station website, and at Fibre Markets. Our Studio Shop is also open during Craft Days or by appointment outside of these days.

Our Craft Days allow you to work on your own project, seek advice, learn a new fibre skill or maybe just spend time with fellow fibre crafters while potentially ticking off a project or two in the process.

Please bring your knitting, crocheting, spinning, hand sewing, or any project you are working on and enjoy a drive in the country!

Coffee, tea and snacks provided, but bring your lunch and stay awhile.

Everyone is welcome, the more the merrier!

Note: Craft Days are primarily held on the 3rd Saturday of every mont,h but occasionally we do have to juggle the dates.

events.long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

I'm so excited to be bringing this workshop for the third time to Nelson this Sept 2026.

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Saturday 19th September - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm


Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.




Where: Broadgreen House, 276 Nayland Road, Stoke, Nelson. 7011. NEW ZEALAND (The Le Cren Room)
When: Saturday 19th September 2026
10:30am - 12:30pm or 2-4pm

events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a Community Seed & Plant Swap, where we gather to share the abundance of our gardens and connect with fellow growers.

We're running a local seed and plant swap right here at the farm, next to the shop. It's a simple kaupapa: bring along any spare seeds or plants you'd like to pass on, pop them on the tables provided, and take home whatever catches your eye. All seeds should be labelled in bags, and plants labelled too so everyone knows what they're getting.

This is a chance to diversify your garden, meet other local growers, and keep the cycle of sharing alive. Whether you're after heritage varieties, curious about something new, or just keen to see what others are growing, you're welcome here.

Mangaroa Farms will have the coffee cart running, and the farm shop will be open if you need to stock up on anything else. Parking will be in a paddock a short walk from the shop.

Remember to bring your own envelopes or bags, labels and a pen to collect any seeds that take your interest.

We will begin at Sat 19th September | 11:00am at 98 Whitemans Valley Road (Garden Tour or Shop). Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape 🍷

Welcome spring in style and step aboard The Trinity Hill Vintage Express for a magnificent, all-inclusive rail and epicurean adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for an exclusive winery experience at one of New Zealand's most prestigious estates.

Sit back and indulge as our majestic steam locomotive sweeps you through changing landscapes, winding its way through the dramatic scenery of the Manawatū Gorge toward sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the romance and grandeur of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, capturing the thunderous echo of the engine, and taking in the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be at your service. You can purchase a range of premium alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, fresh hot coffees, teas, and sweet treats to enjoy right from your seat as the scenery rolls elegantly by.

Our tracks lead straight to Hastings, where a private coach awaits to escort you directly to the legendary Trinity Hill Vineyard in the globally acclaimed Gimblett Gravels district.

This exclusive afternoon centers completely around celebrated viticulture:
- Behind the Cellar Door: Go on an insider's tour to discover their world-class winemaking craft and rich heritage.
- Curated Artisan Lunch: Unwind on the stunning estate grounds with a premium lunch box featuring your choice of a hand-crafted sandwich (such as the bold Beef and Kraut with pickles and cheese, an elegant Chicken and Tarragon, or a vibrant Salad and Hummus with salsa verde).
- Perfect Pairings: Accompanied by a savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, your estate lunch is paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's flagship Hawke's Bay Collection Wine.

Your ticket covers your return rail travel behind a genuine steam locomotive from Kapiti, Horowhenua, or Manawatū, complete with reserved premium carriage seating offering panoramic views. You will have full access to our open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography, alongside entry to our fully licensed café carriage throughout the rail journey. Seamless coach transfers will also be waiting in Hastings to transition you smoothly from rails to vines.

Once at Trinity Hill, you will enjoy an exclusive winery tour exploring Trinity Hill’s history and winemaking craft. To complement the afternoon, you will receive a curated estate lunch box featuring a premium sandwich, savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's premium Hawke's Bay Collection Wine (or a non-alcoholic alternative).

Plimmerton depart – 5:25am

Levin depart – 7:00am
Palmerston North depart – 8:10am

Hastings arrive – 11:55am

On arrival into Hastings, passengers transfer by coach to Trinity Hill Vineyard.

🌸 What to Expect — Sacred Women’s Circle

Welcome, Sister. 🌿
If you feel called to join us, trust that feeling. This is a women-only space created for connection, reflection, healing and genuine sisterhood.

✨ Your Experience

Held by Crystal Mihinui, Reiki Master, Music Therapist, classically trained pianist and Sound Healing Practitioner, the circle combines energy work, music, sound and nature to create a deeply relaxing and nurturing experience.

Our gathering may include:

🌸 Sacred Circle & Oracle Cards — opening the space and connecting with intuition, nature and ancestral wisdom.

🌙 Womb Healing — gentle womb mudras, sacred mantras and feminine energy practices.

🔔 Shamanic Sound Journey — guided meditation, crystal singing bowls and energy healing.

💗 Sisterhood Sharing — a safe space to share, listen and connect without judgement.

🔥 Release Ritual — letting go of what no longer serves you.

🌿 Forest Bathing & Journaling — quiet time to reconnect with yourself and the natural world.

The intention is simple: slow down, soften, connect and leave feeling lighter.

📍 Location

We gather at a beautiful private forest setting surrounded by native trees, birds and mountains.

Meeting details are provided after booking. You can either:

- Meet at our home studio and rideshare together, or
- Meet directly at the outdoor location.

☔ Rain Plan: If the weather isn't suitable, we have a beautiful indoor alternative.

🎒 What to Bring

- A vegetarian dish to share
- Journal & pen
- Comfortable clothing suitable for the forest
- Swimming gear if you'd like to take a dip 🏊‍♀️
- An open heart 💗

🎟️ Tickets & Inclusivity

Children are welcome and children's tickets are half price.

Community Services Card concessions are available — please bring proof of entitlement.

🌸 A Note on Cancellations

As a small, heart-led family business, tickets are non-refundable. If you can't attend, you're very welcome to gift your ticket to another sister.

Come exactly as you are.

events.long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

I'm so excited to be bringing this workshop for the third time to Nelson this Sept 2026.

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Sunday 20th September - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm


Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

10:30am - 12:30pm or 2-4pm

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.
What you will take away: A finished artwork piece A understanding of Kintsugi Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

events.long_description:
Kaiwhakaataata Māra | Garden Performers
SPRING’S SPRITES

Celebrating this 35th year, Shakespeare Globe Centre New Zealand is delighted to bring some of Shakespeare’s most sprightly characters to life to help re-enliven the Wellington City Council’s Botanic Garden ki Paekākā, as it springs back into life after wintering over.

On Sunday 20 September, for an hour or so from 10am and again from 1pm, Pucks, fairies, friends and the odd Bottom will caress your ears with familiar quips and quotes from the Bard’s canon, as you hover to behold the rebirth of plants erupting into bloom.
For half an hour from 11.30am and 2.30pm, the characters combine at the Joy Fountain by the Glenmore Street entrance to present ‘exploded’ versions of their quotes into vignettes of his favourite plays. If you wish to participate, there will be a few roles with cue-scripts available to join the revels and explore the beauty of Shakespeare’s words and magic midst the fresh flowers springing forth.

But wait, there’s….a costume competition, with prizes, for the best Bottom and Puck, presented at the end of the performance. Fun for all!

Join Mangaroa Farms for Somatic Breathwork Journey —  Tue 22nd September | 6:00PM - 7:30PM

Join Amy Webber and Mangaroa Farms for a journey into your breath. Somatic Breathwork™ is a full embodiment experience designed to help you release stress, trauma, emotions and stuck energy from the body. This powerful modality uses your own breath to shed layers that no longer serve you, creating space for meaningful change in your life.

Through consciously connected breathing patterns, you'll tap into your body's innate wisdom to discover areas needing clearing. The immersive musical experience may bring forth cathartic releases—laughing, moving, crying, or shaking—all welcome expressions that help move pent-up energy through your system.

In the second half of our journey, we'll shift to a gentler breathing technique, helping you reconnect with your true self. Together, we'll use the breath to envision how you want to show up in the world, the changes you wish to make, and gain clarity on living your best life.

We will begin at Tue 22nd Sep | 6:00pm at 298 Whitemans Valley Road (Wharekai/Yurt)

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
Overview

Dare to Lead is the ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures, and organisational change.

The ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures and organisational change.




"Highly recommend."
"Inspiring."
"An amazing experience."
"One 'aha moment' after the other."




Founded on the research of Dr. Brené Brown, Dare to Lead™ is an empirically based courage-building programme, delivered by Boma New Zealand CEO and Certified Dare to Lead™ Facilitator Kaila Colbin.

Brené has spent two decades studying shame and more than seven years specifically looking at leadership. During her research, she interviewed leaders from all over the world — from Fortune 100 companies, non-profits, public sector entities, and more — and asked one question: what is the future of leadership?

Remarkably, their answers pointed to one thing: we need braver leaders.




We need more courage.




The most significant finding from Brené’s latest research, and the foundation of Dare to Lead™, is that courage is a collection of four skill sets that are teachable, measurable, and observable.




After completing the three-day Dare to Lead™ programme you'll understand how to:
Effectively navigate vulnerability and unlock change
Turn values from fluffy language into tangible, practical behaviours
Build a common culture of trust in your team
Cultivate the skills to rise from setbacks and be more resilient




This curriculum is essential for teams who want to:
Be better equipped to deal with difficult conversations
Reduce unhealthy and unproductive behaviour
Be more creative and innovative
Build resilience and improve alignment
Foster a culture of accountability and trust




This experience is for you if:
You're in a position of leadership within your organisation
You see the potential in people and processes, and are willing to take responsibility for achieving that potential
You’re passionate about accelerating performance in yourself and others
You have to navigate organisational change as part of your role


Need help with the cost?

If you are an Educator or at a Not-for-Profit, you can automatically access a special price of $1,995 + GST when you register.

We also have partial scholarships available to attend the programme. Apply here and we’ll be in touch.

Boma is a Regional Business Network Provider. Your organisation may be eligible for funding support to attend this programme. Find out more at regionalbusinesspartners.co.nz




Our Health and Safety Plan

Boma is committed to delivering safe events. We follow best practices suggested by the New Zealand health authorities and work closely with our suppliers to prioritise health and wellbeing.

Our comprehensive health and safety plans ensure you can book with certainty and attend with confidence.



Our refund policy

For details on event refunds and transfers, please see our refund policy.




Contact us

Please email hello@boma.global with any questions.

events.long_description:
Overview

Behind the Pillows and Pens, an evening at Wellington Quarter Hotel.

Some of the best business decisions aren't made in a boardroom. They're made over a shared meal, a good conversation, or a moment that makes you stop and think, "this could work." Join us for Business After 5: Behind the Pillows and Pens, an evening at Wellington Quarter Hotel designed to do exactly that.

This is a progressive, hands-on evening where you'll move through the hotel in small groups, tasting, exploring, and experiencing firsthand what it would feel like to bring your business here, whether that's a client lunch, a conference, a staff reward, or your next Christmas Party.

By the end of the evening, you won't just know what Wellington Quarter Hotel offers. You'll have felt it.

What you'll get out of it:

The chance to network and build relationships with other local business leaders.
A firsthand look at spaces suited to your meetings, boardroom lunches or executive stays, so you can decide if they're right for you.
Tastings and demonstrations that let you experience the food and beverage offering rather than just hear about it.
A first look at Frankie's, and why it could become your go-to spot for business lunches and after-work drinks.
Inspiration and ideas for your next conference, client lunch, staff reward, or Christmas Party.

Whether you're planning your next big event or just want to see what's possible, this is your opportunity to explore Wellington Quarter Hotel and decide for yourself.

Who should attend
Designed for Wellington Chamber of Commerce members and the wider local business community, particularly those operating in the hospitality and corporate services.

Join us for this After 5 session and walk away with fresh perspectives and valuable business connections.

Spaces are limited. Register now to secure your place

events.name: Free First Home Buyers Seminar
events.venue:
The Habitat Hub Nelson
Nelson, Nelson Region
events.long_description:
Overview

One free evening. A mortgage adviser, a lawyer, a real estate agent and a building inspector answer every first home question you have.

Thinking about buying your first home? Start here.

Buying your first home can feel overwhelming. There are deposits and pre-approvals and LVRs and a pile of jargon you've never heard before and underneath it all, the question that actually keeps you up: can I even get approved?

This evening is designed to answer that. No sales pitch, no pressure, no jargon left unexplained. Just a clear, honest walk through what it actually takes to buy your first home in Nelson, from the people who do this every day.

What we'll cover

Budgeting and deposits how much you actually need, and where it can come from
Pre-approval what lenders look at, and how to put yourself in the strongest position
The First Home Loan scheme who qualifies and how it works
Finding the right place what to look for, and what the current Nelson market is doing
Making an offer conditional vs unconditional, and where people get caught out
The legal side sale and purchase agreements, LIM reports, title, settlement
Builders' reports what a building inspection covers, and the red flags worth walking away from
And beyond what happens after you get the keys

Who you'll hear from

We've brought together the full team you'd normally have to chase down one at a time:

A Mike Pero mortgage adviser, on finance and pre-approval
A real estate agent, on searching, negotiating and the local market
A property lawyer, on contracts, conditions and settlement
A building inspector, on what to check before you commit

There'll be time for questions, and you're welcome to stay afterwards for a one-on-one chat.

Who it's for

Anyone thinking about their first home whether you're planning to buy in the next few months or just starting to wonder if it's even possible. Bring your partner, bring a friend, bring your parents. Come with questions.

The details

📅 Thursday 24 September, 6:00pm
📍 The Habitat Hub Nelson, 166 Tahunanui Drive, Nelson
🎟️ Free to attend registration essential, seating is limited

Questions? Email scott@mikepero.co.nz

This seminar is general information only and isn't personalised financial advice.

Read less

events.long_description:
Overview

Explore the connections between astrology, emotions and the body, and discover a deeper perspective on wellbeing beyond treating symptoms.

Heal the Cause, Not the Symptom
An Evening on Astrology, Emotion, and Where Disease Really Begins



Have you ever noticed how the body keeps trying to tell us something, and we just reach for a pill or a cream instead of listening?

After having worked one-on-one hundreds of people with many of which having physical issues. I have yet to find someone who's physical issue is not related to an emotional cause or imbalance in their lifestyle and their nature. Skin issues often relating people getting under your skin and not expressing what's harbouring inside. Tension in one's legs which often stays for lack of boundaries and stability (no foundation to stand on), often Anger that shows up as inflammation. Fear that locks into the gut or the joints. Studying astrology and ancient teachings has made this even clearer, because these traditions map exactly how specific planets and signs govern specific parts of the body, and what happens when we live out of step with our own nature and purpose.

That's really what disease is. Dis-ease. Being out of ease, carrying stress the body hasn't found a way to release.

Join us at Bhakti Lounge for an evening where we trace these connections directly: which planets and signs govern which parts of the body, why illness tends to land exactly where it does, and how to work with the root emotional cause instead of just managing symptoms with pills and creams.

Event start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.
A plant-based dinner & dessert follows the event - all included in your ticket!




Meet your host Gopi:

Gopi helps spiritually minded professionals achieve clarity and overcome challenges on their path through his unique integration of hypnotherapy and palmistry. During his former life as a monk, he delved into the timeless wisdom of astrology, palmistry, and the ancient knowledge of the mind and consciousness, gaining deep insights into human psychology. He combines these powerful teachings with modern, effective tools as a certified practitioner in applied hypnotherapy, along with the knowledge he gained through his diploma in psychology and counselling.

events.long_description:
Overview

Journey through the five elements in a gentle Yoga Nidra for stillness, surrender and a deeper return to yourself.

Yoga Nidra: From Earth to Ether
Starts at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




Join me for a journey inward through the five elements.

Begin with the grounding embrace of Earth, move into the fluidity of Water, awaken the warmth of Fire, open into the freedom of Air, and finally arrive in the spaciousness of Ether.

A gentle Yoga Nidra for softening, surrendering and exploring within the stillness.

Earth
I am held.

Water
I surrender.

Fire
I transform.

Air
I breathe.

Ether
I am.

Be still.
Breathe.
And come home to yourself.

Yoga Nidra followed by a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert! All included in your ticket.


Meet Nicola, your host

Nicola of Namaste Nicola is a dedicated yoga teacher with over 20 years of experience teaching across Australia and New Zealand. With more than 300 hours of training with international teachers, her approach is gentle, soulful, and deeply grounded in yoga philosophy. Nicola creates a calm and nurturing space where students can slow down, rest deeply, and reconnect with themselves through practices such as Yoga Nidra, Hatha, and Yin Yoga.

WELLINGTON! IT’S GETTING FAST & GROOVY. 🌀 Ned Bennett makes his way to Aotearoa, hitting Wellington, Auckland & Christchurch this September.

Ned Bennett is a DJ and producer known for his dynamic, high-energy sets that blend various dance music genres. Ned’s ability to keep his style fresh and non-repetitive has made him a standout in the Melbourne music scene,earning the support of fellow-renowned artists like KETTAMA, Skin on Skin, VTSS, Patrick Mason, and many others across the globe.

﻿
Emerging from the ever-talented pool of Melbourne / Naarm talent, Ned Bennett has swiftly carved a space for himself in the scene. Taking inspiration from 90s groovetechno, suave garage and bouncy house, Ned Bennett has crafted a signature sound which has been put on full display across Australia and Europe; and has created standout performances at festivals such as Beyond the Valley, Let Them Eat Cake, and PitchMusic and Arts. With releases on both internationally recognised labels such as Suara and RAW, and his own label, Fractal Tapes, Ned Bennett’s diverse productions show no sign of slowing down.

events.long_description:
BHNZ Convention 2026 - Musika o Mātairangi
The 2026 Barbershop Harmony New Zealand Convention will take place in Wellington from September 25–27, 2026, hosted at the modern Tākina Convention Centre. This three-day event will bring together barbershop singers, quartets, choruses, and enthusiasts from across the region for a celebration of harmony, performance, and community.

Attendees can look forward to a full schedule featuring competitions, workshops, coaching sessions, mass sing-alongs, and showcase concerts highlighting both emerging talent and seasoned performers. Tākina’s world-class facilities provide an ideal setting for vibrant performances and social gatherings, all within walking distance of Wellington’s cultural and culinary attractions.

The convention aims to inspire musical excellence, foster connection within the barbershop community, and offer an unforgettable experience for performers and audiences alike.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Melding inspirations of folk, soul, pop and psychedelia with the guitar and spirited storytelling of musician-actor Nikita 雅涵 Tu-Bryant (Avatar 2, Far North); the thick  lushness of Moog synth and Fender Rhodes from Ed Zuccollo (aka Zuke); and the filthy  drive and barking drums of Rick Cranson (Little Bushman), KITA have long-since  solidified themselves as a must-see live band with a massive sound.
Front-woman Nikita 雅涵 Tu-Bryant is amidst her Artist in Residence at The Hannah Theatre in Wellington, translating her debut art-house film "LOVE LIVES HERE 愛住在這裡" for stage. The narrative originally inspired by the band's EP LOVE LIVES HERE which they toured nationwide in 2023. Tu-Bryant is debuting the film into a full immersive cinema-live-theatrical experience with a chorus of dancers and live band for her residency at the end of this year. In the meantime, she revives the live-in-concert version of this vulnerable ambitious work-in-progress. Excerpts from the film will be remixed live by Elfling. This show was showcased at Twisted Frequency, and now powerhouse trio KITA bring it back to the capital playing one of their favourite venues in Pōneke. 

Support act to be revealed beginning of September

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mental Health First Aid Aotearoa
NZ Citizens and residents pay $219 with ID.  f you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $499 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register..
Mental Health First Aid is an evidence-based workshop which gives people the skills and confidence to have supportive conversations with their whānau, co-workers and community and help guide them to professional help if needed.
You will learn to recognise common mental health challenges, how to provide initial help to someone experiencing a mental health challenge using a practical, evidence-based action plan, and how to respond in a crisis situation. During the workshop you will have the opportunity to practice new skills in a safe environment.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Mental health challenges covered in the course include:
Depression
Anxiety
Psychosis
Substance use problems
Mental Health Crisis Covered:
Suicidal thoughts and behaviours
Non- Suicidal self-injury
Panic attack
Traumatic events
Severe effects from Alcohol or other substance use
Aggressive behaviours
People who attend Mental Health First Aid training can complete a short online assessment to be accredited as a Mental Health First Aider. You must attend the full two days to be able to do the online assessment for accreditation. The accreditation is valid for three years.
If you choose not to be accredited, you will receive a certificate of participation if you attend the full course. You will also receive a workbook as part of your course fee.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Overview

A warm, fun workshop about networking and friendship for writers, artists and anyone wanting to connect to a community.

In a world where being a part of a community is more important than ever in career and life--especially in creative industries--we’re faced with the challenge of how to make long lasting, vital connections.

When we’re younger, society is set up to help us make friends and to build professional connections, whether it be through school, university or sporting or social groups.

But what if we don’t feel comfortable in those settings?

Or what if we’re older and have experienced some of the ups and down that life can bring, leaving us with a feeling of isolation.

Or what if we’re wanting to make connections that would help us in our careers but aren’t quite sure how to go about it?

Join psychotherapist Emma Constantine and author, poet and world traveller George Penney in this two hour talk that covers practical steps on network building and friendship for creative people wanting to broaden their social and professional lives.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

Read less

events.long_description:
Biker Breakfast
Bikers Breakfast is on again this year.
Closer to the date will advise details of a ride, but RAC wgtn will also have a stand there to share what we are about.
Open to some people to be available to help on the stand.

Other details of the Bikers Breakfast are:-
"We are organising our second annual Bikers Breakfast on Saturday 26 September from 8:30 am – 12:30 pm. This motorcycle safety event will be held in collaboration with Kapiti Coast District Council and Southwards Car Museum. Last year the Ulysses Club participated, and this year we would like to have a few more clubs in attendance, if possible.
Ride Forever course providers will be attending to speak with motorcyclists about the merits of learning to ride safely by signing up for ACC’s Ride Forever courses. The Motorcycle Collective will be setting up a safety gear Op Shop with a range of motorcycle apparel and equipment, and we will be giving away hot drinks and bacon butties.
A blind zone demonstration will show how easily a motorcycle can be invisible to large trucks – riders can sit in the cab of the truck and see if they can spot the bikes. There will be a helmet cleaning station and free rider safety packages that include important safety items like screen cleaners and re-usable hand warmers."

Overview

With a unique piano-vocal cabaret style, Sue and Steve create a harmonious blend of nostalgia and artistry.

Welcome To Our Lounge - Featuring songs from Carole King & Linda Ronstadt

Featuring the timeless songs of Carole King & Linda Ronstadt. Together, Sue and Steve create a harmonious blend of nostalgia and artistry, dedicating their performances to the timeless contributions of legendary artists Linda Ronstadt and Carole King.

With a unique piano-vocal cabaret style, they breathe new life into beloved classics, offering audiences an intimate and engaging experience.

Sue Dyson, a gifted vocalist known for her warm and captivating stage presence, backed by talented pianist Steve Papworth, are set to offer an extraordinary musical experience that celebrates the enduring legacies of Linda Ronstadt and Carole King.

Set in a laid-back intimate atmosphere, their performances promise an engaging experience where audiences will tap their feet to the classics that have defined generations.

Sue has graced the stage of New Zealand's 'Good Morning Show' multiple times, showcasing her vocal prowess and musical versatility. Additionally, Sue has lent her voice as a backup vocalist at the prestigious New Zealand Music Awards and has enjoyed significant success with her original country music in Australia.

Steve Papworth is a Palmerston North-based musician with a wide-ranging musical background spanning six decades playing keyboards across many musical genres. events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Following the announcement of their forthcoming EP Water For Dogs, Wellington four-piece rock outfit Wet Denim are taking the new music to the stage with a three-date release tour across Aotearoa this September and October.

Water For Dogs, due for release on Thursday 17 September, is shaping up to be Wet Denim’s most ambitious and expansive body of work yet. Singles ‘Living Room’, ‘Silence’ and ‘Mirrors’ have each offered a glimpse into the band’s refreshed rock direction, pushing their sound and their songwriting, all while retaining the energy that defines their live shows.

"We are beyond excited for this tour and to revisit some of our favourite venues around Aotearoa. We are incredibly proud of the new record and are ready to bring you our most high energy run of shows to date" - Wet Denim

Having already revealed some of Water For Dogs to a sold-out crowd at Wellington’s Moon in May and taken the new material to RNZ Afternoons NZ Live, the band are now set to bring the full record to life.




Wet Denim - Live on RNZ - Full Set




Made up of Nick Goodwin, Luca Crampton and brothers Jack and Joe Ledword, Wet Denim have fast become known as a must-see live act within Aotearoa’s music scene. Their last EP On The Line (2024) took them across Aotearoa and Australia and nabbed them support slots with international artists Highly Suspect, The Vanns, The Grogans, Bootleg Rascal, Teenage Dads, The Rions, The Rubens and local legends Blindspott.

Water For Dogs shows the band at their most assured. Don’t miss your chance to see it live in full for the first time this Spring.




Merch is also available for presale with GA tickets, avalible to collect on show day.




San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue
