What to Expect: Sacred Women's Circle


🌸Welcome, Sister. If you are feeling a pull in your heart to join us, that calling is your initiation.
Trust where you are being led. The circle lives within each of us.
Sacred Women's Circles have been used for thousands of years to build supportive communities, encourage authentic self-expression, and remind us that we are never alone on our journeys.

This is a dedicated, women-only gathering to honor our womb energy and embrace our sacred sisterhood.
Together, we step into a safe container to lower our walls, let our facades drop, and form real, authentic relationships rooted in vulnerability and trust.

✨ Meet Your Host: Crystal Mihinui
Your space is held by Crystal Mihinui, a dedicated practitioner with over 40 years of profound experience in music, frequency, and energy work. Crystal weaves her extensive background into every circle to create a deeply safe, transformative container for your healing. Her unique medicine includes:
Reiki Master: Channeling universal life force energy to restore balance and harmony to your body, mind, and spirit.

Music Therapist & Classically Trained Pianist: Using a lifetime of technical mastery and a deep understanding of musical psychology to shift emotional blocks and soothe the nervous system.
Sound Healing Practitioner: Blending acoustic frequencies to guide you into profound states of meditation, relaxation, and inner awakening.

🌿 The Journey & Flow
Gathering at our beautiful, secret forest spot surrounded by native trees, birds, and mountains, our flow includes
Sacred Circle & Oracle Cards: Opening our space with Archangel cards, inviting in nature spirits, and honoring our ancestors.
Womb Healing: Activating our deep feminine intuition using womb mudras and sacred mantras.
Shamanic Sound Journey: A deeply restorative guided meditation powered by crystal singing bowls and energy healing from the realm of the Fae.
Sisterhood Sharing: Returning to the circle to softly share our experiences, stories, and wisdom.
Ritual Releasing what no longer serves us by offering our written words to the sacred forest.

Forest Bathing & Journaling: Immersion in the healing frequencies of nature.📍

Location & Meeting Points
We have two meeting point options, both provided upon booking.
You can choose to:
Meet at our cozy home-based studio to rideshare together
Or meet directly at our beautiful outdoor location in Rivendell.☔

Rain Plan: If the wild weather joins us, we will move to our beautiful indoor alternative (details provided upon booking).🎒

What to Bring
A shared vegetarian dish to enjoy together during our gathering
A journal and pen for your reflections
Comfortable clothing suitable for the forest.
Swimming gear (if you would like to take a dip! 🏖).🎟

Investment & Inclusivity Children's Tickets: Children are very welcome to join our sacred space and are half price.
Community Services Card: Concession tickets are gladly available; please bring your proof of entitlement on arrival

Cancellation Policy: As a small, heart-led family business, our time is precious. Tickets are non-refundable, but you are deeply welcome to gift your ticket to another sister if you cannot make it.

SEXY AGEING IS COMING TO STOKES VALLEY 🔥

Have you noticed that training doesn't seem to work the same way it used to?

Maybe the weight is slowly creeping up. Perhaps you're experiencing hot flushes, mood swings, poor sleep, brain fog, low energy, low sex drive or you're simply wondering why the things that once worked for your body no longer seem to work.

You're not alone.

So many women have been asking us for support and guidance to help them better understand what is happening to their bodies during perimenopause and menopause.

At Be Suite, we listened. That's why we are incredibly excited to welcome Tracy Minnoch-Nuku, founder and CEO of Sexy Ageing, to Stokes Valley.

Tracy has spent more than 30 years working within the health and fitness industry. Her career has included leadership roles with Fitness First Asia and Les Mills Asia Pacific, as well as co-founding one of Asia's first boutique fitness chains, Fire Fitness. As Tracy began experiencing menopause symptoms herself, she was shocked by the lack of evidence-based information and support available to women. Determined to change that, she founded Sexy Ageing, launched the internationally recognised podcast of the same name, wrote My Menopause Memoir, and created programmes specifically designed to help women thrive throughout this stage of life.This workshop will cover topics including:✔ Understanding perimenopause and menopause✔ Why your body changes as you age✔ Weight gain, sleep, mood, energy, and hormones✔ Training and nutrition strategies✔ Practical tools to help you feel stronger, healthier, and more confidentWhether you're experiencing symptoms yourself, preparing for the future, or supporting somebody you love, this workshop is for you.This event is open to both members and non-members, so bring your friends, mothers, sisters, daughters, workmates, and whānau.

events.long_description:
Silver Sonics with Seismic State and Electric Tapestry @ Moon
Silver Sonics have escaped Whanganui to tour the lower North Island this winter and have teamed up with some local favourites - Seismic State and Electric Tapestry, to bring you a night of unforgettable, high energy rock.

Silver Sonics are an indie-rock, neo-psych, pop/rock band hailing from the creative cauldron of Whanganui. Their sound fuses pop swagger with 90s grooves and 60s melodic hooks reminiscent of Britain and America with a distinctly NZ flavour. You can expect their show to be an uplifting sonic ride with energetic, authentic grooves, catchy guitar riffs and meaningful lyrics.

Seismic State play high-octane alt-rock with a blues-funk soul. A staple of the New Zealand rock circuit, the Wellington quartet is known for a professional, high-energy live show. Since the release of their debut EP State of Things, which earned international airplay and a Top 58 spot on The Generator FM’s Kiwi 101, the band has consistently anchored bills at iconic venues including San Fran, Valhalla, Moon, Lovelands and Underworld Tavern. Seismic State delivers a sophisticated performance built for the big stage.

Electric Tapestry are an alternative rock band known for their unique blend of progressive rock, shoegaze, post-rock, and pop. The five-piece group describes their eccentric sound as a "space rock dish of creamy psychedelics, metal chunks with a pop topping.” Characterized by their three-guitar setup, they layer a variety of musical techniques—ranging from shimmering Dunedin-sound jangle, warm fuzz, and funk-infused rhythms to intense heavy metal guitar solos.

With these 3 acts in one night and for just $10, you'll need to get in quick, this one is sure to be a sell out!

events.long_description:
But Why, Dad?
Kids ask the best questions.
“Why is the sky blue?”
“Why do we dream?”
“Why does Dad always wear socks with sandals?”

In ‘But Why, Dad?’, no question is too silly, too big, or too confusing to turn into a song! Hot on the heels of the smash-hit ‘All The Things I Wish I Could Be’ — praised as “a celebration of possibility, identity and good old-fashioned silliness” — this brand-new Kiwi kids’ comedy concert dives into the wonderful, sometimes wobbly world of emotions, discoveries, mistakes, and mysteries, with plenty of laughs along the way.

Once again, loveable dads Jeff and Tom bring their “excellent comic chemistry and a relaxed rapport with the audience” to the stage. The live music is a highlight — “catchy, well-crafted and often hilarious” — with “subtle nods for adults tucked among the big beats for kids.”

‘But Why, Dad?’ invites the audience to be part of the fun — clapping, singing, and even shouting out their own big questions, which are cleverly woven into the action.

At its heart, this proudly local production celebrates curiosity as the ultimate superpower — encouraging tamariki to stand up, speak up, and ask questions, because that’s how we learn more about ourselves and the world. Funny, fast-paced and full of heart, ‘But Why, Dad?’ is a riot of music and curiosity that proves asking “why” the best superpower of all — even if Dad doesn’t know all the answers.

Every “why” is an adventure waiting to happen!

events.venue: Bhakti Lounge Wellington,175 Vivian Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Somatic Breathwork: Spring Cleanse & Rise
Clear winter’s heaviness and awaken your natural aliveness through a gentle somatic breathwork journey into greater clarity and presence.

About this Event


Somatic Breathwork: Spring Cleanse & Rise





Starts at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

Spring is a threshold, the season the body naturally wants to clear out, lighten, and open.

Spring Cleanse & Rise is a 60-minute somatic breathwork journey that works on two levels at once. First, we clear: releasing the heaviness, fog, and holding that can settle in over winter. Then, from that cleaner, quieter space, we open, using the breath as a doorway into a deeper, more spacious state of awareness.

Because when the body has less to carry, something else can move. A subtle, rising sense of aliveness. A feeling of connection to something larger and quieter within you. Many people describe it as coming home to a part of themselves they'd forgotten was there.

This is that experience made accessible, no belief system required, no experience needed. Just your breath, a safe and consent-led container, and a willingness to meet what opens.

Through a trauma-aware breathwork arc, we'll support your system to:

release the stagnation, weight, and fatigue carried through winter
soften the guarding that keeps you stuck in your head
let a natural, rising energy move up and through the body
open, gently, into a more expansive and connected state of awareness

You'll leave feeling lighter, clearer, and quietly awake, grounded in your body and open to more.

Who this is for

This session is for you if:

you can feel spring's shift but you're still carrying winter in your body
you've felt heavy, foggy, flat, or stuck in your head
your chest or breath has felt tight, shallow, or braced
you're curious about deeper, more expansive states, but put off by dogma or jargon
you want something that genuinely lands in the body, not just another idea to think about
you're new to breathwork and want a welcoming, choice-based space to begin

What to expect

Arrival (consent + information), chair, side-lying, and low-intensity options available
Guided breath arrival and brief body scan to ground and centre
Breath demonstration + choice of intensity tracks (including a gentle nasal-only option)
A guided somatic breathwork arc, clearing first, then opening, steady and body-led
Optional movement to support release (micro-shakes, shaking, or gentle unwinding)
Space to rest in whatever opens, spacious, quiet, supported
Integration rest + grounding
Closing reflection (brief journaling prompt or quiet pause)

Benefits you may notice

You might experience:

a lighter body and a clearer, more spacious mind
more warmth, aliveness, and energy moving through you
a felt sense of connection, presence, and inner spaciousness
emotional release without overwhelm
deeper, easier breathing
a steadier, more awake baseline that stays with you

What to bring

Please bring:

Warm layers (we'll warm up, but your body may cool during rest)
Water bottle
Small towel
Optional eye mask or light scarf
Journal and pen

Pre-class prep

Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at if there's anything you'd like to share before the session.

Contraindications and safety

Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy, serious cardiovascular conditions, uncontrolled blood pressure, glaucoma or retinal detachment, epilepsy or seizure history, recent surgery or concussion, or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.

Aftercare

After the session, remember to:

Drink plenty of water
Eat nourishing food
Engage in simple movement or a short walk
Journal your insights
Get an early bedtime

Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours. Reach out if you need support.


You'll also receive a guided audio breathwork aftercare to support you in the 24 to 48 hours after the session, with gentle regulation, grounding, and integration.





Event followed by a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert! All included in your ticket.



About Lynn (Facilitator)

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Lynn supports people who are high-functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or quietly stuck on the inside.

Lynn's work blends three pillars:

Somatic breathwork to regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, and deep rest, in a gentle, consent-based way
Life coaching to translate what opens in session into real change in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily life

Lynn's approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn't on forcing anything, it's on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, open, and remember its natural capacity for calm and connection.


1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching, a spot is open

If you felt a yes in your body during this session, you're invited to go deeper. Lynn is opening a private 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching spot for someone ready to work with nervous system regulation, somatic inquiry, breathwork, and grounded life coaching support.

To enquire, DM "rise" on Instagram or email with the subject line: October 1:1.





Booking and policies
Doors close 5 minutes after the start.
Refunds or transfers are as per Bhakti Lounge policy.


Questions before you join? Email and Lynn will support you.




Agenda


🕑: 05:45 PM - 06:00 PM
Arrive to Bhakti Lounge

🕑: 06:00 PM - 07:00 PM
Somatic Breathwork: Spring Cleanse & Rise
Host: Lynn

🕑: 07:00 PM - 08:15 PM
Plant-based dinner and dessert!

events.long_description:
Four Last Songs - Wellington
One of the world’s most acclaimed conductors, Sir Donald Runnicles, returns to the NZSO in a programme of pure luxury and ravishing beauty.

Programme:
R Strauss Rosenkavalier Suite
R Strauss Four Last Songs
Brahms Symphony No. 3

The sensuous, glittering raptures of the Rosenkavalier Suite evoke the decadence of 18th century Vienna in a dazzling array of complex waltzes.

Then delve deeper into Richard Strauss’ most personal, revealing and achingly beautiful music with his sublime Four Last Songs. These profound songs, performed by silver-voiced soprano Madeleine Pierard, sumptuously evoke a sunset portrait of a wife well loved and a life well lived.

We balance this decadence with the crystalline Symphony No. 3 from Johannes Brahms. In music that plays between light and shadow, the work takes on as its organising motto frei aber froh — free but happy.

Sir Donald Runnicles appears with generous support from Dame Bronwen Holdsworth DNZM.

events.name: Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance
events.venue: Hebden Cres,Dry Creek Campsite, Haywards, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance
We will climb for 40 minutes up the 4WD Buchanans Road Tramping Track, passing Dendrobium cunninghamii, Earina autumnalis, Helichrysum lanceolatum and Metrosideros colensoi.

From there we’ll walk bait lines and informal unformed tracks for a 90-minute circuit of Syzygium maire (maire tawake, swamp maire). Botanising time will be additional to this. Bring good footwear and gaiters if you have them for waterlogged sites. There is one place with hip-stretching tall steps cut into soil. Areas can be slippery when wet. Hand ropes are beside steep mud steps. This is a 7.5km walk with moving time of around two and a half hours.

There is recent research on Syzygium maire in the Wellington region, published by the School of Biological Sciences at Victoria University. The authors highlight that we ‘need to identify refugia in accessible, albeit sometimes fragmented, habitat’ and recommend ‘leveraging human–nature interactions in areas to create, expand, and protect habitat for [this] rare species in a rapidly changing world’. Syzygium maire has a threat classification of Threatened-Nationally Vulnerable. The research illustrates the preferred habitat of Syzygium maire is waterlogged areas. Such areas are few and shrinking, both nationally and in Wellington region.

This trip will look at thriving Syzygium maire that have fruited and seeded in the rare wetlands below Boulder Hill. We’ll see Ramarama, Threatened – Nationally Critical, and Coprosma rubra, At Risk – Declining and over 100 other plant species observed on iNaturalist. These can be seen in a map view of the proposed quarry Overburden Disposal Area.

Ominously there’s a Fast-track proposal to turn this precious area into a quarry overburden disposal area. This has been reported on by Radio NZ. The Friends of Belmont Regional Park and Wellington Botanical Society have strongly opposed this. The Fast-track application is here.

Non-members are welcome to join, making it an excellent opportunity to explore this region’s native flora.

Meet: Dry Creek Carpark, Hebden Crescent, Kelson, Lower Hutt at 9.30am. This Carpark with toilets is a 10-minute walk from Manor Park Station on the Hutt Valley Line. Trains leave Wellington at 8.35am and arrive at Manor Park Station at 9.08am.

Leader: John Barnett, 021 063 1590,

events.long_description:
The WBS presents: a concert featuring Skin and Bone
From deepest Dunedin comes the quirky quintet known as Skin and Bone. Formed in early 2019 from two of Dunedin's longest-running contemporary folk and jazz bands Catgut and Steel and The Chaps, Skin and Bone are: John Dodd (bass, vocals), Stephen “Wee Huddy” Hudson (drums, vocals), Mike Moroney (guitar, vocals), Anna Bowen (fiddle, mandolin, vocals) and Emily Sterk (clarinet, saxophone, vocals). They are five superb musicians with a pedigree as long as your arm, bringing you a solid repertoire of Western Swing with a decidedly Kiwi bend. Based on the country-jazz sounds of the 30s and 40s, this most danceable band will have you immersed in the tight harmonies and musicianship of ol’ time Americana and Kiwi originals in equal measure.

In their self-styled genre of Cowboy Lounge, they have no peer. Drawing heavily on the legacy of Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys, The Mills Brothers, Leon Redbone and others of their ilk, Skin and Bone bring their swing styles to the Great American Songbook and add plenty of their own quirky original songs to every performance. With five diverse singers, their arrangements are predictably vocal-forward and well harmonised; with fiddle, mandolin and clarinet lines at once both authentic in style and unique. Locally they have become the darlings of the young and vibrant swing dance scene and are the band of choice of Dunedin dance chapter Swing Riot for their regular Lindy Hop and Blues events and the Dunedin Swing Festival.

On the back of their recent appearance at the Whare Flat and Canterbury Folk Festivals, and their recently released album Last Bus to Brockville, they bring their particular schtick to the South of the North in a whirlwind four-day tour of Carterton, New Plymouth, Palmerston North and Wellington. Be it festivals, dances, concerts or any showcase, Skin and Bone are the entertainment choice that will have brogues tapping, dresses swirling and smiles and earworms to take home.

Presented by: TEG Live & Destroy All Lines
UK Indie Rock icons RAZORLIGHT head to New Zealand for the first time ever to perform a headline show in Wellington as part of their ‘’America’’ world tour! The band are celebrating the 20th anniversary of their 5x Platinum self-titled album, a landmark release that cemented their place among the defining acts of the early 2000’s indie scene.
With era-shaping hits like ‘America’, ‘In The Morning’ and ‘Before I Fall To Pieces’, Razorlight became one of the UK’s most successful guitar bands of their generation, delivering three Top 5 albums, multiple Platinum certifications, winning an NME Award, and performing on some of the world’s biggest stages.
Razorlight’s live shows channel the same hook-laden, post-punk-infused energy that defines their sound, but amplified into something harder, tighter and far more intense.
Their melodic swagger of early-2000s indie, driven by a restless passion makes every track feel like it’s about to ignite. Their sets tend to move with a kind of breathless momentum, tight rhythms, bright guitar lines, and delivery that between exposed emotion and a sharp, commanding force. Live, Razorlight animate the entire room.
‘’Razorlight reminded fans why they won their hearts with a masterful performance featuring astonishing electric guitar riffs and impeccable stage craft yet again from Borrell.’’ – The Upcoming
‘’The rhythm drove through the room like a heartbeat, and the connection between the band members was electric. Each note and lyric lands with precision and passion.’’ – At The Barrier

events.long_description:
New Zealand, prepare to surrender to the might of AUGUST BURNS RED this October, with the GRAMMY Award-nominated stalwarts set to return to our shores joined by special guests BLOOM,
“We are so excited to headline and return back to New Zealand after a decade! We are bringing along our new friends in Bloom to make this a can’t miss show. This tour will also be the first place in the world where we do a tour celebrating the release of our brand new record Season of Surrender. We hope to see you all soon!” - August Burns Red
Crafting their signature brand of metalcore for over two decades, AUGUST BURNS RED have ferociously established themselves as one of the foremost acts in the genre. Hailing from Lancaster, Pennsylvania, the band's milestones and legacy spans everything from multiple top 10 placements on the Billboard Top 200 and tours with everyone from Bullet For My Valentine through to A Day To Remember and countless more. Also with two GRAMMY Award nominations in their wake, nominated for Best Metal Performance in 2016 for Identity and again in 2018 for Invisible Enemy, AUGUST BURNS RED have never rested on their laurels or stopped pushing the limits of their sound; a fact that has loudly carried into 2026 with the upcoming release of a their tenth studio album Season Of Surrender due out on June 5 via Fearless Records. 
On a live front, AUGUST BURNS RED's reputation is as formidable as their creative output, renowned for their visceral performances across the globe, most recently stupefying Australian crowds in 2023 supporting Polaris nationally on the Fatalism Tour. Praised by Scenestr for delivering "a raging masterclass in pure American metalcore with a 20-year, career-spanning set list that resonated spectacularly" of the Adelaide show supporting Polaris, X-Press Magazine also declared of the band's 2023 Perth performance on the same run that ABR demonstrated "why they have cemented themselves as one of the most respected names in the scene." 
One of Australia's most prolific rising heavy acts, BLOOM wield an open-veined take on melodic hardcore that has seen them tour the globe, release two full-length albums and cultivate an army of dedicated fans along the way. Emerging in 2017, BLOOM released their 2024 debut full-length, Maybe In Another Life, before swiftly turning their gaze to their 2025 sophomore album, The Light We Chase. Wowing with their multi-faceted and matured collection of songs on album #2, also expanding their creative reach further than ever before, BLOOM kicked off 2026 with their biggest headline performances to date, touring Australia nationally to celebrate The Light We Chase. Whether sharing stages with the likes of Silverstein and Thornhill or enamouring as headliners, you can definitely count on one thing when it comes to a BLOOM live show: it is seriously not to be missed.

events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”
Hero image: © Cornelia Parker. Courtesy of the artist and Frith Street Gallery, London

events.long_description:
Che Fu is on a national tour celebrating 25 years since breakthrough album, 'Navigator'. He'll bring his blend of soul, reggae, hip hop, rock, and Pacific influences to the Michael Fowler Centre. He'll be joined on stage by longstanding band The Kratez as well as soul artist Aaradhna, vocalist Betty-Anne, and hip hop artist King Kapisi.
Che Fu appeared on the NZ music scene with funk rockers Supergroove while still in high school. After around five years, he went solo and released hit song 'Chains' in 1996. You might recognise his other chart-topping songs ‘Fade Away’ and ‘Misty Frequencies’ on the 'Navigator' album.
The Niuean/Māori musician became a pioneer of hip-hop and Pasifika music. He was recently inducted into the NZ Music Hall of Fame. He's earned a Pacific Music Awards Lifetime Achievement Award. He's also a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit.

events.long_description:
It's in the Ballot - Wellington North Electorate - IN Studio
'It's in the Ballot' takes the format of the Kiwi TV classic 'It's in the Bag' game show and puts a political twist to it.

About this Event



Contestants of 'It's in the Bag' become political candidates in 'It's in the Ballot' Meet the Candidates.

Candidates choose a numbered box which has a question that has been submitted online by voters before the show.

It’s in the Ballot” is a community-led awareness and participation initiative. We aim to increase voter interest in the general and council elections nationally.

By using broadcasting and web-based technologies to deliver in-studio; online on Facebook, YouTube and Twitch; and edited as YouTube videos we aim to enable voters to make informed voting decisions.

This means you can send the weblink of the YouTube Video of your electorate show to your friends and whanau to encourage them to watch the show before they cast their votes.

Enrolments cut off date is Sunday 25th October 2026

Enrol at - https://vote.nz/enrolling/enrol-or-update/enrol-or-update-online

Early voting starts Monday 26th October 2026

Election Day is Saturday 7th November 2026






Agenda


🕑: 06:30 PM - 06:50 PM
Audience and candidates arrive so they are seated by 7pm

🕑: 06:50 PM - 07:00 PM
Candidate briefing and pre-broadcast checks


Info: We check that the technology is working, including those candidates who are attending online.



🕑: 07:00 PM - 08:00 PM
First half of the show


Info: The ‘It's in the Ballot’ host will introduce the local host who joins us to present the questions in the boxes. Each candidate starts with an Opening Statement (1 minute) on why you should give them your electoral and party vote. The candidates choose a numbered box and speaks to the question (1 minute). Candidates are given the same number of questions. Candidates are sent the question sheet 24 hours before the show so they can prepare their responses.



🕑: 08:00 PM - 08:10 PM
Midshow break

🕑: 08:10 PM - 09:00 PM
Second half of the show


Info: Three Hard Hitting questions (1 minute) are answered by all candidates followed by a Closing Statement (1 minute).



🕑: 09:00 PM - 09:30 PM
After show 'meet and greet 'with candidates, hosts and production team


Info: We encourage all attendees to stay after the show to talk to the candidates in person. You may also like to take a photo with the candidates to use on social media to encourage your followers to watch the recorded show before they cast their postal votes from Tuesday 9th September 2025 and must be casted into voting drop box by 12pm Saturday 11th October 2025

events.id: Effective Business Analysis-Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand-All Events In
events.name: Effective Business Analysis
events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Effective Business Analysis
Defining change with clarity and agility. Discover how to apply the core skills and techniques of elicitation, analysis, and communication.

About this Event


Description
The business world is demanding faster change, the ability to adapt and solutions that are fit for purpose. As a business analyst, you're counted on for your skills as a conceptual and practical thinker, a relationship builder, and a translator. You're relied upon to identify and describe the change required to address business issues. Sometimes there are problems that require a fix, opportunities that need to be realised or situations where the business simply doesn't know but is prepared to "give it a go" and experiment to gain insights to what it should do next.
In this course, you'll be introduced to a series of context aware, business-focussed approaches that you can apply to:
Work with stakeholders to uncover the business issue that needs to be addressed
Define the change required within its context
Prioritise and scope the requirements based on business value and
Specify requirements clearly to those delivering the solution
Designed and delivered by our Equinox IT team of practicing business analysts, this course covers how to structure your analysis activities based on the context and the issue at hand to describe requirements that fully represent the change required.




Outline
Day 1
Overview and concepts
What is business analysis?
Requirements analysis framework

Discover – understanding context
Understanding a business domain
Adjusting to different types of initiative
Stakeholders – identification, classification and engaging
Techniques (root cause analysis, 5 whys, diverge, converge, etc.)
The discovery canvas

Focus topic: Elicitation –gathering information and understanding
Purpose and context
Selecting the right technique (interviews, workshops, research, observation, brainstorming, etc.)
Planning a session
Running a session
Post session activities
Main exercise - role play

Day 2
Define – understanding the change required
Introduction to capabilities
Information and data – concept/domain Modelling
Business process – tips on modelling
Business rules – their relationship with other business concepts
Scenarios – use cases
Change strategy map
Change aspect map
Defining user and other stories

Scope – understanding priority and value
Helping the business to assess value
Techniques
User story maps

Day 3
Focus topic: Workshop Facilitation–gaining consensus
Being self-aware
Facilitation
Preparation
Group dynamics
Handling various situations
Main exercise - role play

Deliver – packaging for delivery
Backlog refinement
Developing good acceptance criteria
Understanding various types of solution requirements and contributing elements

Focus topic: Communication – telling the story
A brief overview of the difference between specification and communication




Learning outcomes
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to;
Analyse and understand the kind of business issue that needs to be addressed
Engage stakeholders and analyse their business needs
Define a change strategy
Define the aspects of change required
Understand various business models e.g. business process, information, business rules
Define a user story and associated requirements
Use effective techniques to elicit requirements
Understand how to plan and facilitate a requirements workshop
Understand scoping based on business value
Analyse, document and review solutions and detailed requirements
Define acceptance criteria
Understand how to communicate with a variety of audiences




Accreditation and certification
This course aligns with the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge v3.0®.




Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts, systems analysts and enterprise analysts of all experience levels. The course will also be of value to any project team members involved in requirements definition activities.




Prerequisites
There are no prerequisites for this course, however, some experience in business analysis will help.

events.long_description:
Sewing - All Levels
All levels welcome! Beginning sewers will learn basic skills and techniques and those with some experience will improve their skills and learn tips and tricks.
Beginners - If you're a beginner, you'll start by making a lined bag, which teaches all the basic skills involved. After that you'll move on to a project of your choice, in consultation with the tutor.  Please bring: 1 metre of firm cotton fabric for your bag outer and 1 metre of a lighter cotton fabric for the lining. You'll also need to bring scissors, a Bernina bobbin (this can be purchased from the CEC office on the day of the course for $7), pins, thread to match your outer fabric, an 18 cm zip and tape measure to the first session.
 If you're a returning student, or have already mastered the basic skills, you'll work on your own project so please bring along whatever you're currently working on (or something new) and your sewing kit. 
Please note PDF patterns are not suitable for this course unless you are very experienced in using them;  we strongly recommend patterns from the following companies:  Simplicity, Butterick, New Look or Quicksew.
By the end of the course, you'll have been introduced to basic skills in dressmaking, if beginners, or further skills for the more experienced.
You'll be able to:
• Use all sewing machine equipment and demonstrate basic sewing techniques (basic seams and finishes)
• Begin to read a commercial pattern and select appropriate materials for task
• Cut out and construct a garment using techniques learned
• (In addition), use a variety of advanced sewing techniques e.g. rolled hems, various zip insertions (invisible and standard), make buttonholes or line garments. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. events.name: Scottish Country Dancing
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Scottish Country Dancing
Why do Scottish Country Dancing? Great music and amazing ‘brain gym’ for body and mind! Scottish Country Dancing is a very social form of dancing, danced in "sets" usually with four "couples" - unlike Highland Dancing which is usually solo dancing. Have fun and meet new people, while getting fit!
It’s suitable for all levels of fitness, and is a great way of meeting and socialising with new people. Scottish country dancing is a common pastime for thousands of dancers in many countries, whether you’re in Japan, Germany, the US or Scotland itself.
Wear soft flat shoes and loose clothing and bring a bottle of water. No partner is needed – we change partners for every dance!
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Name and perform to beginner level the five major steps of Scottish Country Dancing
• Name and perform ten simple formations
• Participate in five simple Scottish Country dances, in strathspey (slow) and reel/jig (fast) tempo
• Clap rhythm to reel, jig and strathspey tempo
• Have the confidence and skills to join a club to progress your social dancing 
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk]. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Crochet for Calmness
The repetitive movements of crochet help the brain make more serotonin, which can decrease tension and feelings of depression. We’ll move through all the steps from the starting slipknot to reading patterns and diagrams and making your first crochet projects.
You’ll learn to make a granny square, change colours and how to increase and decrease. You’ll also find out more about the notations and abbreviations of crochet stitches so you can make those awesome crochet projects you've been waiting to make!
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Discuss the benefits of crochet for relaxation and alleviation of mood
• Read a basic crochet pattern and recognise crochet terminology
• Choose yarns and hooks for projects
• Use a range of stitches with confidence
• Complete at least one project of your choice (granny square, keychain, garden decoration)
Suitable for all beginners, both left and right-handers and those who may have struggled to learn to crochet. Initial materials provided but please bring along any yarn or crochet hooks you would like to work with.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Songwriting: How to Write Your Own Songs
The course is ideal for anyone who wants to write better songs - whether you’ve got a few songs under your belt or you’re a complete beginner. Take a song idea through to a finished song you can be proud of. Split into easy-to-follow steps, this course walks you through everything from finding titles to writing chord progressions and ensuring your lyrics and melodies fit together. You’ll share your creations with fellow songwriters and get personalised feedback. You’ll see exactly how to turn theory into practice and write your best songs yet.
This course includes:
-  Practical tips and techniques for songwriting
-  Ideas for making your songs stronger, more expressive and more appealing to your audience
-  How to overcome writer’s block, be an inspired and prolific songwriter who writes authentic songs
-  An opportunity to share your songs with fellow students, bounce off ideas and learn from one another
-  Learn how to structure a song effectively
-  The pillars of songwriting and how to use them
-  How to write better lyrics
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Discover the exact steps to successfully write your own original songs; expanding a song from a verse and chorus, to a complete song while keeping your listeners engaged using transitions and dynamic contrasts between sections
-  Come up with ideas, write lyrics, melodies, chord progressions and instrumental grooves that have an emotional impact on you and your audience
-  Identify the structure of a great song, including how to combine melody, chords, lyrics and rhythm that create magic for your listeners
-  Possess the confidence and skills to find inspiration and get past common creative hurdles and blocks so you can develop an initial spark of creativity into a complete song
-  Stay inspired and find your authentic voice as a songwriter. r

The rasp in her singing voice is as immediately recognisable as her talent for entertaining. Nobody puts on a show like R&B/soul singer Macy Gray. The Ohio-born artist came to fame in 1999 with her triple-platinum debut album ‘On How Life Is’. Her concert at Wellington’s St James Theatre will deliver a jaw-dropping celebration of chart-topping hits I Try, Still, Do Something, Sexual Revolution, and Sweet Baby. You can also expect her new single I’m Too Sexy from her upcoming album, The Trouble With Truth. 
Presented in association with the Wellington Jazz Festival, this is a rare chance to see one of the great R&B and soul artists of a generation. Macy Gray has sold over 25 million albums worldwide and won a GRAMMY Award along with two BRIT Awards. She has collaborated with everyone from Ariana Grande to Maino and Galactic. Her music consistently resonates throughout pop culture, transcending many genres and building a devout and diverse fan base.

events.long_description:
Expect familiar melodies, unexpected turns, and a celebration of jazz. For two nights only, Set Fire to the Brass brings a two-part show to The Opera House. First on stage, say ‘Hello’ to Kiwi vocalist Joanna Darling. She gives English singer-songwriter Adele’s songs a lush, jazz-infused edge. She’ll give full-hearted renditions of hits like Rolling in the Deep and Skyfall. Members of the Rodger Fox Big Band and local musicians lead the second half with improv solos and classic jazz standards. 

Joanna has performed in musicals, cabarets, and as a soloist on international cruise lines. She combines a powerful vocal belt with piano and guitar. The Rodger Fox Big Band has played at prestigious jazz festivals and won six Tui Awards for the best New Zealand jazz recording. Together, they deliver the emotional depth of Adele’s lyrics with the warmth of live jazz.

events.name: Calligratherapy - Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Calligratherapy - Beginners
Many of us live sedentary lifestyles, sitting for up to eight hours or more a day hunched over our keyboard - all the while rarely taking a proper breath! Even if we wanted to take a deep enriching breath into the lower lobes of our lungs, we are limited due to our posture. Often due to the stresses and strains of a busy work and life balance, our unconscious brain can develop a pattern of holding, irregular and shadow breaths.
Does this sound like your experience? 
Not being able to breathe properly is the key cause of many chronic respiratory diseases (Nestor, 2020)
Calligratherapy combines science journalist James Nestor's theory on proper breathing with the philosophy of ancient Chinese calligraphy to promote a state of optimal wellbeing.
Calligratherapy has been developed specifically for those who have never practiced calligraphy before and who are interested in deriving the benefits without having to learn the language or all the characters. It integrates the simple and intuitive act of inhaling and exhaling into calligraphy practice with Eastern philosophy behind it.
A range of different breathing exercises are embedded into each 90 minute session focusing on different calligraphy scripts.  Over the five weeks, you will develop and practice the awareness of healthy breathing, while learning new techniques of Chinese soft brush calligraphy covering five different scripts. 
All materials included in course fee.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Start a new creative practice in Chinese soft brush calligraphy
Develop your own mindfulness strategy
Better manage everyday stress levels and access a calm, empowered and positive state of mind
Find ways to explore eastern philosophy and develop deeper connections with your spiritual self. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
How to be a DJ - An Introduction
Always wanted to try being a DJ but not sure where to begin? Experienced and professional DJ Shan (Shannon Chng-Rawiri) will teach you all about the technical aspects, equipment and terminology, as well as the industry in general, and enable you to put together a confident short performance.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Gain an understanding of the work content and career opportunities in this industry
Learn the difference between what a DJ is required to deliver in the following situations: Mobile, Club, Radio, Turntablist and Hobby
Participate in various practical activities: Slip Cueing and Baby Scratch, basic beat matching and song structures
Gain a good understanding of the equipment used and terminology including: - Tables: pitch control - Mixer: crossfader, input faders, EQ, gain, cue system - Needles: back tracking - Slip Mats
Learn about Counting Bars and Matching Tempos - The difference between a Bar, Phrases and BPM - Techniques to Count, Hand position and movement etc
Confidently present a 5 minute performance in class
The course will be held at DJ Shan’s studio at Shop 21, 73 Cuba Street, Wellington.  Bring headphones, a USB with your favourite music and a laptop, if you have one. Limited to eight participants.

Knitting for Beginners
Come and reap the benefits of a mindful and meditative craft-form.  Meet other people interested in making things with their hands, chat over crafting and find out what the craft craze is all about.
Join crafter Stella Carruthers as she shares her ten years plus knitting experience in this beginner’s knitting class that supports each student as an individual learner.
Master basic knitting techniques, learn how to cast stitches on and off the needles, explore the knit and purl stitches and practice how to hold the needles in a way that is comfortable for you - then learn how to knit in the English style.

Scriptwriting
During this course, you will develop and build on your writing skills so you can confidently produce scripted narrative. You will learn how the basics of scriptwriting work, whether it be for stage or screen.
 Topics discussed and practised include the three act structure, script format, the differences between writing for film, theatre and television, creating dialogue, world building and more.
 We’ll take part in exercises, watch clips and have group discussions. In workshops, you’ll give and receive feedback, developing your scriptwriting skills through both. By the end of the course, you’ll be ready to finish your script, and take the next steps toward bringing it from page to stage (or screen!).
 Bring pen and paper.

- Analyse film, television, and theatre with a new lens for the way scripted stories work
- Develop character arcs and dynamics
- Create and build worlds
- Write effective dialogue and work with subtext
- Develop and implement a writing routine that works for your life
- Give and receive constructive feedback on your writing
- Have the confidence to put your work out into the world

events.long_description:
Inner Worlds: Sound Bath
Journey inward through timeless stories and soothing sounds in an immersive sound bath for stillness, reflection and deep listening.

About this Event


Inner Worlds: A Story-Led Sound Bath





Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

Across cultures and throughout history, stories have guided people inward, offering wisdom, comfort, and connection. This immersive sound bath blends ancient poetic narratives with the soothing sounds of harmonium, flutes, crystal bowls, and gentle voice to create a space of stillness, reflection, and deep listening.

Mats, blankets and cushions are provided but feel free to bring anything else to aid your comfort.





A plant-based dinner & dessert follows the event - all included in your ticket!



Meet Alexandra, your host:

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.


Meet Smita, your host:

From a young age, Smita was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.





Agenda


🕑: 05:45 PM - 06:00 PM
Arrive to Bhakti Lounge

🕑: 06:00 PM - 07:00 PM
Inner Worlds: Sound Bath
Host: Alexandra

🕑: 07:00 PM - 08:15 PM
Plant-based dinner and dessert!

events.long_description:
Whiria te Tangata: Weaving People Together
Pause, breathe and create in a Māori weaving workshop exploring raranga, connection and the beauty of making by hand.

About this Event


Whiria te Tangata: Weaving People Together





Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




Join us for a putiputi weaving workshop with local weaver Haley Te Rire. Share a moment to pause, breathe and create. Rooted in the traditions of raranga (Māori weaving) and shaped by her whakapapa as uri of Tūwharetoa ki Kawerau, this wānanga invites you to explore the beauty of weaving as both craft and connection.

Whether this is your first time weaving or a return to familiar rhythms, you’ll be welcomed into a calm, communal space. Leave with your own putiputi that carries intention, aroha, and the echo of those who came before us.





Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!


Meet your host Haley: 

Haley is a local weaver and uri of Tūwharetoa ki Kawerau who shares the art of raranga as a way of fostering connection, creativity, and wellbeing. Grounded in her whakapapa and guided by mātauranga Māori, Haley sees weaving as more than a craft, it is a way to slow down, reconnect, and honour the stories and knowledge carried through generations.

The Joy of Improvisation
Improv is theatre without a script and a fun way to build your skills in many areas, including team work, public speaking, storytelling and on-your-feet creative thinking.
This is the perfect place for absolute beginners to get acquainted with the joy and art of improvisation, inspired by the generous creative philosophy of Keith Johnstone. It's also a great place to get back into improv if you've been away from it for a while.

events.long_description:
Presented by: TEG Live
TEG Live is proud to present Secret Screenings with Beau Miles, an intimate live touring show bringing Beau’s unreleased and unfinished film collection — none of it yet on YouTube — to venues across Australia and New Zealand in 2026.
The premise is straightforward: three or four of Beau’s new films, shown somewhere between a first and final draft. The audience won’t know the titles before they see them. The films aren’t finished, but are entirely watchable. And in between screenings, Beau tells the stories behind them - why they exist, why they look the way they do, and why a man who lives on a small farmlet in Victoria keeps putting himself through things that are, by his own admission, sometimes remarkable, often mundane, and occasionally disgusting.
It’s an evening that moves between film and live performance - part director’s commentary, part stand-up tangent, part confessional. The stories may or may not connect to the films. The Q&A that closes the evening has been independently verified as world-class by one audience member. That audience member was Beau. He’s confident.
Beau Miles has built a devoted following through a body of work that resists easy categorisation - adventure films that aren’t really about adventure, mundane experiments that turn out to mean something, and a stubborn commitment to doing things slowly and in person. Secret Screenings brings that sensibility into the room: unmediated, unfinished, and told by the person who made it.

events.long_description:
Elegance - Wellington
Dynamic British Isata Kanneh-Mason make her NZSO debut in a concert featuring Mozart, Brahms and Andrée.

Programme:
Andrée Andante Recitative
WA Mozart Piano Concerto No. 27
Brahms Serenade No. 1

Isata Kanneh-Mason, the eldest sibling in a dynasty of extraordinary musicians, is being lauded as a pianist who is “the real deal” (classical-scene.com). What a treat to hear her bring such intelligent elegance to Mozart’s last piano concerto. Praised by BBC Music Magazine as capable of making “lines sing beautifully and virtuosic passages dance, finding intimacy and eloquence at telling moments”, Kanneh-Mason is the perfect performer to bring this mature, serenely lovely concerto to Aotearoa New Zealand audiences.

To round out this programme, the NZSO performs two works that deserve a wider audience. Brahms’ Serenade harks back to Mozart’s own delightful serenades, while Elfrida Andrée’s Andante Recitative, written in 1878, was only rediscovered in the 1980s, and “open[s] in broody darkness, but quickly blossom[s] into optimistic, songful melody” (Michael Clive).

Secret Screenings with Beau Miles (Wellington)
Beau Miles is taking his Secret Screenings on the road - bringing a collection of new, unreleased films to intimate venues across Australia and New Zealand in 2026. None of them are on YouTube yet. You’ll see them first.

The idea is simple: three or four of Beau’s films, shown somewhere between a first and final draft. None of them fully finished, but are entirely watchable. None of them named in advance. You won’t know what you’re watching until it starts - and each one has a story to tell beyond what’s on screen.

In between films, Beau tells a bunch of stories about why the films are the way they are. Why he loves finding things. Why he needs to shower more. Why a man living on a small farmlet in regional Victoria keeps dragging himself into rivers and eating spotty bananas and filming it all. The stories may or may not have anything to do with the films being shown. That’s part of the deal.

The evening finishes with a Q&A - voted the best thing ever witnessed by one audience member. That audience member was Beau. He stands by it.

Presale commences: 11am, Thu 11 June
General sale commences: 11am, Fri 12 June

events.id: Financial Planning for Retirement-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Financial Planning for Retirement
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Financial Planning for Retirement
Massey University's annual Retirement Expenditure Guidelines study (2019) found:
Just 40% of pre-retirees believed they were well-prepared for retirement, and 57% considered retirement to be a concern.  They also confirmed, New Zealand Superannuation is not sufficient to fund the retirement most people want.
Ministry of Social Development (2020):
22% of all people receiving New Zealand Superannuation also receive additional support payments, with over 44,000 superannuants receiving additional accommodation support,
And if you needed to obtain Government assisted accommodation, at the end of March 2020, more than 16,300 households were waiting for state or social housing.
Living in a motel or boarding house with strangers (who may have other vulnerable backgrounds) is not an ideal or safe location to spend your retirement years.   But for many, it is the only option they can afford.
If you have not planned for your retirement, then this course is you! 
This course has been developed for people in their 50’s or 60’s that are looking at retirement and have no idea if they can financially survive it: what to do, what $’s they need, how or where they can generate additional income, or even where to go to get help. 
It is targeted towards those that still have some time (for some - not much) to make adjustments, learn some basic financial skills, make some big decisions, and positively influence the quality of their pending retirement. 
You will be introduced to a simple step by step guide to developing a financial plan for retirement. 
You will work though a case study in class, and can then go away and repeat the process with your own data/details.  You will be provided with comprehensive course notes to enable you to update the case study information with your own information. 
At each step, key considerations and financial concepts will be defined, explained and discussed to help you understand the financial requirements of retirement.  
Are you ready for the retirement lifestyle you hoped or dreamed of?  If not, then this course is for you.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Disclaimer:  The tutors are not financial advisors.  No investments, products nor specific recommendations will be provided.  A step by step planning process will be taught by working through a case study.  Key considerations that should be used by the participants when looking at their own options to bridge the financial gap between what is available through superannuation and what is required to meet lifestyle goals will be provided and discussed.  Product names may be used in examples and explanations to help participants understand the financial concepts and the planning process.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Genealogy - Basics of ancestry.com DNA tests
Got your test results back and still wondering what a centiMorgan or a shared match is?  Find out what the size of your match means and the tools available to help you work out possible family relationships.
We'll start by looking at Clustering and how the Grouping tool on Ancestry.com can help with this.  We'll also look at the ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools to see how they can provide suggestions for knocking down brick walls in your research.
Also covered during this course are other websites you can upload your results to, how to manage other family member's DNA test results and other tools available when you get a bit more advanced - and just in case you need help in the future, we'll look at some of the places you could get this from.
Please note:  this course will only cover DNA tests taken through Ancestry.com  All computer courses are run in the school computer labs and you are required to use the school desktops for the duration of the course (you are not able to use your own laptop).  Some of the courses may require you to login onto the network. 
Bring a USB stick and your Ancestry.com login details.
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Understand the information provided by Ancestry.com about your DNA matches
-  Use the Grouping, ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools on Ancestry.com
-  Use the Shared CentiMorgan tool on DNAPainter.com
-  Understand where to find other tools
-  Understand the options for using other DNA websites
-  Understand where to get further help

events.long_description:
Getting the Most from AI: Practical Skills for Everyday Use
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $29 with ID, all others pays $120).
AI tools are everywhere, but knowing which one to use — and how to use it well — makes all the difference. In this hands-on workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through practical techniques to make AI a genuinely useful partner in your work and life. Whether you've tried it a few times or use it regularly, you'll leave with real skills you can apply straight away, with no technical background needed.
We'll start with a quick tour of the main tools — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot — so you understand what makes each one different. (They're less different than you might think!) Then we'll spend most of the day going deep on Claude, which Jon considers the easiest to use, while also being the most powerful.
We'll cover real examples, answer your questions as they come up, and spend plenty of time experimenting together.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
- Write effective prompts that get clearer, more useful responses
- Use AI for research, brainstorming, writing, and creative work
- Understand the differences between the major tools and when to use each
- Recognise the tools' limitations (and how to work around them)
- Apply practical strategies for using AI in your personal or professional projects
- Confidently troubleshoot when AI gives unexpected or unhelpful answers
Please bring: A phone or laptop with ChatGPT and Claude installed and signed in to both. Enough battery to last the day.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Sculpture - Intro to Creature Sculpting
Join us for a fun day of creature making! Design and sculpt a one-of-a-kind character in your own style from polymer clays in a full spectrum of colours!

Working with oven-cured clays and wrapped wire armatures, this workshop offers a variety of modelling methods and approaches - a great opportunity to turn sketches & ideas into tangible 3D forms. Modern clay inventions mean we can create translucent, glittery, semi-flexible, UV reactive or even glow-in-the-dark elements to add more realism or a touch of the surreal into each creation!

Students will be coached through designing and creating a small-scale creature sculpture, beginning simple, and building to a more complex final form as we get familiar with materials.

The class offers beginner students a fun introduction to sculpting organic forms from scratch, and for those with some hands-on creative experience, it offers a great opportunity to experiment, hone and advance your making skills to new levels.

If you can, bring along some design ideas, sketches or reference images to help kick start the sculpting process on the day.

Please wear closed-in footwear suitable for a workshop environment. bring a work apron if you have one or wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little grubby. Remember to bring your reading glasses if you have them.

events.name: Sourdough Bread Baking Workshop
events.venue: Mangaroa Farm, 98 Whitemans Valley Road, Te Awa Kairangi, Upper Hutt
events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for an afternoon in the kitchen with Doris Zuur, who has been baking the slow way for decades. Rye sourdoughs raised on a living starter, wholemeal loaves that rise through an afternoon, Swiss Zopf plaited by hand, focaccia, and a fermented buckwheat loaf for those who can't eat wheat. Her bread is the kind that fills a house with its smell and a table with quiet conversation.

Spend an afternoon with her in our kitchen. You'll mix, knead, plait and bake alongside her. You'll learn how to keep a starter alive, how to read a dough by touch, and the small decisions (temperature, time, gusto) that turn flour and water into a good loaf.

You'll leave with:
- A jar of living starter to take home
- A warm loaf from the oven
- Doris's full recipe collection (rye sourdough, wholemeal, Swiss Zopf, fermented buckwheat, focaccia, Oaties)
- Her "0800 bread helpline" for when you need a hand at home

Afternoon tea included. Bring a clean glass jar with a lid, an apron, and a willingness to slow down.

We will begin at Sat 17th October | 10:00am at 298 Whitemans Valley Road (Wharekai/Yurt).

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
Hospital Records’ 30th anniversary celebrations
Hospital Records to Celebrate 30th Anniversary with Hospitality 2026

Hospital Records is one of the most influential labels in dance music and a cornerstone of the drum & bass movement right from its foundational year, is entering its 30th year. To kick off the celebrations, the label has announced its return to NZ on Saturday, 17 October 2026 celebrating three decades of Hospital Records.

For this special anniversary edition, Hospital Records will spotlight a vibrant spectrum of drum & bass talent from across the scene, celebrating the label’s ever-evolving identity across three decades featuring standout performances from DJ DANNY BYRD + Unglued + Hoax set to ignite the stage.

Part of Hospital Records’ global 30th anniversary celebrations. Since its founding in 1996 by Tony Colman and Chris Goss, Hospital Records has grown into the world’s largest independent drum & bass label, recognised for its consistency, creative vision and the strong sense of community at the core of its music and events. Through its flagship brand Hospitality, the label has built a worldwide reputation for high-quality DnB experiences across the world.

Acclaimed Ruawaipu and Ngati Porou dummer-composer Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa is the 2026 Wellington Jazz Festival commissioned artist. A defining force in Te Whanganui-a-Tara's music community for two decades, he has brought his distinctive voice to stages and studeios across Aotearoa and beyond.

Wellington, get ready to party with BJÖRN AGAIN!

The only ABBA-endorsed tribute show hits the stage for one spectacular night that is bound to be a Super Trouper celebration of ABBA’s timeless discography.

This internationally acclaimed show brings the glitter, the glam, and all the greatest hits with dazzling energy, spot-on vocals, and outrageous costumes. It’s a full-blown ABBA revival where audiences of all ages can sing, dance, and party like it’s 1979.

Praised by rock royalty and media worldwide —Metalica, Nirvana, Sir Tom Jones, and ABBA themselves – the show has earned glowing reviews:

Tell your mum, tell your grumpy teenager, tell Fernando – tickets won’t last!

Fly Fishing
An introduction to fly fishing for trout, which includes choosing gear, finding the fish, fly tying and casting and a practical fishing session.
By the end of the course, you'll be able to: 
• Apply the basics of fly fishing
• Choose the appropriate tackle
• Have an appreciation of the entomology associated with trout
• Demonstrate practical aspects of casting, knot tying, tying of flies and stream craft
• Present an appropriate fly to the water with a reasonable chance of catching a trout
There are three sessions at the high school, plus a session at the Capital Trout Centre and a choice of two river sessions (times and dates to be discussed at the class). events.venue: 3 Market Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011
events.long_description:
Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day
Learn to create beautiful enamelled jewellery with Lisa Sinclair.

Join us for a full-day enamelling workshop where you’ll explore colour, texture, and fire to create vibrant enamelled jewellery in copper or silver.

This hands-on class focuses on the fundamentals of enamelling, showing you how to apply, fire, and layer enamel to achieve rich, expressive surfaces. You’ll make a simple yet beautifully textured pendant or pair of earrings, then learn how to add a pop (or flood!) of colour to bring your piece to life.

Beginners to metalwork are very welcome - pre-formed shapes are available so you can focus on experimenting with colour, pattern, and mark-making. If you have some metalworking experience, you’re encouraged to take things further by creating and texturing your own metal forms before enamelling.

This is a playful, creative workshop and an ideal class for anyone who loves working with colour, surface, and experimentation - whether you’re new to enamels or keen to deepen your skills.

What you’ll learn:
The basics of enamelling on copper and silver
How to prepare metal for enamelling
Applying enamel using different techniques
Firing enamel and building up layers of colour
Creating texture and pattern in metal
Tips for achieving clean, vibrant enamel finishes

The class fee covers enamel materials but NOT metals. Students can choose from a range of pre-cut copper blanks or use their own copper sheet. Findings and chains are available to purchase at a range of good prices to suit all budgets.

Kids aged approximately 12+ are welcome. Any participant under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

For health and safety reasons, students must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.

Workshop fee $248, early bird $225 till 28 Sept.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This course is designed for parents and caregivers of neurodivergent tamariki who want practical, evidence-informed strategies to better support their child’s wellbeing, behaviour, and participation at home and school.
Across three sessions, we will explore the foundations of neurodiversity, including different neurotypes, strengths-based perspectives, and neuroaffirming language. You will gain insight into sensory processing, regulation, and the critical role of connection and co-regulation in supporting your child.
The course also provides guidance on navigating Aotearoa New Zealand’s health, education, and disability systems, including how to access supports and advocate effectively for your child. We will explore common challenges such as school refusal, burnout, and meltdowns, with practical strategies for prevention, in-the-moment support, and recovery.
There will be opportunities for discussion, reflection, and shared learning, as well as a Q&A-style panel session incorporating both professional and lived experience perspectives.
This is a group-based learning environment (not individual therapy), with an emphasis on practical tools, connection, and empowerment.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.
It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.
Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”

events.long_description:
Shea McAleese: The Evolution of a Four-Time Olympian
What does it take to perform on the world's biggest stage?

And perhaps more importantly, what happens when the cheering stops, the jersey comes off, and it's time to reinvent yourself all over again?

Join four-time Olympian and New Zealand hockey legend Shea McAleese for an inspiring Learning Lunch exploring the highs, challenges and lessons of a life spent pursuing excellence.

From a young Hawke's Bay athlete with a dream to representing New Zealand at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games, Shea's journey offers a fascinating insight into commitment, resilience and what it really takes to perform at an elite level.

But this isn't simply a story about sport.

It's about leadership, teamwork, personal growth and learning how to evolve through different chapters of life.

Today, Shea works as an international coach and leadership mentor, helping individuals and teams perform at their best. Drawing on lessons from elite sport, he shares a practical and human perspective on building trust, developing culture and creating environments where people thrive.

Expect honest stories, valuable insights and a fascinating look behind the scenes of life as an Olympian, coach and leader.

Meet Shea 🎤

Shea McAleese is one of New Zealand's most celebrated hockey players and a proud son of Hawke's Bay. Over a 16-year international career he represented the Black Sticks 320 times, competing at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games. Since retiring from international hockey, he has transitioned into international coaching and leadership development, working with elite teams and building a global following through his coaching platform, Inside Hockey.

What We'll Explore
• The realities of competing at four Olympic Games
• Lessons from elite sport that apply to everyday life
• Leadership, trust and building high-performing teams
• The transition from athlete to coach
• Resilience, growth and adapting through life's different chapters

events.long_description:
DUE TO OVERWHELMING DEMAND, MUDHONEY HAS UPGRADED VENUES TO MEOW NUI.
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.
Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.
More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.
"When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound." – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)
A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

events.venue: Meow,17 Edward St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mudhoney │Wellington
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.

Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.

More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.

A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.
