events.venue: Hutt Bowling Club,6 Myrtle Street, Lower Hutt, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Power Up Central Hutt
Come to the first of the new 2026 Power Up The Hutt information sessions in the Hutt Bowling Club, Myrtle Street on the evening of Thursday 29th October at 7:30pm.

Power Up the Hutt is a free five-part community event series bringing together Hutt Valley residents who want to cut their power bills, reduce their carbon footprint, and future-proof their homes.

New Zealand has reached an electrification tipping point — households can now save money and significantly reduce their emissions by switching their appliances and vehicles to electric. But knowing where to start can feel overwhelming.

These friendly, practical evenings — hosted by local volunteers with experience in electrification and drawing on the research of Rewiring Aotearoa — will walk you through the real options available right now: solar panels and home batteries, electric vehicles, heat pump hot water systems, induction cooking, and making the switch from gas to electricity.

Businesses, schools, or community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome. No jargon. No sales pitch. Just straight talk from your neighbours about what works, what it costs, and how to get started.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Posture Perfection is Possible!
Are you a computer slouch, feeling stiff and tense at work? Do you find it difficult to maintain a good posture?  Does your posture cause back, neck or shoulder tension?  Would you like to enjoy more freedom in everyday activities?
Under the guidance of an experienced teacher, we'll explore movement in ways that help you reduce tense unhelpful habits.  Movement lessons are done on the floor or sitting on a chair and are based on the pioneering work of Israeli physicist and engineer Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais.
This workshop is suitable for all ages (over 16) and fitness levels.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
• Identify and reduce muscle tension
• Move with more lightness and freedom
• Improve your posture
• Describe some basic anatomy
• Have tools to use at home and at work
Bring two blankets (or a mat and a blanket) and wear loose, warm and comfortable clothing. Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch. Please note that instructions are given verbally rather than by demonstration, so good hearing and understanding of English is required.
Feel free to contact the tutor, Sue Field on 027 466 7123, if you have any questions. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Sound Healing Experience at Lotus Yoga Centre
We invite you to a special evening of Sacred Harmonic Sound with multi-instrumentalist Claudio Escutia. This immersive sound journey offers a deeply restorative experience that invites you to settle into stillness, reconnect with the heart, and explore a sense of inner spaciousness through vibration

About the event
Claudio skilfully layers the sounds of gongs, crystal and Tibetan singing bowls, Native American flutes, and other traditional instruments, enhanced through high-quality audio equipment so the sound can be both heard and felt throughout your body.Harmonic sound and vibration offer the nervous system a chance to truly rest. In this state of relaxation, the thinking mind softens, and we find connection to citta — the heart-mind. From this place, silence arises naturally through the vehicle of sound.This experience is open to everyone. No previous yoga or meditation practice is needed.


What to bring:Bring your own yoga mat or camping mattress, small pillows, eye pillows and blanket to assure comfort.

Booking is essential — spaces are limited and this event often fills quickly.

About ClaudioClaudio is a multi-instrumentalist musician originally from Mexico City and now based in Wellington. Born into a family of musicians, he began playing music at a young age and later studied classical guitar. His journey led him to Montreal, where he explored jazz, world music, and spiritual sound traditions.

Extensive travels in Asia and Europe deepened his connection with Indian music and yogic philosophy. He studied Tibetan singing bowls in Kathmandu and Varanasi, and has since worked with a wide range of instruments including the sitar, esraj, bansuri, harmonium, flutes, gongs, and voice.

Claudio’s work blends technical skill, deep presence, and a profound respect for the healing power of sound.

Contribution:

Early bird: First 10 bookings $40
General admission : $45

Learn more buy tickets and listen to Claudio’s music here:

Website and Event link:
https://www.claudioescutia.com/events/sound-healing-experience-at-lotus-yoga-centre-2

SoundCloud https://soundcloud.com/claudioescutiasounds

Instagram
https://www.instagram.com/claudio_yoga_sound_healing

Facebook

events.long_description:
Presented by: SBM Presents
Killswitch Engage return to New Zealand in 2026, bringing more than two decades of genre-defining metal to the stage with their biggest Antipodean headline shows yet, joined by special guests Sylosis. The Western Massachusetts heavyweights helped redraw the map for modern metal in the early 2000s, fusing blistering European-inspired guitar work, East Coast hardcore energy and emotionally charged, uplifting lyrics into a sound that changed the game for a generation of bands and fans.
Across a landmark career, Killswitch Engage have earned three Grammy nominations for Best Metal Performance, multiple gold and platinum records, billions of streams and a reputation as one of the most powerful live acts in heavy music. From classic albums like Alive Or Just Breathing, The End of Heartache and As Daylight Dies through to chart-topping releases Disarm the Descent, Incarnate and 2019’s Atonement, they’ve consistently raised the bar while packing out venues and festival main stages around the world.
Fresh from celebrating 25 years as a band and the release of their latest album This Consequence – featuring the blockbuster single “I Believe,” the biggest radio hit of their career – Killswitch Engage are set to deliver a career-spanning set for their New Zealand fans.
Expect a night that runs from era-defining anthems to new favourites, all delivered with the intensity and heart that has seen them share stages with everyone from Iron Maiden and Slayer to My Chemical Romance, Mastodon, Slipknot and Parkway Drive.

events.long_description:
The Mad Hatter's Market Express
🚂🎩 Mad Hatter's Market Express | Sunday 1 November 2026 🎩🚂

All aboard for a day that's delightfully mad!

Leave the car behind and journey through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge aboard one of Steam Incorporated's heritage trains as we head for the famous Woodville Mad Hatter's Market Day.

Relax in beautifully restored heritage carriages, soak up the sights, sounds and smells of classic rail travel, and enjoy a unique day out with family and friends before arriving in the heart of one of the region's most colourful community events.

🎩 At Woodville you'll discover:
🌼 Over 70 market stalls packed with local crafts, food and treats
🎶 Live entertainment throughout the day
☕ Delicious cafés and local hospitality
♠️ Children's activities, old-fashioned games and a touch of steampunk magic
👒 The legendary Crazy Hat Competition – don't be shy... the crazier the better!

Whether you're travelling for the markets, the beautiful train, or simply a relaxing day away, this is one of the most enjoyable heritage rail experiences on our calendar.

🚂 Your journey includes:
✨ Heritage train travel through the breathtaking Manawatū Gorge
👀 Open-air viewing carriage for unbeatable photo opportunities
📍 Boarding available from Paekākāriki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Ōtaki, Levin and Palmerston North
🚌 Shuttle buses available from Woodville Station into the town centre

🎟️ Dust off your maddest hat, gather your friends and family, and make the journey part of the adventure.

Seats are expected to disappear quickly – book early and join us for a wonderfully mad day out! 🎩🚂

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Cheesemaking - Brie and Queso Fresco
The ultimate class in practical cheese making!   Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home.  You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.  
All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.
During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make.  You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.
A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Make Brie and Queso Fresco
- Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
- Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: French Pastry for Beginners
events.venue: Le Ciel Bakery, 100 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
French Pastry for Beginners
A 4-Week Hands-On Series

Step into the world of French pâtisserie with our beginner-friendly four-week course designed to teach you the essential techniques behind some of France's most iconic pastries. Guided by Le Ciel's experienced pastry chef and owner, Shuchi, you'll build your confidence week by week as you learn the foundations of classic French baking.

This progression-based course is perfect for anyone who loves baking, wants to develop professional techniques, or is looking to begin their pastry journey. Each class focuses on a new skill while building on what you've learned in previous weeks, making it easy to continue growing as a baker.

Week 1 – French Macarons

Take on one of France's most famous pastries with confidence. Learn how to create smooth macaron shells, perfect feet, balanced fillings, and troubleshoot common problems so you can recreate them successfully at home.

Week 2 – Choux Pastry

Master the fundamentals of pâte à choux as you learn to mix, pipe, bake, fill, and finish classic French favourites including profiteroles and éclairs. You'll also learn how to make silky pastry cream and achieve perfectly crisp shells.

Week 3 – French Tarts

Discover the secrets to beautiful French tarts by learning sweet pastry dough, blind baking, creamy fillings, fruit finishing, and professional presentation techniques.

Week 4 – Mille-Feuille

Complete the course by creating the elegant Mille-Feuille. Learn how to work with puff pastry, prepare rich vanilla crème pâtissière, assemble delicate layers, and finish with a professional glaze.

What's Included
Four hands-on classes
Step-by-step instructions from professional pastry chefs
All ingredients and equipment are provided
Recipe booklet to take home
Your creations to enjoy and share
Small class sizes for personalised guidance

Who is this course for?

This course is ideal for complete beginners and enthusiastic home bakers. No previous baking experience is required—just bring your enthusiasm and a love of French pastries.

By the end of the four weeks, you'll have mastered a range of foundational pastry techniques and be ready to continue into our future intermediate pastry workshops.

Spaces are limited to ensure every participant receives plenty of individual guidance. Early booking is recommended.

We will be running 2 starts for this course:
Dates for course:
First course: September 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th
Second course: November 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th

events.long_description:
The Cake Club Picnic 3.0✨️
Love cake? So do we! Join us at The Cake Club Picnic – a one-of-a-kind gathering dedicated exclusively to cake. You don't want to miss it!

About this Event

Welcome to The Cake Club Picnic! 🍰
By popular demand and our first cake picnic was a success, we are happy to host another epic Cake Picnic!
Join us for a deliciously fun day out at Bellevue Gardens Hotel on Sunday, November the 8th, 2026.
Whether your a professional baker, a passionate home baker, or simply someone with a sweet tooth, The Cake Club Picnic is the perfect event to indulge your love of all things cake!
Entry requires both a ticket and a cake - one per person.
Everyone attending must bring a cake of their own. No cake, no entry - no exceptions. This rule keeps things fair and fun for everyone involved.
Even if you're bringing a guest under tickets you have purchased, they must bring a cake too. Sharing one cake between two people won’t cut it. We appreciate your understanding and commitment to the cake-loving community!
🎂 What to Expect:
A relaxed indoor and outdoor garden setting - enjoy the space rain or shine!
A shared cake table filled with baked goodies brought by everyone attending - taste, share, and show off your creations!
Chill vibes and great company - meet fellow cake lovers, swap stories, and make sweet memories.
Picnic-style seating - bring a blanket, find a sunny spot, or grab a seat indoors.
A self-service tea and coffee station to keep your cup full as you sample cakes.
Cake Size Requirement:
Please bring a cake that can generously serve at least 12 people. Think full-sized bakes -enough to share and make sure everyone gets a proper slice (or two)! 🎂✨ - REMEMBER - CAKE ONLY!
Cake Set-Up:
You’re welcome to do final touch-ups at the venue, but please avoid full setups or major decorating on-site. Display tables will be shared with other guests, so we want to keep things smooth and stress-free for everyone.
Serving Tools, cake detailed label & Cake Stands:
Please remember to bring your own serving tool so guests can easily cut and enjoy your cake.
We will provide you with a cake label card and card insert stick for everything to look uniformed!
Want to show off your creation? Feel free to bring a cake stand to elevate your cake-literally and visually! 🍰🔪✨
Boxes & Utensils:
We've got you covered! The host will provide boxes for you to pack up cake slices during the event, along with forks, spoons, napkins, and water to keep things easy and enjoyable. 🍴📦💧
Rubbish:
Let’s keep the vibes sweet and the space clean! Please use the bins provided on-site and help us leave the venue just as lovely as we found it. We also kindly ask that you take any leftover rubbish or personal items with you when you head out. ♻️🧼💛


Disclaimer & Event Guidelines
This is a community-friendly event, and all participants are expected to behave in a respectful and responsible manner toward others. By attending, you agree to be patient, follow the event rules, and respect everyone's space, time, and contributions.
If you are bringing a homemade cake, you confirm that it has been prepared in a clean and safe environment to the best of your ability. Please note that food is consumed at your own risk, and the event organisers and venue accept no responsibility for allergic reactions or food-related illnesses.
Cakes that contain common allergens (e.g. nuts, dairy, eggs, gluten) must be clearly labelled to help others make informed choices.
This event will be photographed and filmed for use in future marketing, content, and social media promotion. By attending, you grant permission for your image and likeness to be used across both online and offline platforms by the event organisers.
You attend this event at your own risk. The organisers, volunteers, and venue are not liable for any injury, loss, damage, theft, or illness that may occur. Please keep an eye on your personal belongings - you are responsible for them.
Thank you for helping us keep this a fun, safe, and inclusive experience for all! 🍰💛
Bring your appetite, your friends, and your best bake. Everyone is welcome - just come ready to relax, connect, and enjoy a truly sweet day out!


Agenda


🕑: 11:00 AM - 03:00 PM
How the Cake Club Picnic Work
Info: You’re welcome to arrive from 11AM to set up your cake and take some time to admire everyone else’s beautiful creations before the event officially begins. Cake Cutting & Group Rotation-

To keep things fun and relaxed, all participants will be grouped by coloured wristbands, which you’ll receive at the registration table.

When it’s your group’s turn, you’ll have 5 minutes to browse and slice a piece from any cakes you’d like to try. This helps make sure everyone gets a fair and enjoyable experience sampling all the amazing creations.

Once all groups have had their turn, feel free to go back and enjoy any leftover cake! ?


Important: Please don’t take or use other people’s serving utensils or display stands - these belong to the cake owners and need to be returned to them. Thank you for being respectful and keeping the cake vibes sweet!

events.name: National Dog Database
events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
National Dog Database
Using the NDD to its full potential. Get hands-on and use realistic scenarios to explore and learn the functionality of the NDD website.

About this Event


Description

The National Dog Database went live 1 May 2006 and provides a countrywide overview of dog control in New Zealand.

It brings great benefits to the animal control industry including the ability to;

track classified owners and dogs
monitor the national infringement count of owners
look up out of district dog and owner details
locate dogs when only limited information is available;
and contribute accurate data to ongoing policy analysis.







Outline

Using the NDD training environment (it looks just like the live NDD system but contains fictional data), the NDD training workshop will explore the following areas:

Background – the history of the NDD project – from 2003 to present
TA Extracts – how information gets from your local system to the NDD and the feedback the NDD will give you as well as the different types of files you can send
Searching – how to get the best out of the search screen and how to interpret the results of your search
The ToDo List – what are errors, warnings, information and system notifications? Detailed discussion about what you need to do with them.
Automated and Manual Linking – National Duplicates – comparing dogs and owners that look similar but are in different districts, and how to manually search for other duplicates.
Security – passwords, adding new users or expiring old accounts, as well as the owner protected status.
Reports – what reports you can run and how to use them in your TA. Did you know there are 18 different kinds of reports that you can generate from the NDD and that you can use some of them to compare your TA’s data to a national summary?







Learning outcomes

With a focus on maintaining data quality, participants in the workshop will learn to use the NDD as a tool for animal control and further understand the importance of administrative roles at the local level. Following the completion of the NDD training workshop, NDD users will have the confidence to use the database to its full potential.







Audience

This course is suitable for managers, team leaders and users with animal control administrator responsibilities.







Prerequisites

To participate in the NDD training workshop you must be a registered user of the National Dog Database (employee or contractor). You are required to bring your own laptop.

events.long_description:
Photography: Unlocking the Secrets to Captivating Images
Elevate your photography from ordinary to extraordinary and ensure your work stands out in the digital age. Creating captivating photographs and understanding what makes a photograph engaging is something every photographer should master. Camera settings are essential, but once you know them, you need to learn how to take photographs that stir emotions, impact your audience, and leave a lasting impression. After all, isn’t that the true purpose of photography? People don’t want to see the same landscapes or flowers they’ve seen thousands of times. But how do you turn what you love into something that makes people go, "Wow"?
Captivation in photography means stopping a viewer in their tracks, making them look, feel, and connect. It’s about delivering a photograph that enthrals, evokes profound emotions, and shifts perspectives.
In a world brimming with images, only a few have the power to truly captivate and linger in our memories.
 This pioneering course is your gateway to mastering the art of creating captivating photographs at a time when AI-generated images are saturating our visual landscape. Create something genuine and memorable—images that spark curiosity, evoke emotions, and inspire changes in perception. It's time to define your unique style, refine your vision, and make your mark.
 Course Outcomes
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to: 
Identify the foundational elements that transform an ordinary image into a captivating one.
Create photographs that make people say "Wow" by applying techniques that add a spark of wonder to your shots.
Infuse your photographs with curiosity, making each frame a source of intrigue and interest.
Understand why some images linger in memory and how to make your photographs unforgettable.
Develop a unique style and vision that sets your work apart in the crowded digital landscape.

events.long_description:
Enigma - Wellington
NZSO Artistic Advisor and Principal Conductor Gemma New with legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough present a concert of charm, mystery and bold vision.

Programme:
Ross Harris Concerto for Orchestra (World Premiere)
Saint-Saëns Piano Concerto No. 5 Egyptian
Elgar Enigma Variations

Edward Elgar’s greatest masterpiece remains swathed in mystery.

His Enigma Variations, a set of 14 variations on a theme you never actually hear, has been the subject of both intense scrutiny and great love, thanks to the compositional genius and throbbing heart pulsing in these compelling variations.

Similarly, Saint-Saëns’ Fifth Piano Concerto has beguiled audiences with its Eastern-inspired sounds — hence its Egyptian nickname. To weave his own spell on us, legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough returns to our shores. Praised by Limelight for possessing “an other-worldly stillness and strength [and] the perfect technique combined with the utmost poetic fluency”, Hough promises to transport us to another world.

We proudly premiere Ross Harris’ Concerto for Orchestra. A four-time winner of the SOUNZ Contemporary Award, Harris’ artistry and bold vision electrifies this newly commissioned work, driving the orchestra to new heights.

events.long_description:
Raurimu Thunder
Mainline Steam Heritage Trust is embarking on our biggest trip of the year. Modern diesel trains cover this route daily without a second thought, but we are doing something entirely different. We are throwing out the modern dampening, bypassing the mundane, and tackling New Zealand's greatest rail challenge the way it was meant to be conquered: with raw, untamed steam power.

Raurimu Thunder puts you trackside and onboard as our heavy heritage steam locomotive charges into the rugged heart of the North Island to take on the legendary Raurimu Spiral. This is a full day, high horsepower assault on a brutal mountain grade. No filters, no computer assists—just pure, unfiltered vintage engineering working at the absolute limit.

Relax in climate controlled comfort or head to the open air viewing platform to hear and see our heritage steam locomotive charge across dramatic landscapes and tackle the country's most legendary railway challenge. Large panoramic windows frame the unfolding wilderness, ensuring you enjoy every moment of the giant climb in absolute comfort, no matter the unpredictable Central Plateau weather.

How Your Day Flows:
The Scenic Approach: Settle into our premium carriages at your local station as the whistle blows and the journey begins. We steam smoothly through rolling rural valleys toward the base of the Central Plateau. Indulge in fresh barista coffee, artisan snacks, or a local craft beer from the fully stocked cafe carriage as the excitement builds.

Conquering the Spiral: Feel the earth shake as our locomotive battles the 1 in 50 grade of the world famous Raurimu Spiral. This 1898 engineering masterpiece overcomes a massive 139 metre vertical rise through a brilliant layout of horseshoe curves, deep tunnels, and a complete 360 degree loop. Experience the tight, coiling geometry firsthand from the outdoor platform, where you can practically see the front of the train loop right over the back.

The Trackside Photo Runby: Step off the train directly onto the rugged track ballast for the ultimate adventure highlight. Clear your camera lenses and find your vantage point along the tracks. Feel the anticipation build as the massive steam locomotive sets back out of sight, then marvel at the raw power as it charges back up the spiral for an unforgettable, full steam display.

The Atmospheric Return: Board your assigned premium carriage at the summit for a cozy, relaxing journey home. Swap stories with fellow travellers and enjoy a premium glass of regional wine from the salon bar as the train rolls comfortably into the night, concluding an epic day of New Zealand rail history.

Silver Star Dinner Service

As the day draws to a close and the train settles into its evening journey home, make the most of the experience with our Silver Star Dinner Service.

For $26.99 per meal, enjoy a freshly prepared dinner from Hungry Rush Ohakune, served during the return journey. It’s the perfect way to relax after a day of steam, scenery and adventure.

Choose your preferred dinner option when you book, with your selection made and paid for conveniently during checkout.

Your Dinner Choices:

The Wingman
Tender smoked chicken wings, marinated in chipotle buttermilk and served with crispy fries and a smoky hickory cola BBQ sauce.

The Burger & Fries
A juicy New Zealand beef burger with American cheese, grilled onions, pickles and house burger sauce, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

Fish & Chips
Fresh East Coast tarakihi in a light, crispy batter, served with golden fries, minted peas, fresh lemon and a house-made dipping sauce.

The No Meat Burger & Fries — Vegetarian

events.long_description:
Cheesemaking - Farmhouse Cheddar Cheese Workshop
During this hands-on workshop, you’ll be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of farmhouse style cheddar.
The fee includes a cheese press (value $95.00) which can be used every time you want to make a hard cheese. It holds up to 6 litres of milk and this is what you’ll be taking your cheese home in to press for 12 hours after the workshop. All ingredients, recipes and a full set of course notes are provided.
You’ll also receive comprehensive instruction on how to wax (if you choose to) and then mature your cheese over the next five weeks. Alexis will also demonstrate how to make halloumi cheese which will then be grilled for you to enjoy! There’ll be a short lunch break and cheese making supplies such as wax will be available to purchase.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
• Describe the basics of sanitisation and hygiene
• Recognise the difference between raw and pasteurised milk and know where to source them
• Make a round of cheddar cheese using a cheese press
• Describe how to wax and mature the cheese
• Describe how to make halloumi, following a demonstration

events.name: The Digital Minefield: AI, Misinformation, and Detox
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Together, workshop participants will demystify how artificial intelligence actually works, acknowledge some of the harms of this new technology, learn about the characteristics of mis/disinformation, build resilience against fake news, and explore why our brains weren’t built for the infinite scroll. You will walk away from the workshop with a better understanding of the hidden forces shaping your screen, equipped with real-world tools to cut through the digital noise.
 
Dr. Andrew Chen is a leading New Zealand specialist at the intersection of digital technology ethics and public policy. With a PhD from the University of Auckland in Computer Systems Engineering, Andrew brings a deep technical understanding and applies it towards systemic issues and interventions. With extensive experience advising public agencies and private companies on governing emerging technologies, Dr. Chen translates complex technical concepts into clear, accessible insights for the community. He is passionate about helping people understand technology's societal impacts, and thinking more deeply about what’s happening behind the scenes, so we can all navigate today’s complex digital landscape.
 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

The 2000’s Day Party is here!

Get Ready to Throw It Back to the 2000s! 🎉

Join us for an unforgettable day filled with the biggest hits of the 2000s, featuring chart-topping tracks from your favorite artists of the decade. Whether you’re a noughties music lover or just here for the nostalgia, this party is all about good vibes and even better tunes! 🎧💃✨

What to Expect:

🎶 Nonstop Noughties Anthems: Sing your heart out to the iconic hits that defined the decade—from pop bangers to rnb classics and everything in between.

🕺 Dance Floor Throwbacks: Show off your best moves and relive the energy of the ultimate noughties party scene.

Let’s make it a day to remember—noughties style! 💿🎤🎉

Expect to hear music from:

Beyoncé ⭐️ Britney Spears ⭐️ Eminem ⭐️ Justin Timberlake ⭐️ Usher ⭐️ Rihanna ⭐️ Coldplay ⭐️ Daft Punk ⭐️ Alicia Keys ⭐️ Linkin Park ⭐️ Avril Lavigne ⭐️ Green Day ⭐️ Christina Aguilera ⭐️ OutKast ⭐️ Jay-Z ⭐️ The Black Eyed Peas ⭐️ Shakira ⭐️ Kelly Clarkson ⭐️ Pink ⭐️ Ne-Yo ⭐️ Fall Out Boy ⭐️ Nickelback ⭐️ Lil Wayne ⭐️ Taylor Swift ⭐️ 50 Cent

FAQ’S

🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?

Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.

🗣️ Do you do group discount? Stag/Hen etc

Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.

🗣️ Will there be more tickets available if the event is sold out?

Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addition to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.

🗣️ Is the venue accessible?

Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.

🗣️ Can I resell my tickets?

Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.

🗣️ Are your events 18+?

All of our events are strictly 18+. A valid photographic ID may be requested on entry.

🗣️ What do I do if I cant find my tickets or confirmation email?

events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: Astral People & Handsome Tours
Neo-soul artist Greentea Peng arrives in Australia and New Zealand this November, delicately infusing hypnotic dub with seductive hip-hop swings and jazzy neo-soul excursions.
The South London born Greentea Peng is an artist whose work is guided by self-inquiry, shaped by the dualities she inhabits: pain and pleasure, engagement and withdrawal, expression and stillness. Her emotional literacy is transformed into a blend of neo-soul, dub and jazz, all draped in psychedelic textures.
After rediscovering her love for music while travelling - where she joined a local band in Mexico - a renewed sense of self-confidence propelled her return to London and the release of her 2018 EP, Sensi. The project marked the beginning of a distinctive sound carved from heavy, weighty narration, dubby grain, hissy textures and sparse arrangements. The six-track release is anchored by negative space that sits tightly side-chained to the kick, creating a breathing, pumping feel, while minimal melodic movements allow tension to build and swell around her earthy, soulful voice.
This early foundation continued to evolve, punctuated by notable moments such as her performance of "Downers" on COLORS, which garnered millions of views, as well as her television debut on Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC, where she performed her breakout track "Hu Man". These milestones paved the way for her 2021 debut album, MAN MADE, which she described as a record designed to resonate "more in your heart space, and less in your headspace".
Her latest offering, TELL DEM IT'S SUNNY, dives deeper into her enduring practice of self-witnessing - a work of affirmation, emotional maturity and radical self-acceptance. From "BALI SKIT PT. 1", a soundscape that rises and falls like the ribcage of a shadowy spirit, to "RAW", where we're once again met with Peng's poignant voice notes, the album showcases an artist continuing to explore her inner world with clarity and conviction.
Now, the psychedelic R&B soulstress returns to Australia and New Zealand this November, bringing her rich catalogue of deeply personal, genre-defying music to audiences once again.

Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognized for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

events.long_description:
It’s a 70s rock musical of biblical proportions, and it’s back. Jesus Christ Superstar is heading to St James Theatre, and Wellington audiences are in for a treat. This production won the 2017 Olivier Award for Best Musical Revival and came fresh off an acclaimed 2023/24 tour of the United Kingdom. 
Jesus Christ Superstar explores the biblical events leading to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire.
The 1970s rock score features lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber. Well-known numbers include I Don’t Know How to Love Him, Gethsemane, and Superstar.

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre,111 Wakefield St, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Beethoven 9 - Wellington
The grand finale of the NZSO’s 2026 mainstage season features the grandest of symphonies: Beethoven’s Ninth.

Programme:
Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead Hoata
Beethoven Symphony No. 9

Its audacious juxtaposition of styles, sounds and forces, including the revolutionary inclusion of a choir, marked the Ninth as a landmark work, not just for Beethoven but for music itself. Its monumental achievement and undeniable emotional power will be brought to stunning life with the help of Orpheus Choir Wellington and City Choir Dunedin.

Our essential need for community and connection is also at the heart of Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead’s Hoata. Named for the Māori phase of the moon where the moon is barely visible, Hoata was written in 1979 during a cold northern hemisphere winter and evokes the icy blizzards and intense isolation that swirled around the composer as she wrote.

events.name: Saint Etienne tickets
events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
One of the UK’s most beloved and enduring pop groups, SAINT ETIENNE, are heading to Australia and New Zealand for the very last time. Following the announcement that their 2025 album International would be their final studio release, the iconic trio will take their celebrated catalogue on a farewell tour across the region this November and December.
Released in September 2025, International was met with rapturous acclaim, returning Saint Etienne to the UK Top 10 and reaffirming their status as one of Britain’s most treasured musical institutions. Now, fans across Australia and New Zealand will have the rare chance to experience the band’s shimmering, genre‑blurring sound live, one final time.
With a career spanning more than three decades, Saint Etienne’s songbook is rich with classics including ‘Only Love Can Break Your Heart’, ‘Spring’, ‘Nothing Can Stop Us’, ‘You’re In A Bad Way’, ‘He’s On the Phone’ and ‘Wood Cabin’ tracks that helped define an era of British pop and continue to resonate with audiences worldwide.
Formed in 1990 by Croydon natives Bob Stanley and Pete Wiggs, Saint Etienne struck gold from the outset with their debut single, a transformative cover of Neil Young’s ‘Only Love Can Break Your Heart’, which quickly became a club anthem. The arrival of vocalist Sarah Cracknell in 1991 completed the definitive lineup, her debut on ‘Nothing Can Stop Us’ and the Mercury Prize‑nominated album Foxbase Alpha cementing the group’s place in UK pop history.
Their follow‑up album So Tough soared into the UK Top 10, leading to a landmark moment in 1994 when Saint Etienne became the first band ever broadcast live from Glastonbury Festival.
Now, after decades of innovation, reinvention and irresistible pop craftsmanship, Saint Etienne prepare to say goodbye to Australian and New Zealand audiences.
A final bow from one of Britain’s most cherished groups which is not to be missed.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Self-Hypnosis - Hypnotise Yourself
Self-hypnosis is a fantastic self-development tool. It can also be used for controlling pain, accelerated healing, letting go of limiting behaviours and a number of other applications. This workshop will provide you with a good insight into the world of hypnosis, demystify it and dispel the myths that surround it.
You’ll learn a structured method of taking yourself into hypnosis (informed by scientific research), some of the classic applications of self-hypnosis and evidence-based skills that will convince you without doubt of your ability to hypnotise yourself.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
• Define and discuss hypnosis
• Practice self-hypnosis
• Create and write hypnosis scripts for personal change
• Use the language of self-hypnosis
• Relax hypnotically to deep levels
Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch, pen and paper.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Beekeeping - Next Step
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Beekeeping - Next Step
This is a practical and hands-on experience so bring your beekeeper’s outfit and your lunch. Please check your course instructions for more information on what you need to bring on the day.  The tutor can lend you a veil if you don't have one, please let the CEC office know a week before the course is due to run so this can be arranged.
The workshop starts in the classroom and is followed by a visit to a local apiary.  (Please note that you will working with live bees during the visit so there is a chance of being stung by one.)
If weather isn't suitable on the day, the morning session will still go ahead but the visit will be postponed to the next available Saturday.   Please note that if you can't make the catch-up visit, it's not possible to join in later courses due to number restrictions (a part-refund will be made). You must have done the Beginners' course first.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
• List the key steps in setting up a hive
• Describe how honey is extracted
• State what causes swarming and some ways of preventing it
• Describe what needs to be done to manage Varoa and American Foul Brood 
• Construct kitset frames for a honey super
• Open up and inspect a hive 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Thai cuisine and cooking has a key secret - the secret is that authentic Thai food balances key flavour elements. events.long_description:
Australian singer-songwriter Courtney Barnett is heading back to New Zealand five years after her last sell-out tour. The ‘Creature of Habit’ tour coincides with the release of her fourth studio album of the same name. The album is emotionally resonant and explores the central question: how to get out of your own way so you can truly feel your life. With singles Stay in Your Lane, and Site Unseen’ setting the tone, the album and concert mark a decisive new chapter in her musical evolution. Along with the latest music, she will delve into her extensive back catalogue. 
In addition to a Grammy nomination, Courtney has won multiple ARIAs (Australian Recording Industry Awards). She is known for a style that incorporates intimate storytelling with indie rock and bursts of raw grunge-like energy. Her blend of moody guitar, witty, anecdotal lyrics and laconic talk-singing has cemented her as “one of the most distinctive voices in indie music” (The Mancunion).

events.id: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Richard Dawkins is a world-renowned evolutionary biologist. When published in 1976, his book, ‘The Selfish Gene’, reframed our understanding of life, behaviour, and human nature. Now, 50 years later, he is coming to Wellington to reflect on the book’s revolutionary legacy. He explores what fifty years of science has confirmed or challenged and explains why its core questions are more urgent today than ever before. 
‘The Selfish Gene’ has remained a cornerstone of modern science. It introduced the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the now-ubiquitous concept of the ‘meme’. The ideas in it ignited global debate and five decades of subsequent research. Richard Dawkins is one of the most consequential scientific communicators of our time, so don’t miss the rare opportunity to hear him speak in person.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Dutch groove-explorers YĪN YĪN are bringing disco, funk, psychedelia and dance to Wellington’s San Fran Friday 27 November and Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Saturday 28 November. 
Made up of Erik Bandt on guitar, Kees Berkers on drums, Jerôme Schere on keyboards and Remy Scheren on bass, YĪN YĪN are the kaleidoscopic instrumental quartet from Maastricht, Netherlands, renowned for their genre-bending records and transportive live experience. 
Emerging out of an experimental jam session in a remote ballet school village in 2017 that resulted in the making of their debut album The Rabbit That Hunts Tigers, the band have since created another three critically acclaimed albums and spent the better part of the last decade chasing rhythm across continents. 
With relentless international touring and performing everywhere from Fuji Rock Festival and Lowlands to North Sea Jazz Festival and Clockenflap they have been collecting sounds, textures and musical flavours like souvenirs, drawing from a multitude of influences such as ‘70s Thai Funk, Japanese City Pop and crate-dug global disco. Each project has evolved alongside the eager exploration to immerse their worldly experience into a sonic universe of their own.
Their latest of which,Yatta!, arrived in January 2026. A defining influence on Yatta! Is the cosmic allure of Italo Disco - the psychedelic futuristic dance music that emerged in Italy during the late 1970s and flourished throughout the 80s. “It has something of a mystique,” the band explains. 
“Because all the producers were using new recording techniques and effects and stuff like that, but there are not many pictures or videos of how they were creating things in the studio.You have to use your own fantasy and create your own story about how that music is created.”
This one sees the band into their most realised selves yet, translating into an unmissable live experience. “We tried to make a mix of songs that are very energetic and danceable and are party starters, but also have songs that take you on trips and are more easy. People can also just chill and relax and listen to the music and enjoy it.” - YĪN YĪN 

Aotearoa, get ready to move. YĪN YĪN are set to take on Aotearoa for the first time for two shows this November.

events.name: An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
After a sold-out tour in early 2026, Sir Tony Robinson brings his talk show back to Wellington. Catch ‘An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson’ at The Opera House. The television presenter, actor, and award-winning writer has an impressive decades-long career. Tony will divulge behind-the-scenes stories from his life on and off screen. He’ll then read from his fiction debut ‘The House of Wolf’, an epic tale of Alfred the Great and the bloody birth of England. He won’t hog the microphone the whole time — you’ll also get the chance to ask him questions. Expect masterful storytelling from Tony and lots of laughs from the audience. 

You might have seen Tony play Baldrick in Rowan Atkinson’s cult 80s sitcom ‘Blackadder’. In the show, his “I have a cunning plan” catchphrase and comedic timing made him a household name. He’s also celebrated for his work in historical broadcasting, which includes presenting 20 seasons of ‘Time Team’. His infectious enthusiasm for history continued, as he wrote his first novel aged 78. The book delves into the (often grim) realities of life for ordinary people caught between Saxon kings and Viking raiders.

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
By the time indie/folk singer songwriter Aldous Harding hits Wellington, she will have travelled across the UK and Europe with her Train on the Island tour. By the time the tour reaches the Michael Fowler Centre, it will be a finely oiled machine.   
Named after her fifth studio album Train on the Island, all ten of the album’s songs will appear in the concert, including One Stop, and Venus In The Zinnia.   
Aldous Harding captivates listeners with what Martin Pepperell describes as an ‘elastic and shape-shifting voice’. This, combined with eccentric performances, has catapulted the Lyttelton-born singer to fame. Her second album ‘Party’ won the Taite Prize in 2018, and The Barrel, from her third studio album ‘Designer’, won the 2019 APRA Silver Scroll award.

events.long_description:
DOORS OPEN 6:00pm
SHOW START 7:00pm

Leaving Dublin, Ireland where he was born and raised until the age of 22, David got drunk on travel and never quite hit sobriety of it. He has lived and worked in twelve countries and visited over eighty. His shows draw on his wide travels, cultural observations, attempts at language study, (occasional) international drinking session(s) and being a mildly confused immigrant. 
David is the winner of the prestigious annual San Francisco Comedy Competition, (previous finalists include Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Dana Carvey) and runner-up in the Moth’s largest US Grandslam storytelling competition. Also a bestselling writer, David recorded his debut special Documented for Dry Bar Comedy in 2019, his follow up Cultural Appreciation in 202, and his award winning show Shelf Help in 2025. He has been featured on TED.com, Sirius XM, Just For Laughs, Netflix is a Joke Festival, RTE’s Late Late Show, The Irish Independent, Inc, NPR, and the Huffington Post among others. A festival favorite, David's videos have also gone viral many times over with over 800 million views and a social following of over 2 million people. More info: davidnihill.com

events.name: DECEITS AOTEAROA TOUR 2026
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

Annual Compliance Forum 2026 Wellington
Keeping Ahead of Change, Managing Risk & Building Confidence

About this Event



9:00 Welcome and Industry Update

Industry update
Key issues to keep on the radar

9:30 Around the Table: What Are You Dealing With?

Share the key compliance issues and challenges you're currently facing
Identify common themes across organisations, buildings and roles
Share solutions, experiences and lessons learned

10:30 Morning Tea

10:45 Compliance Schedules: Keeping Pace with Changing Guidance & Interpretations

Strategies for updating and amending schedules
Responding to changes in legislation, regulations and guidance
Identifying when a Compliance Schedule needs to change
Practical review of real examples

12:00 Lunch

12:45 Building Compliance in Practice: Case Study Workshop

Work through a real building compliance scenario
Identify compliance obligations and risks
Determine what information, documentation and evidence is required

1:45 Using Discretionary Exemptions for Specified Systems and Minor Works

When exemptions can be used
Applying Schedule 1 (2) to alterations, fit-outs and minor works
Specified systems and other compliance considerations
Work through practical examples and common pitfalls

2:45 Afternoon Tea

3:00pm Action Planning

Translate today's learning into practical actions
Identify priorities for your role, clients or portfolio

3:30 Looking Ahead

Key takeaways
What’s coming up
Final discussion

4:00 Close





Your host: Rosemary (Rosie) Killip

If you’ve been around building compliance for a while, you probably already know Rosie.

Rosie has been translating, untangling and occasionally questioning building rules since the 1990s - and founded Building Networks in 2000 to help make sense of it all.

She loves nothing more than taking a complicated compliance issue, pulling it apart and asking the question: “But what does this actually mean in practice?”

Expect a practical day, plenty of discussion, a few challenges to the status quo - and probably a laugh or two along the way.

Kāpiti Food Fair 2026
Make a day of it. Gather your friends and whānau, plan your destination getaway, secure your accommodation and VIP parking early, and get ready to savour the flavours, sounds, and spirit of summer at Kāpiti Food Fair 2026.

Kāpiti Food Fair is where great food, great people, and great summer memories come together. As one of the Wellington region’s most anticipated food festivals, it offers a vibrant celebration of New Zealand’s food culture, bringing together the very best producers, artisans, chefs, entertainers, and food lovers for an unforgettable destination day out.

More than just a food event, Kāpiti Food Fair is a lively summer festival that celebrates the incredible talent and diversity of New Zealand’s food and beverage industry. Visitors can sample and shop their way through an exciting United Nations of flavours, discovering artisan products, boutique beverages, handcrafted treats, international street food, fresh produce, specialty ingredients, and unique home and kitchen products. It is a place to try, buy, eat, drink, relax, and uncover new favourites.

events.long_description:
Tui Brewery Express: The Ultimate Christmas Party!
Climb aboard The Tui Express for the ultimate end of year office Christmas party! This is the perfect workplace celebration that beats the standard corporate dinner, making it an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages. It’s the ultimate way to reward your hardworking team, swap out the boring boardroom, thank your favorite clients, and celebrate the year's wins with a spectacular Sunday on the rails.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to capture an epic, casual end of year team photo than from our open air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for ditching the laptops, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.

The festive celebrations start the second you step on board! Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. Your crew can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non alcoholic refreshments to toast to your Q4 wins, along with hot espresso coffees and plenty of food, sweet treats, and snacks right from the rails as the stunning scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15 minute walk to the world famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for your group. Once at the brewery, relax and toast to your team's successes in the iconic historic grounds. Forget the awkward office Secret Santa and the sad boardroom sausage rolls, your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non alcoholic alternative) to celebrate a successful year together!

Your ticket covers your return journey from your chosen departure station in beautifully appointed premium carriages alongside exclusive rail only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open air viewing platform for unbeatable team bonding, sightseeing, and staff photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling drinks, coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared festive BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

events.long_description:
UK music’s biggest underdogs, indie rock juggernauts The Reytons, keep charging forward on their unstoppable rise. Having flirted with overseas territories successfully over the past 5 years, the band are now heading out on their very first World Tour, and have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand this November and December

Renowned for their raucous live shows, and touted by many as the best live act of their generation, the British 4-piece pride themselves on their honesty and pure energy. Having taken their native UK by storm, with number one albums, sold out park shows and major festival headlines, the lads from Rotherham are taking on the world with their upcoming world tour.

In 2025 alone, they toured the UK, headlined Tramlines Festival and the iconic Wembley Arena. The upcoming world tour is a huge statement for a band who have hurdled every obstacle with nothing other than blue-collar grit and determination. It cements them as a band at the top of British music. The Reytons also recently announced their fourth studio album A Love Letter To A Broken Town - due for release in July.

Rooted in the rough around the edges humour and honesty of everyday life, The Reytons continue to channel their origins into everything they do, and A Love Letter To A Broken Town sees them staying true to those roots while pushing their sound forward with confidence and intent.

“I honestly feel like this album is the best we’ve ever done!” explains frontman Jonny Yerrell. "A lot of bands and artists like to change direction later in their careers, but that’s just not us. We absolutely love the style of music we make, the social commentary aspects and the people who turn up to jump around with us. Why would we change? Expect more, just bigger and better with a few surprises on the side! "

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

Few groups have had a greater impact on alternative hip hop than The Pharcyde.
Emerging from South Central Los Angeles in the early '90s, they rewrote the rules with their wit, originality and unmistakable chemistry, delivering two of the most influential albums of the era.
From the platinum-selling Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde to the genre-defining Labcabincalifornia, classics like "Passin' Me By," "Runnin'," "Drop," "Otha Fish" and "Ya Mama" continue to inspire generations of artists and remain essential listening more than 30 years later.
The Pharcyde's legacy extends far beyond their own catalogue. They helped open the door for a more playful, soulful and inventive style of hip hop, collaborated with a then- emerging J Dilla, worked with visionary director Spike Jonze, and proved that creativity could be just as powerful as bravado. Their influence can still be heard across modern hip hop, while their timeless live show continues to win over audiences around the world.
Featuring Imani, Slimkid3, Fatlip and DJ Cee Brown, this is your chance to experience one of hip hop's defining groups live.
Secure your tickets early and don't miss the opportunity to see true pioneers of alternative hip hop when they return this December.

Stopping off in Wellington, Auckland, Christchurch and Queenstown, the band will perform tracks from 'Asleep In The Machine', plus their most recent and fourth self-titled studio album, and all the classics from their extended discography.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
UK psychedelic heavyweights Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats return to Australia and New Zealand this December, bringing their dark, hypnotic live show to stages across the country.
The brainchild of Kevin Starrs, Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats have spent over a decade carving out a singular space within the global heavy music landscape. Since emerging in 2009 from the depths of the British underground, the band have built a reputation for their unmistakable fusion of warped psychedelic pop, downer blues and doom-metal intensity.
Too bold and idiosyncratic to be easily defined, Uncle Acid’s sound is steeped in haunting melodies, layered vocal harmonies and eerie, cinematic arrangements, offset by crushing riffs and a persistent sense of unease. It’s a sonic world that feels both deeply nostalgic and completely otherworldly, cementing Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats as one of the most compelling live acts in contemporary rock.
With their last visit to our shores in 2020, Australian audiences can expect a set that traverses the band’s cult catalogue, delivered with the immersive intensity that has made them a must-see worldwide.

Prepare to be surrounded by the magic and wonder of the Christmas season!
Families will love the magical train ride in one of our specially decorated carriages. You’ll meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.
Set to the sounds of carols passengers are invited to join us to be whisked away on the North Pole Express. Delight in the magic of Christmas as the train departs for a journey to collect Santa who has been magically transported to an undisclosed location along the tracks.
From the distance the North Pole Express arrives then the train Conductors invite you and the other passengers to climb aboard shouting “All aboard!”.


All Aboard
During the first leg of the journey wide-eyed children of all ages are invited to engage with characters who are eager to hear what makes the Christmas season special to them.
You’ll meet the conductor, and join in the fun singing and dancing with your hosts and a few other characters who will appear in your carriage on the journey.
At the 'North Pole' Cocoa Class passengers enjoy their iced chocolate from their souvenir mug, and a delicious cookie served by our North Pole Express hosts. Candy and Claus Class passengers will be served aboard the train on the way to the North Pole.
Along the journey Santa appears in your carriage to present each passenger with their very own Christmas ornament. During the trip, characters in each carriage lead passengers in carolling and entertainment as the train makes its way back home.
Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. North Pole Express always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

events.id: Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky-Star Safari Observatory, 1169 Ponatahi Road, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky
events.venue: Star Safari Observatory, 1169 Ponatahi Road, Carterton
events.long_description:
Spend an evening under one of the world’s finest dark skies and learn how to photograph the Milky Way, constellations and deep-sky objects. This immersive masterclass is designed for curious explorers, hobby photographers and anyone who has ever looked up and wished they could capture what they saw.

Your instructor is an experienced astro-educator, and you’ll be taken step by step through the art and science of night-sky photography with DSLR or mirrorless cameras. You’ll learn how to focus at infinity, choose the best camera settings, build compositions under the Milky Way, and work with RAW files, noise control and exposure strategy. You’ll photograph live star fields and leave with images you can genuinely be proud of.

No astronomy expertise or prior astrophotography experience is required — just your curiosity. Bring a camera and tripod if you have them, but if not, you can still attend, learn from telescope-linked imaging feeds, and gain the skills and confidence to shoot the cosmos on your own.

Held at Star Safari, right in the Wairarapa dark-sky heartlands, this experience takes place under the same southern skies recognised by Lonely Planet as one of the world’s top stargazing destinations. If you’ve ever wanted to try astrophotography, this is the moment, and this is the place.

What you’ll gain:
- Confidence to shoot the night sky
- Proven camera settings and workflow
- Real photos of the Milky Way and southern star fields
- Knowledge you can use anywhere the southern sky is visible
- A rare, premium learning experience under a world-class sky

Perfect for couples, travellers, creatives, astronomy lovers, and anyone who wants a deeper connection to the night.

Spaces are limited to keep the experience personal.

events.long_description:
Tora Bombora - 2027
The Return of Tora Bombora.

Wellington Anniversary Weekend, 22 - 24 January, 2027

After five incredible festivals and a four year hiatus, Tora Bombora is returning for the sixth edition - Tora Bombora Ono

For four summers, the paddocks sat quietly. The stages slept, the winds kept moving across the hills, and the coast returned to its familiar rhythm. But some things never really leave. They simply wait.

————————————————————

Ticket System and Key Dates

'Tora Bombora Whānau'

He’s been referred to as the God of the comic essay. Author David Sedaris is a savant of sardonic wit. Wellington gets to experience his razor-sharp sense of humour when he visits to promote his latest book - ‘The Land and Its People’. David will take to the stage to read from the collection of essays and freshly minted diary entries. This will be followed by a candid audience Q&A session and an extended book signing that — true to form — will run as long as it needs to.   
In ‘The Land and Its People’ he reflects on what it means to be a foreigner, a brother, and a lifelong friend — trying on the role of caretaker after his partner Hugh’s hip-replacement surgery. Equal parts tender and devastating, it’s classic Sedaris: the kind of writing that makes you laugh until you feel guilty, then laugh again anyway. It has been said that listening to him read is an affirming, joyful experience that leaves a person feeling as if their cup has been filled right to the brim.

events.long_description:
Presented by: SBM
Propagandhi will make their long-awaited return to Australia and Aotearoa in early 2027, marking their first shows in the region in nearly eight years.
The ever-evolving standard-bearers of politically charged punk have actively kicked against musical confines and bro-punk conservatism, promoting a message of anti-fascism since 1986. Distilling their DNA of breakneck riffs, hardcore ethos, and radical consciousness, their message remains as vital, and volatile, as ever.
The tour comes in support of the Manitoba, Canada-based outfit’s eighth album, *At Peace*. In true Propagandhi fashion, it’s smart music for dangerous times. “Everything I’m singing about is still coming from being the same person that wrote and sang our first record *How to Clean Everything* in 1993,” Chris Hannah states, recalling the band’s snarky skate-thrash origins.
“But what we’re putting into the songs now, probably reflects more despair than 30 years ago when we had similar perspectives, but with strands of hope and naivete. Now it’s the existential dread of eking out a life worth living in this completely failed society.”
Propagandhi are set to bring their incendiary live show back to Australia and Aotearoa, drawing from a body of work that continues to challenge, confront, and inspire.
New album "At Peace" out now Propagandhi.com

events.venue: Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Following the sell-out success of their European summer tour, System Of A Down is heading to Hnry Stadium for its only New Zealand concert. Wellington audiences will also be entertained by warm up act and alternative rock icons Faith No More. 
This concert marks System of a Down's first Wellington show, and their first time playing in Aotearoa in more than a decade. Blending metal with diverse influences including jazz, opera, and Armenian folk, System Of A Down have sold more than 42 million albums worldwide. They released their debut self-titled album in 1998, but it was not until the release of 'Toxicity' in 2001 that their popularity exploded. Heavy music fans can expect a massive career-spanning set filled with the songs that have defined the genre for more than 25 years.
It's been a long time between Wellington shows for Faith No More. The last time the San Francisco-based band played in the capital was 1997. Responsible for such classics as Epic, Midlife Crisis, and a distinctive cover of The Commodores' Easy, they've developed a die-hard following over the last 40 years. 
Together the bands will bring decades of hard rock (and its fans) to Wellington for what promises to be one of the most electrifying nights of heavy music the city's ever seen.

events.long_description:
Homegrown Wellington band Drax Project are booked for a very special gig — the grand reopening of Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall. After a 13 year hiatus, the building is back online and who better to christen it than a local band with an international reputation? 
Drax Project fuses pop, R&B, hip-hop, and jazz. They formed in 2014 after meeting in Wellington (members studied Jazz Performance at Victoria University and Whitireia Polytech). After capturing local audiences busking on the streets, they launched a professional career. Since then, they’ve released two albums, toured extensively, and opened for global heavyweights Christina Aguilera, Ed Sheeran, and Camila Cabello. 
Joining Drax Project on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved artists. Oscar-winning Bret McKenzie will open the evening alongside his eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders. 
When Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall officially reopens in February, it will be 13 years since the iconic venue closed for refurbishment and strengthening. This landmark concert, full of Wellington talent, is the perfect way to honour the city’s rich cultural and musical legacy.

events.long_description:
Drax Project and Friends | Town Hall, WELLINGTON
DRAX PROJECT TO HEADLINE GRAND REOPENING OF
TE WHARE WHAKARAUIKA WELLINGTON TOWN HALL SATURDAY 20 FEBRUARY 2027

Hometown heroes Drax Project are set to make history as the first act to perform at Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall when the doors officially reopen on Saturday 20 February 2027, marking the first event in the iconic venue since its closure for refurbishment 13 years ago.

The landmark concert will honour Wellington’s rich cultural and musical legacy, with Drax Project returning to the city where they first captivated audiences as buskers on central Wellington’s streets, before launching a career that would see them become one of New Zealand’s most successful acts.
Joining them on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved global names, Bret McKenzie, who will open the evening alongside his
eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders.

Tickets go on sale at midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

The show will also feature a host of surprise special guests throughout the night, including some of Drax Project’s favourite collaborators, inspirations and friends, creating a uniquely Wellington occasion and a celebration of the wider New Zealand
music whānau.

For Drax Project, being invited to reopen the historic 122-year-old building is a true full-circle moment as they explain
“This is going to be a very special gig for us! We all met while at uni here and Wellington is where we got our start. The Town Hall closed before Drax became a thing, but playing there is something we've always dreamt of doing as a band.”

Since emerging from Wellington’s busking scene, Drax Project have built an international career that has seen them amass nearly a billion streams resulting in 34 Platinum certifications globally. Renowned for their live show, they have toured extensively across the world including sharing stages with Ed Sheeran, Christina
Aguilera, Camilla Cabello and George Clinton. Though their music has sustained international success, Wellington remains at the heart of the band's story, making their return to reopen one of the capital’s most treasured venues a fitting homecoming.

Don’t miss your chance to be a part of this historic night. Tickets go on sale midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

events.long_description:
In February 2027, DEL AMITRI return to Australia with Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits a celebratory tour showcasing the songs that defined their remarkable career, from early indie beginnings to international chart success.
Formed in Glasgow in 1982 by Justin Currie, Del Amitri found their long term creative backbone in guitarist Iain Harvie, whose presence has been central to the band’s sound for decades. Their breakthrough came with the 1989 album Waking Hours, featuring the enduring hit ‘Nothing Ever Happens’ and the deliciously catchy ‘Kiss This Thing Goodbye.’ The early ’90s brought further global recognition with ‘Always the Last to Know’ and their biggest US success, ‘Roll to Me,’ which reached Number 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 and remains a worldwide jukebox favourite.
Across seven studio albums, Del Amitri have sold over six million records, earning a reputation for sharp songwriting, wry lyricism and melodic, emotionally resonant rock that continues to connect across generations.
After a hiatus in the 2000s, the band returned for sold out reunion tours and, in 2021, released Fatal Mistakes, their first collection of new music in 18 years, reaffirming their signature sound for both long time fans and new listeners. Del Amitri are currently in the studio recording their new album which is set for a release later this year.
In 2027, the band celebrates their legacy with a powerful, career spanning Australian tour Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits.

Formed in Sheffield in 1980, the band ABC brought a mix of new romantic, post-punk, and disco-funk to dancefloors. Now, 45 years since they began, they're making their way to New Zealand. Expect a set packed with sharp suits, polished pop, and some of the band’s best-known tracks. 
Charismatic singer Martin Fry fronts ABC. He's likely to serenade you with many of the band's favourites including The Look Of Love, Poison Arrow, All Of My Heart, and When Smokey Sings. All of them made it into the top 20 hits in the New Zealand music charts at the time. ABC’s debut album, ‘The Lexicon Of Love’, reached number one in New Zealand for three weeks and stayed in the album chart for 33 weeks. Even after all this time the songs still draw people to the floor to dance.

https://hellovilagvlog.hu/uj-zeland-kiscsoportos-korutazas-kalandtura-a-vilag-vegen/

Készen állsz arra, hogy eljuss a világ egyik legvadabb és legérintetlenebb tájára? Az Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén azoknak szól, akik nem csak látni szeretnének, hanem valóban átélni akarják a természet erejét és változatosságát. Utunkat az Északi-sziget különleges világában kezdjük: Auckland, Hobbiton, Rotorua és Wai-O-Tapu gejzírmezői, gőzölgő hőforrásai és vulkáni tájai már az első napokban megmutatják Új-Zéland nyers arcát. A Lake Taupō partján haladva érkezünk meg a Tongariro Nemzeti Parkba, ahol drámai vulkáni panorámák és alpesi környezet vár ránk — itt nem csak nézelődünk, beleállunk az élménybe. A főváros, Wellington után átkelünk a Cook-szoroson, és megérkezünk a Déli-szigetre. A Picton környéki fjordos partvidéktől az Abel Tasman térség aranyhomokos öblein át vezet az utunk tovább. A vad West Coast mentén elérjük a különleges formájú Pancake Rocks szikláit, majd a lenyűgöző Franz Josef-gleccser világát. A túra csúcspontjai közé tartozik Te Anau és a legendás Milford Sound, ahol hajóra szállva függőleges sziklafalak, vízesések és mély fjordok között haladunk. Ez nem egy klasszikus városnézős túra, hanem egy tartalmas, természetközeli Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás, ahol rövid idő alatt meglepően sok mindent látunk, mégsem rohanunk. Kiscsoportban utazunk, rugalmasan, a legszebb panorámautakon haladva — mert a világ végén nem sietni kell, hanem megélni minden kilométert.
